headline: Is Jensen Huang coming back to Nvidia? Here's what we know
html_content:
Less than a week after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO, reports of a potential comeback have begun to circulate, as a section of employees, shareholders and industry supporters rally behind the former chief executive.

The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Huang was considering a return and had discussed the possibility with his confidants.

According to the report, Huang and his allies are putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his reinstatement.

They are also expected to seek support from the White House.

Separately, current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and other supporters have launched an online petition called 'Stand with Jensen', demanding that Huang be reinstated as CEO while an independent investigation establishes the facts.

The petition has already attracted more than 174,000 signatures, including over 91,000 shareholders, over 8,700 current employees and over 72,000 supporters of Huang.

The signatories say they have not been presented with evidence "substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy".

"Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen's leadership. The inquiry must establish the facts, not merely justify an outcome already imposed," the letter read.

The petition also calls on the board to disclose the scope, independence and expected timeline of the investigation, while giving Huang an opportunity to respond before reaching a final decision.

The campaign has apparently received support from Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, whose names appear among the signatories.

However, their affiliations are self-reported and have not been independently verified.

Experts divided over Huang's chances of returning

Expert opinion remains divided on whether Huang will return, although speculation about a possible comeback appears to be gaining traction.

Prediction market platform Kalshi currently puts the probability of Huang returning at 12%.

Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Management and a financial commentator, has a considerably more optimistic assessment.

He now puts the odds of Huang returning at 51%, saying the movement in his favour is gaining momentum.

Munster also described Huang's resignation as a "facade", arguing that the board had effectively forced his hand.

"But that distinction between 'resigning' and getting fired is key because it gives the Board air cover that they never let him go and therefore could welcome him back," he said.

Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Advisors and a technology analyst who closely follows Nvidia, has a very different assessment.

He sees no possibility of Huang returning as CEO.

"No one individual can replace Jensen as CEO….but at the end of the day after this global scandal the old Jensen with the black leather jacket and rock star persona is gone for good….that cannot be replicated and any talk of a damaged Jensen coming back to Nvidia is ridiculous in our view given the legal/Board/DC scrutiny/moral compass/China tentacles," he posted on X.

"We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO. It’s about moving forward for Nvidia and it starts Tuesday with earnings as Colette leads NVDA ahead (for now)."

Nvidia shares have fallen around 6% over the past five trading sessions, leaving the stock down approximately 14% this year.

Neil Shah of Counterpoint Research, meanwhile, told CNBC that Huang's return would be positive for Nvidia shares.

The amount of capex, the trillion dollar capex which is being spent every year has to continue to make this train going," he said.

However, Shah also raised questions about the governance framework under which Huang might operate if reinstated.

"The only thing I'm concerned about is are there going to be any guardrails around Jensen. Will he be able to orchestrate with the same level of energy and same level of enthusiasm and will the circular deal stop? Will there be more governance? If he cannot work freely and take the ecosystem to the same, breakneck speed, will he be that effective? That is the big question," he said.

Meanwhile, online support for Huang continues.

Meanwhile, Huang's departure has already triggered a political storm in Washington.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to place Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company at the centre of the controversy, on the US trade blacklist despite suspicions that it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

US President Donald Trump has also faced criticism from some Democratic leaders following reports that he had been informed about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang in May this year, as well as a year earlier, but continued to support the Nvidia chief.

Separately, Nvidia's search for a permanent CEO continues even as the company has appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim chief executive.

The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas for the top job at the chipmaker.

Haas, who has led the SoftBank-backed UK chip company since 2022, worked at Nvidia for around seven years more than a decade ago.

He also reportedly maintains strong relationships with Huang and several members of Nvidia's board.

Whether the company ultimately considers a return for Huang or moves ahead with an external successor remains uncertain.

For now, the growing campaign in his favour has added another layer of uncertainty to Nvidia's leadership transition.

headline: FinteqHub Exec: Automated routing boosts approval rates as autonomous payments emerge
html_content:
Artificial intelligence is beginning to transform payment orchestration, replacing manually configured routing rules with systems capable of analyzing transaction performance and adapting to changing conditions.

According to Lev Brodsky, CTO of European payment orchestration platform FinteqHub, the next stage of development will extend beyond selecting payment providers. 

AI-powered systems could increasingly monitor payment infrastructure, identify operational problems, and recommend corrective actions.

The shift comes as major payment companies, including Visa, Google, and Mastercard, develop technologies designed to support transactions initiated by autonomous AI agents.

Brodsky believes these developments could reshape the payment industry in 2027, although several challenges remain.

Machine learning delivers measurable gains in payment routing

Traditional payment orchestration connects multiple payment providers through a unified infrastructure and lets businesses decide how to process transactions.

However, routing decisions typically depend on manually configured rules.

Payments from one country may be directed to a particular provider, while transactions in another currency follow a different route.

The problem, Brodsky explains, is that payment provider performance constantly changes.

A route that delivers strong approval rates one day may become significantly less effective the next.

Manually configured systems can’t always account for every combination of factors affecting transaction success, including the customer's country, currency, card network, issuing bank, and transaction characteristics.

To address this challenge, FinteqHub developed a proprietary machine learning-based payment routing model.

The company completed testing of the model in 2026, with results demonstrating a significant improvement over traditional routing templates.

In an A/B test covering approximately 14,100 payment operations, the model achieved an approval rate of 48.62% for initial payment attempts, compared with 35.96% for conventional routing templates.

This represented an improvement of 12.66 percentage points within the tested traffic segment.

Brodsky cautions that machine learning models require regular updates because transaction patterns and provider performance change over time.

Following retraining, a newer version of FinteqHub's model outperformed its predecessor by 7.19 percentage points.

These results demonstrate why the future of payment routing depends on continuously learning systems rather than a fixed set of rules.

Higher approval rates don’t always mean better financial results

Despite the improvements offered by machine learning, Brodsky warns that maximizing payment approval rates shouldn’t be the only objective.

A provider may successfully process more transactions while charging significantly higher processing fees.

Businesses must therefore consider the overall economic outcome rather than simply routing payments through the path with the highest approval probability.

Reliability presents another challenge. If a machine learning model becomes unavailable or makes incorrect decisions, payment infrastructure must keep operating without disrupting transactions.

FinteqHub has incorporated fallback mechanisms into its architecture, allowing transactions to return to established routing rules when necessary.

Brodsky also emphasizes the importance of monitoring AI decisions, including which routes models select, what information they use, and how those choices influence transaction outcomes.

These controls help identify errors and ensure automation does not introduce additional operational risks.

AI could transform payment reconciliation

Beyond routing, Brodsky identifies payment reconciliation as another area where artificial intelligence could significantly improve financial operations.

Companies working with multiple payment providers must regularly compare transaction records between their internal systems and external payment platforms.

Differences in transaction statuses, amounts, and reporting formats can create discrepancies that finance teams must investigate.

FinteqHub's Reconciliation Tool already automates payment-record comparisons and supports more than 23 provider integrations.

The next stage, according to Brodsky, could involve using AI to identify why discrepancies occur, not just detect them.

For example, if a reconciliation system identifies several hundred mismatched transactions, AI could classify the problems, request additional information, generate reports, and recommend corrective actions.

This could significantly reduce the routine investigation required of finance specialists.

By 2027, Brodsky expects payment reconciliation to move toward intelligent exception management, allowing employees to focus on complex cases while automated systems handle more investigative work.

Agentic commerce creates a new challenge for fraud prevention

The growing adoption of autonomous AI agents introduces another challenge for payment infrastructure. Companies including Visa, Google, and Mastercard are developing protocols intended to support payments initiated by software agents acting on behalf of consumers.

Brodsky argues that existing fraud prevention systems may struggle to distinguish legitimate automated transactions from malicious activity.

Consider a customer instructing an AI agent to purchase an airline ticket for no more than €500.

The agent could independently compare available offers, choose an appropriate flight, and initiate payment without the customer interacting directly with the merchant's website.

From the perspective of traditional fraud detection systems, however, the transaction might appear suspicious.

It could originate from a cloud server and lack familiar indicators of human activity, potentially resembling automated fraud.

Payment infrastructure must therefore develop reliable mechanisms for identifying authorized agents and verifying their permissions.

Brodsky points to Google's Agent Payments Protocol, Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol, and Mastercard's Verifiable Intent as examples of the industry's efforts to address these challenges.

Will AI agents replace traditional checkout interfaces?

As autonomous agents become increasingly capable of completing purchases, payment platforms may need to support two distinct transaction scenarios.

The first involves conventional online shopping, where customers interact directly with a checkout interface.

In this environment, businesses will continue to prioritize convenient payment experiences, locally relevant payment methods, saved payment details, and fewer steps to complete a transaction.

The second scenario involves AI agents initiating payments without conventional user interaction.

Rather than relying on a visual checkout interface, these transactions require programmatic access to payment infrastructure, authorization verification, spending limits, and reliable transaction processing.

Both scenarios could operate on the same underlying infrastructure, although their technical and security requirements would differ.

Brodsky expects payment orchestration platforms to evolve accordingly, moving beyond transaction routing toward a broader role in coordinating financial controls, risk management, and autonomous payment activity.

For businesses preparing for 2027, the challenge will be building payment systems that support greater automation without sacrificing reliability, transparency, or control.

headline: Intel stock faces fraud lawsuit over $23 billion share sale after 29% crash
html_content:
Intel faces a shareholder lawsuit alleging that executives concealed worsening personal computer demand before the chipmaker raised $23 billion in an August share offering, adding another challenge to its troubled turnaround.

The proposed class action, filed on 13 November in California, names chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and finance chief David Zinsner. It follows Intel's 28.6% share-price collapse on 30 October, which erased roughly $140 billion from its market value.

The suit raises uncomfortable questions about the timing of management's warnings.

Intel stock (NASDAQ: INTC) closed Friday at $59.66, far below the offering price of $95.

Why Intel's $23 billion offering is under scrutiny

Shareholders led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System allege that Intel understated the damage caused by slowing PC sales, excess inventories and manufacturing constraints.

The complaint covers purchases between 23 July and 29 October. It argues that management's public statements failed to reflect problems already affecting demand and profit margins.

Intel completed its share offering on 12 August, issuing approximately 242 million shares at $95 each.

Regulatory filings show gross proceeds of $23 billion and net proceeds of $22.6 billion, intended for general corporate purposes including investment and working capital.

The plaintiffs allege that the timing gave Intel an incentive to minimise the deterioration. They seek unspecified damages, not $23 billion in compensation.

The allegations arrive amid existing doubts about management. After October's sell-off, Seaport Research Partners analyst Jay Goldberg described the market reaction as "a loss of faith in management's credibility", according to Reuters.

Intel stock: Weak PC demand eclipses AI growth

Intel's third-quarter headline figures initially suggested progress. Revenue climbed 21% to $16.5 billion, while adjusted earnings reached 52 cents per share.

Its data-centre and AI business grew revenue 78% to $7.3 billion, benefiting from demand for processors used in servers.

But the client computing division generated $8.1 billion, down 5% annually. More damaging was Intel's forecast for fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, against analysts' expectations of roughly $17.1 billion.

Rising memory prices have made computers more expensive, while manufacturers are working through surplus inventories.

At the same time, shortages of materials used in chip packaging have restricted Intel's ability to meet demand for server processors.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya highlighted another weakness: limited evidence of progress in attracting customers to Intel's contract-manufacturing operations.

"The stock has not communicated enough traction with external foundry customers," Arya wrote in comments reported by TheStreet.

Bank of America downgraded Intel to Neutral and lowered its price target from $145 to $100.

Can Intel stock rebuild investor confidence?

The lawsuit places Intel's disclosures alongside its operational recovery on investors' list of concerns.

At Friday's close, shares were about 37% below August's offering price, despite remaining roughly 62% higher for the year. That combination complicates arguments that the October collapse created an obvious bargain.

"A cheaper stock does not necessarily offer better value," Dan Kemp, founder of Portfolio Thinking, told MarketWatch after the sell-off.

Investors will look for improvement in PC demand, more dependable server-chip supply and evidence that external customers are committing to Intel's factories.

Successful execution could support earnings and restore confidence. Further inventory reductions, costly manufacturing delays or a prolonged legal dispute would make the recovery harder to assess.

headline: Bitget launches rToken Earn for tokenized ETF yields, with Bitwise to curate strategy
html_content:
Bitget, the world's largest Universal Exchange (UEX), has announced the launch of rToken Earn, a new product allowing eligible non-US users in permitted jurisdictions to generate variable onchain yield on rQQQ and rSPY while retaining exposure to the underlying ETFs.

Available through Bitget Earn, the product removes the need for users to manage a separate wallet or interact directly with decentralised finance (DeFi) protocols.

The introduction of rToken Earn expands the utility of Reality-issued rTokens beyond trading and collateral purposes.

Users can subscribe to dedicated vaults for rSPY and rQQQ directly through their existing Bitget accounts.

Bitget manages subscriptions and redemptions on behalf of users, with no fixed subscription period.

Bitwise Investment Manager, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Bitwise Asset Management, is expected to oversee the curation of the vault strategy.

Ember Protocol will provide the underlying vault infrastructure, while Fluid will support the strategy with its lending markets and liquidity.

The product is built around rTokens issued by Reality, which are backed 1:1 by the corresponding securities. Returns will vary according to market conditions and are not guaranteed.

“An asset should not be limited to just one purpose,” said Gracy Chen, CEO of Bitget.

With rToken Earn, users can maintain their exposure to ETFs like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 trackers while accessing onchain yield through the same Bitget account. With Universal Exchange, we aim to give users more ways to put their assets to work without moving between platforms.

CEO of Bitget
Gracy Chen

The launch comes as Bitget continues to broaden its tokenized equities business in 2026.

According to DeFiLlama Research, cumulative trading volume for rTokens exceeded $1.86 billion between June and July.

In October, Bitget also launched rToken Stock Transfer, allowing eligible users to convert supported brokerage holdings into rTokens through a two-step process.

"Tokenizing equities is the first step towards onchain finance. Putting them to work comes next," said Jonathan Man, Portfolio Manager, Head of Multi-Strategy Solutions & DeFi Strategies, Bitwise.

"We’re set to curate a strategy that connects tokenized ETF exposure with onchain lending opportunities," Jonathan Man added.

"The best financial infrastructure is the kind users never have to think about," said Ibra Barbery, Co-Founder, Ember.

Ember was built so that asset managers can run professional strategies onchain with the controls and security that it requires, and so that platforms like Bitget can offer those strategies through an experience their users already know. Seeing tokenized ETFs move onto that infrastructure is a clear sign of where onchain wealth management is heading.

Co-Founder, Ember
Ibra Barbery

“Lending has always been one of the engines of capital markets, and onchain it can run with full transparency,” said Samyak Jain, Founder and CEO, Fluid.

“Bringing tokenized ETFs into Fluid extends our liquidity layer to some of the most widely held assets in traditional finance, and shows what becomes possible when real-world assets and DeFi share the same infrastructure,” Jain added.

rToken Earn is available from November 16 to eligible non-US users, initially supporting rQQQ and rSPY. Yields remain variable and are not guaranteed, while access is subject to jurisdictional restrictions and eligibility requirements.

Bitwise's strategy curation service is not included in the initial launch and is expected to become available at a later stage.

Yields remain variable and are not guaranteed, while access is subject to jurisdictional restrictions and eligibility requirements. Bitwise's strategy curation service is not included in the initial launch and is expected to become available at a later stage. headline: Why are AMD and Broadcom stocks falling in premarket trading on Monday?
html_content:
AMD and Broadcom shares were falling in premarket trading on Monday as part of a broader semiconductor selloff, with negative sentiment surrounding Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia continuing to pressure chip stocks.

Reports that Huang was considering a comeback, alongside growing support for his reinstatement among employees and industry supporters, have so far failed to lift Nvidia shares, which were also down more than 2.5%.

Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's potential IPO this week will now test whether the AI-fuelled bull market has further room to run.

AMD and Broadcom had initially bucked the Nvidia-led selloff last week, as investors speculated that uncertainty over Nvidia's future without Huang could benefit its competitors in the GPU market.

However, towards the end of the week, investors began reassessing the broader implications of the leadership turmoil for the AI industry and semiconductor trade, dragging the two stocks lower as well.

AMD closed around 9% lower on Friday, while Broadcom shed approximately 5%.

"The dominant driver of risk sentiment is the continuing fallout from the leadership turmoil at AI chip leader Nvidia," Commerzbank Research analysts said in a report.

"The episode has triggered a broader reassessment of the [artificial-intelligence] trade, with investors rotating out of AI-adjacent semiconductor names and into rival chip makers before unwinding those positions as well," the analysts said.

However, both stocks remain around 13% higher over the past five trading sessions, outperforming the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which has gained approximately 7% over the same period.

AMD gets bullish analyst calls amid AI growth expectations

Despite the recent volatility, AMD has received a series of positive analyst calls, with firms pointing to its improving competitive position and strong growth prospects in server CPUs and AI accelerators.

William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform last Thursday, although it did not issue a price target.

The firm said the risk-reward profile had shifted in AMD's favour.

Intel's Xeon roadmap continues to face delays and supply shortages, while the shift towards Arm-based hosts has proved less decisive than previously feared.

AMD's valuation multiple has also declined as earnings estimates have moved higher.

"We see a runway for shares to work from here, with Instinct share gains offering additional upside as AMD stays focused on execution while its largest competitor, Nvidia, contends with a growing leadership and regulatory imbroglio," William Blair analyst Sebastien Naji wrote in a note to clients.

Naji also pointed out that the Dr. Lisa Su-led company was "in the early innings of a multiyear earnings growth trajectory as it continues to execute in server CPUs."

Oppenheimer also raised its rating on Advanced Micro Devices to Outperform from Perform and assigned a price target of $600.

Meanwhile, investment research firm IO Fund believes AMD is gearing up for two major product ramps in 2027, with its server CPUs and AI accelerators expected to deliver stronger-than-anticipated growth, Stockwits reported.

The firm believes the convergence of these two catalysts could strengthen AMD's challenge to Nvidia, even if it does not overtake the chipmaker in GPU market share.

IO Fund said AMD's two strategic product launches — its Venice server CPU lineup and Helios MI400-series AI accelerators — were exceeding the company's initial expectations.

The firm had previously highlighted management's expectations that server CPU revenue would grow more than 70% in 2027, while overall Data Center revenue was expected to increase "well over 100%."

However, AMD has since raised its expectations considerably.

Server CPU revenue is now expected to more than double in 2027, while Data Center AI revenue is projected to grow significantly more than previously anticipated.

AMD has also guided for company-wide revenue growth of more than 80% next year, more than twice the long-term growth model it outlined at its November 2025 Analyst Day.

This comes as major customers, including Anthropic, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle, begin deploying AMD's Helios rack-scale systems.

Broadcom faces concerns over earnings sustainability

Broadcom, meanwhile, received a more cautious assessment from analysts.

Rothschild & Co downgraded the stock to Neutral last week, although it acknowledged that there was considerable upside potential if the company could overcome several challenges.

"Guidance implies Broadcom trades at 11x FY28 EPS," Rothschild analyst Mike Harrison said. "But this counts for little when both the quality and the durability of earnings are under scrutiny."

Harrison also lowered his price target on Broadcom to $398 from $595.

The analyst highlighted the risks associated with Broadcom's exposure to major AI customers, particularly Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as Google's custom AI chip ambitions.

"Broadcom’s alignment with Anthropic and OpenAI means the frontier labs need to establish sustained primacy over open models and become self-financing in short order. Beyond this, the market needs reassurance that Google’s customer-owned tooling efforts will not become widespread. The upside potential to Broadcom shares from clearing these hurdles is appreciable but is unlikely to occur quickly," he added.

headline: Trump plans to name Nvidia among AI 'National Champions': what is this program?
html_content:
The Trump administration is reportedly planning to designate Nvidia as an artificial intelligence “national champion” as part of a new effort to strengthen America's position in the global AI race.

Nvidia will be among more than two dozen ​artificial intelligence-linked companies that will receive benefits of this new initiative, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

The development comes despite the chipmaker's recent leadership turmoil following the resignation of longtime CEO Jensen Huang.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to unveil the selected names, which will also include Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, among others, as per the report.

What is AI national champions program?

According to WSJ, the initiative aims to encourage foreign governments and companies to adopt American AI technology.

The initiative is designed to help US companies win overseas business against Chinese competitors.

The Chinese government heavily funds its domestic technology companies, especially in strategic sectors like artificial intelligence and semiconductors, among others, through extensive state-led industrial policy and financial mechanisms.

The announcement is expected within the next week.

Trump administration wants to package US chips, AI models, software and related infrastructure into integrated offerings that overseas customers can purchase more easily.

Companies in this program could receive faster export license approvals, government support for international operations and access to federal financing.

The initiative builds on the Commerce Department's American AI Exports Program, established under a 2025 executive order to promote the export of complete American AI systems.

Rather than promoting individual products, the program seeks to bring together different parts of the AI ecosystem, including hardware, data systems, AI models, security and applications.

The Commerce Department has already invited industry consortia to submit proposals for such integrated technology packages.

The initiative will provide faster regulatory reviews and government advocacy to the so called "national champions," which is intended to make American technology more attractive to overseas customers.

WSJ also mentions that the official announcement dates are not final and could still be delayed.

Nvidia remains under pressure

The planned designation comes at a complicated time for Nvidia, with the company's export-control practices under immense scrutiny.

Co-founder and long-time CEO Jensen Huang resigned from his role at the company last week amid controversies surrounding his extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese agent.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent weighed in on Nvidia's leadership transition on Sunday, saying the company should look outside its existing management for a permanent CEO.

Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" and questioned whether Nvidia had maintained an adequate culture of compliance with US export restrictions.

“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” Bessent said in an interview on Fox News.

He also pressed Nvidia's board and outside counsel to provide answers within 10 days about the company's compliance practices.

Meanwhile, Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, with House committee chairs requesting closed-door interviews. The Senate Banking Committee has also sought his appearance.

The congressional questioning is expected to address national security concerns surrounding his relationships and Nvidia's chip export practices.

Huang's resignation has also removed him from President Donald Trump's current trip to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.

The former Nvidia chief had accompanied Trump on previous visits to China and played a prominent role in discussions surrounding US-China technology competition.

His absence from the current delegation comes as Nvidia faces increased scrutiny over its China business and the company's leadership transition.

headline: Nasdaq futures crash over 270 points: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens
html_content:
US stock futures were mostly lower on Monday as a rout in Asian shares added to unease ahead of Nvidia's earnings and a packed week of economic releases.

In an early Wall Street Journal snapshot, Nasdaq 100 futures slid 0.9% or 270 points and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.4%, while Dow futures edged 0.1% higher.

The retreat followed Friday's losses of 0.9% for the Nasdaq and 0.4% for the S&P 500.

Investors also face renewed Federal Reserve tightening concerns, weaker Chinese consumption and a test of US spending from retail sales data and major retailers' results.

5 things to know before Wall Street opens

1. Nvidia faces a defining earnings test on Tuesday

Shares fell about 2% in early pre-market trading as investors assessed the company's leadership transition following Jensen Huang's departure.

Nvidia will publish fiscal third-quarter results at approximately 4:20 pm ET on 17 November, followed by a 5 pm conference call.

Analysts expect revenue of roughly $109 billion. More important than the headline figure may be guidance for AI processors and the clarity interim management can offer customers.

2.Fed commentary and minutes may reset rate expectations

Inflation has revived bets on another interest-rate increase in December. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is expected to speak at a San Francisco conference on productivity and jobs on Monday, while minutes from the October meeting arrive on Wednesday at 2 pm ET.

The central bank's latest signals will be watched for how policymakers weigh stubborn prices against economic growth.

3. Asian stocks slide as Chinese demand disappoints

Taiwan's Taiex plunged 6.03%, South Korea's KOSPI lost 3.59% and Japan's Nikkei fell 2.42% on Monday.

Separately, China's October retail sales rose just 0.4% from a year earlier, below forecasts of 0.8%, while industrial output growth slowed to 4.8%.

Investment fell 8.1% over January–October. ING economist Lynn Song argued that weak consumer confidence points to a need for stronger policy support.

4. Retailers offer a test of US consumer resilience

October US retail sales figures are due Tuesday at 8:30 am ET, followed by results from Home Depot that day, Target and Lowe's on Wednesday, and Walmart on Thursday.

Investors will look beyond sales growth to discounts, margins and guidance before the holiday shopping season.

If shoppers are choosing essentials over discretionary products, the reports could expose pressure that headline spending figures obscure.

5. Oil slips as supply begins to outpace demand

Brent crude fell 0.7% to about $95.15 a barrel at 09:19 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate eased 0.4% to $88.19.

The International Energy Agency projects fourth-quarter supply exceeding demand by about 1.7 million barrels a day, as Middle Eastern exports recover.

Cheaper crude could support airlines and consumers but weigh on energy producers.

headline: Is $0.80 next target for XRP after falling below $1?
html_content:
XRP continued to face selling pressure on Monday, trading around $0.956 after declining 13% last week

The cryptocurrency remains below the psychological $1 level as institutional withdrawals and broader market uncertainty weigh on investor confidence.

XRP-linked exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $19.1 million in weekly net outflows, reflecting weaker demand despite continued developments within the XRP ecosystem.

Technical indicators present a mixed picture. XRP has maintained some short-term buying support but remains below important medium- and long-term moving averages.

XRP ETF outflows hit $19.1 million as institutional demand weakens

Institutional sentiment surrounding XRP has deteriorated as exchange-traded funds experience renewed withdrawals.

According to SoSoValue, US spot XRP ETFs recorded approximately $19.1 million in net outflows last week, marking their largest weekly withdrawals since mid-March.

The negative flows suggest that investors are reducing their exposure to XRP amid heightened volatility and broader uncertainty across cryptocurrency markets.

Consequently, sustained withdrawals can weaken market sentiment and contribute to selling pressure.

The latest outflows have coincided with XRP's decline below $1, reinforcing concerns that institutional demand may remain subdued in the near term.

A sustained return to positive net inflows would provide stronger evidence that institutional confidence is recovering.

XRP technical outlook: MACD signals selling pressure despite short-term support

XRP's technical indicators suggest that the cryptocurrency remains vulnerable to further losses despite showing limited short-term resilience.

At approximately $0.956, XRP trades above its 20-period moving average, indicating that some buyers remain active over shorter timeframes.

However, the cryptocurrency continues to trade below its 50-period moving average and significantly below its 200-period moving average.

This suggests that the broader trend remains bearish even as short-term price action shows signs of stabilization.

Currently, $0.8925 represents immediate support. A sustained move below this level could weaken the technical structure and encourage further selling.

Meanwhile, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator signals strong selling pressure.

The Average Directional Index (ADX) also contributes to the bearish trend, although ADX primarily measures trend strength rather than direction.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) reads 26, indicating that XRP is currently in the oversold territory. 

On the lower timeframe, the Stochastic RSI is overbought, raising the possibility that XRP's recent short-term resilience could fade.

Together, these readings suggest that XRP is experiencing a short-term struggle between buyers and sellers within a broader bearish trend.

XRP's immediate technical outlook depends on whether buyers can defend the support near $0.8925. The coin could trade within a range of $0.9074 to $1.0118 over the next few days. 

A successful defense of $0.8925 could allow XRP to consolidate and potentially attempt a recovery toward $1.

Reclaiming the psychological $1 level would represent an important improvement in short-term sentiment.

A sustained move above $1.0118 could also suggest that buying momentum is strengthening beyond the forecast trading range.

However, a decisive breakdown below $0.8925 would increase the risk of a decline toward $0.800.

Currently, the immediate technical outlook remains uncertain. XRP continues to trade below its major medium- and long-term moving averages, while negative momentum indicators suggest that sellers retain an advantage.

A sustained recovery would likely require improving ETF flows, stronger market demand, and a broader stabilization in cryptocurrency prices.

headline: 'AI circular financing crosses $1 trillion': IMF chief flags global economy risks
html_content:
International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Monday that the rapid increase in the scale of circular financing arrangements among AI companies could pose risks to global financial stability.

Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in the Philippines, Georgieva said the global economy had become heavily dependent on the AI industry for growth and investment.

If the confidence around the AI trade suddenly weakens, it would put the world’s financial stability at risk, she said.

The AI investment boom has repeatedly seen off threats even as the bears continue to warn about an imminent collapse akin to previous market crashes.

However, US markets have stayed relatively strong, albeit a bit volatile, despite concerns.

'World economy standing on one leg'

"We have a world economy that is standing on one leg on the AI leg. If this leg wobbles, that can lead to financial stability troubles," Georgieva said.

The IMF estimates that circular financing among AI companies has grown to slightly more than $1 trillion, with approximately two-thirds of the funding coming from debt.

Georgieva acknowledged that the overall amount was not enormous relative to the global economy but warned that the speed of its growth was concerning.

"What concerns us is not the huge size but the rapid increase. So our preoccupation is to watch it and how it is evolving. And most importantly, to what degree it correlates with expectations for profitability for the future," she said.

Circular financing occurs when companies invest money in AI businesses that subsequently use that capital to purchase products or services from their investors.

This risks creating a cycle in which investment flows back to the original company through commercial purchases, potentially strengthening reported revenue and demand while increasing financial interdependence.

The concern is that if AI companies fail to generate sufficient revenue, they may struggle to service their debt or fulfill purchase commitments. This could weaken the financial position of their investors and lenders simultaneously.

Nvidia at centre of AI trade

Nvidia has emerged as one of the most important participants in this financing ecosystem, with its investments and financial guarantees drawing increasing attention.

Nvidia had unveiled a $500 billion AI financing platform in August.

The financing structure was led by the company's longtime CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down last week amid controversy surrounding his extramarital affairs including one involving a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

Bank of America analysts estimate that apart from the $500 billion platform, Nvidia had invested around $70 billion in AI companies through equity stakes and provided approximately $230 billion in financial guarantees as of August.

One of its largest commitments involves a guarantee of up to $105 billion to support financing for an Ohio data center being developed by SoftBank-owned SB Energy for OpenAI.

The leadership change has added uncertainty to the financing initiative, although Reuters reports that Nvidia's financial partners continue discussing deals and have not indicated that the program has been suspended.

Huang's controversy could change things

Analysts are increasingly concerned that Nvidia's willingness to finance AI startups and specialized cloud providers could weaken as lenders demand stronger safeguards.

JPMorgan credit analyst Erica Spear has warned that new deals could take longer or require additional compensation for investors.

UBS analyst Tim Arcuri has estimated that a pullback in Nvidia financing could remove $50 billion or more from the AI funding system.

Georgieva, meanwhile, cautioned that investor enthusiasm can run ahead of what the technology has actually delivered.

The IMF has warned that an AI investment correction, amplified by excessive leverage, could have consequences extending beyond technology stocks.

Its October analysis outlined a worst-case scenario in which US equities could fall 20% and global output could end up 1.1% below its baseline by 2028.

headline: 4 Canadian stocks that stand to benefit from US midterm elections
html_content:
Canada’s stock market has emerged as an unlikely winner of the 2026 US midterm elections.

After Democrats captured control of Congress, investors are increasingly betting that Washington will take a less confrontational approach toward trade with Canada.

That optimism has already helped fuel a rally in Canadian stocks, with market participants looking for names that were most exposed to tariffs, trade uncertainty, or cross-border business disruption.

Four names stand out: Magna International, Canada Goose, Algoma Steel, and Descartes Systems.

Magna International (MGA)

Magna International could be among the biggest beneficiaries of any improvement in US-Canada trade relations.

The automotive supplier operates deeply within the North American vehicle manufacturing ecosystem, where parts routinely cross borders multiple times before a finished vehicle reaches consumers.

Tariffs and trade tensions have weighed on sentiment toward companies tied to that integrated supply chain, creating uncertainty around production volumes and costs.

A more trade-friendly backdrop following the midterms could ease those concerns and support stronger demand from automakers.

As investors reassess the outlook for cross-border vehicle production, Magna stock stands out as a potential winner from reduced policy risk.

Canada Goose (GOOS)

Luxury outerwear maker Canada Goose may also benefit if political momentum shifts toward lower trade barriers.

The company derives a meaningful portion of its revenue from the US, making it sensitive to changes in cross-border commerce and consumer sentiment.

While tariffs were not the only challenge facing the retailer over the past two years, escalating trade disputes added another layer of uncertainty for investors evaluating North American consumer brands.

Any progress toward tariff reductions or a more predictable trade environment could improve confidence in the company’s growth prospects.

That could provide fresh support for GOOS stock, which has largely lagged the broader market’s post-election enthusiasm.

Algoma Steel (ASTL)

Algoma Steel has perhaps the clearest connection to the tariff story.

The Ontario-based steel producer has faced significant pressure from US trade restrictions, which reduced the importance of its American business and complicated its expansion efforts.

Management has previously cited tariff-related headwinds when discussing operating challenges, and the company has taken steps to adapt to a more difficult trading environment.

If the new Congress succeeds in increasing scrutiny of existing tariffs or encourages negotiations between Washington and Ottawa, ASTL could regain access to a more favorable market backdrop.

Investors searching for a direct trade-policy recovery play may find the steelmaker particularly compelling.

Descartes Systems (DSGX)

Unlike the other companies on this list, Descartes Systems is not a tariff-sensitive manufacturer.

Instead, the logistics and supply chain software provider could benefit from improving investor sentiment. Periods of heightened geopolitical uncertainty often push capital toward defensive sectors, leaving growth-oriented technology names out of favour.

As concerns about a prolonged trade conflict begin to ease, investors may become more willing to rotate back into software and digital infrastructure companies.

Descartes, whose platform helps businesses manage global supply chains and trade compliance, is well positioned to benefit from that shift.

A more stable policy environment could help refocus attention on the company’s long-term growth opportunities.

headline: Top Nasdaq 100 stocks to watch: Nvidia, Take-Take Two Interactive, Walmart
html_content:
The Nasdaq 100 Index has slumped and moved into a technical correction after falling by over 10% from its all-time high. It dropped to 27,945 on Friday as jitters surrounding the artificial intelligence (AI) industry continues. This article looks at some of the top stocks to watch this week, including Nvidia (NVDA), Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), and Walmart (WMT).

Nvidia to publish earnings as Jensen Huang lobbies to get old job back

Nvidia stock has been in the spotlight in the past few weeks as investors have focused on Jensen Huang’s developments. In an apology letter to his employees last week, Huang admitted to infidelity. After that, it was reported that he had relationships with at least two other employees, leading to a resignation.

Nvidia stock will be in the spotlight for three main reasons. First, Huang is lobbying hard to get his job back. A petition to have him back has garnered close to 200k signatures, including Elon Musk, Travis Kalanick, and Tom Lee. Thousands of employees have also signed the petition. 

Second, with the stock falling by double digits from its peak this year, there is a likelihood that the initial shareholder lawsuits will start coming up. These shareholders will argue that the company misled them on Huang’s relationships and its Chinese chip sales. 

Third, and most importantly, the company will publish its first earnings report after Huang’s resignation. Analysts expects the results to show that Nvidia’s revenue growth intensified last quarter. 

Kyro App data shows that the average estimate is that its revenue jumped by 90% last quarter to $108 billion. Its earnings-per-share (EPS) is expected to soar to $2.47 from $1.3. Nvidia has a long track record of beating analysts estimates and raising the targets.

Take-Two Interactive to release GTA VI

Take-Two Interactive, one of the biggest gaming companies in the world, will also be in the spotlight this week as it releases the Grand Theft Auto VI game. This game is expected to be the biggest release of the year. Indeed, Logitech, a company that makes accessories, has offered its employees a day off to play the game. Estimates are that the game’s presales have jumped to over $6 billion. 

Therefore, there is a likelihood that the stock will do well when the company releases the game. The challenge, however, is that the game’s release has already been priced in. As such, there is a risk that the stock will pull back.

Another challenge is that the game’s initial statistics will miss estimates as NBA 2K27 game did mid this year. Also, it may experience some weakness if the game has some major bugs. 

Walmart to publish its earnings

Walmart, the biggest retailer in the United States is a big Nasdaq 100 constituent. It was added to the index after it decamped from the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

The company will be in the spotlight this week as it publishes its financial results on Thursday. These earnings will come two days after the US releases the official retail sales numbers for last month. 

The earnings report also comes as the company’s stock continues recovering, with bulls eying the all-time high. 

Analysts are hoping that the upcoming earnings report will be better than the last one, which showed that its sales slowed down. Kyro data shows that analysts expect the earnings report to show that its revenue jumped by 5.34% to $187 billion, with its EPS hitting $0.64. A strong earnings report and outlook will boost the stock.

There are other top Nasdaq 100 stocks to watch this week, including Palo Alto Networks (PANW), AMD, SpaceX, and CoreWeave. SpaceX will react to the successful Starship Flight 15 launch.

headline: Anthropic IPO nears: Why ANT could pop on day one, then dive
html_content:
Anthropic, the creator of Claude, is set to go public this week in what will be the second-biggest IPO on record, behind Elon Musk’s SpaceX. The company aims to raise over $60 billion at a valuation close to $1.5 trillion. However, history shows that the initial surge often gives way to a sharp reversal, costing investors billions of dollars.

Anthropic IPO will raise billions of dollars

The biggest stock market news this week will be the upcoming Anthropic IPO, which will be the second time that an AI chatbot creator has gone public in the United States. The initial one was SpaceX, which owns Grok.

Anthropic will raise over $60 billion from global investors, who will have an opportunity to invest in the most advanced AI company in the world. Estimates are that the company will attract a valuation of over $1.5 trillion.

The recently released S1 statement showed that Anthropic’s business is growing rapidly this year. Its revenue soared to over $16 billion in the third quarter. However, the company’s spending has accelerated, with management planning to spend over $400 billion in compute through 2030.

The IPO will benefit initial investors who took the risk in it. Some of the top companies that will benefit include popular names like Amazon, Alphabet, and Salesforce. Venture capital firms like Sequoia, ICONIQ, and Lightspeed will also benefit.

History shows ANT stock may pop then drop

The upcoming Anthropic IPO will be a big deal for the company and the markets. However, there is a risk that the stock will jump, even double, and then plunge after the initial hype fades.

One reason for this is that the IPO is happening at a time when demand for AI companies has slumped in the past few months. Nvidia, the biggest name of them all, has tumbled by over 30% from its peak. 

Most importantly, in Hong Kong, similar companies like MiniMax and Z.ai have all plunged to their record lows, a few months after they went public in highly hyped IPOs.

At the same time, a closer look at all the past IPOs shows that they initially jump and then plunge. SpaceX, initially soared to $225 in June and then started its strong downward trend, eventually reaching a low of $105 in July. Its attempts to rebound and retest its all-time highs have failed. 

The same happened with Cerebras, an Nvidia competitor that went public in May. It initially doubled to $386 and then plunged to the current $108.7. The initial surge happened because investors were betting on the company being able to disrupt Nvidia and other chipmakers.

READ MORE: Anthropic IPO could see historic $250M retail buying on debut, Vanda Research says

Circle Internet Group, the creator of USDC, initially soared from $60 after its IPO to a record high of $300. It then started falling, and reached a low of $50 a few months after going public. Its stock has struggled as demand for the USDC stablecoin fades.

Figma, a top technology company in the design industry, also initially popped to $142 and then dropped to the current $19.45. The same has happened among other companies that went public last year, including Klarna, Gemini Space Station, and Bullish. In a statement, John Ettinger, a Federated Hermes analyst, wrote that:

“In this IPO market you have to be a bit discerning . . . and realise if this is an IPO which you might be able to pick up cheaper in a few months.”

In addition to its elevated costs, ANT stock may drop for several other reasons. The most notable one is that competition in the industry is rising. In addition to American companies like OpenAI, Google, Meta Platforms, and SpaceX, it is facing more competition from Chinese firms like Moonshot and DeepSeek. Also, it will need to keep spending billions of dollars a year.

headline: SanDisk stock looks cheap, but technicals point to lower Nvidia earnings
html_content:
SanDisk stock extended its strong sell-off on Monday as technology companies continued falling ahead of the closely watched Nvidia earnings report. SNDK dropped to $800, down by over 65% from its highest point this year. This trend may continue after the stock formed an inverted cup-and-handle pattern and as a death cross pattern nears. 

SanDisk stock falls ahead of Nvidia earnings

SNDK and other technology companies continued their downward spiral this week. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index has dropped by over 365 points. Similarly, the S&P 500 and Dow Jones were also in the red.

Technology companies are falling as investors assess the ongoing crisis at Nvidia, where Jensen Huang, the founder, was pushed out last week. Huang is now plotting a way to come back to the company, with an online letter attracting over 200k signatures.

The crisis is a big risk for the AI industry because, under Huang, the company evolved into its “central banker.” It has invested in some of the top companies in the industry, including neoclouds like CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN. 

Huang also organized a $500 billion financing deal with some of the biggest financial services companies in the world, including Apollo Global and Blackstone. It is unclear whether the funding will continue now that its architect has left the company.

The next important catalyst for SanDisk stock will be Nvidia earnings that comes out on Tuesday. This earnings report will act as a barometer for the artificial intelligence industry. A strong earnings report and a boost in guidance will be bullish for companies in the AI space.

SanDisk’s business is thriving and is highly undervalued

SanDisk’s business is doing well as demand for its products remain elevated. The last earnings report showed that its revenue jumped to $11 billion, up by 23% from the previous quarter. It soared by 378% from the same period last year, making it one of the fastest-growing companies in the world.

Most notably, the management believes that SanDisk has more room for growth as the data center rollout gains steam. The company believes that the supply for memory products will remain at an elevated level. For example, it expects that its fiscal second-quarter revenue will be between $12.2 billion and $12.6 billion. The upper estimate is higher than the average target of $12.51 billion. 

SanDisk has moved to insulate itself from the boom and bust cycles of the memory industry by creating large deals with its clients. These deals have a floor and ceiling prices, which will help it generate stable revenue growth over time.

The company has also become one of the cheapest names on Wall Street, with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 3.8, much lower than the S&P 500 average of 18. It is also much lower than other companies, including Micron and Nvidia.

SanDisk stock price technical analysis

SNDK stock chart | Chart: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the SNDK stock has been in a strong sell-off this month. It has already formed an inverted cup-and-handle pattern, a common continuation sign in technical analysis. 

The stock is also about to form a death cross pattern, which happens when the 50-day and 200-day moving averages cross each other. This death cross often leads to more downside over time. 

The stock has remained below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level, confirming the bearish outlook. It has also remained below the Supertrend indicator. Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, with the next level to watch will be at $600. A move above the resistance level of $998 will invalidate the bearish outlook and point to more downside.

headline: Rocket Lab stock jumped after earnings, but key risks points to a reversal
html_content:
Rocket Lab stock has rebounded in the past few days as investors reacted to its earnings report, which showed that its revenue growth and backlog continued growing. RKLB jumped to a high of $67, its highest level since October 9. Still, the company could be at risk after SpaceX’s Starship launch.

Rocket Lab published strong earnings

RKLB stock jumped after the company published its financial results, which showed that its business continued to grow. 

Rocket Lab’s revenue jumped by 73% in the third quarter as demand for its services soared. It made $268 million, with its backlog soaring by 52% to $3.6 billion. This backlog is spread across its key products like Electron, HASTE, and Neutron.

For example, the company secured over $515 million in Neutron contracts from constellation operators. These contracts brought its backlog to 16 missions ahead of its launch. 

Most notably, the company now expects that its revenue will keep growing over time. The company expects that its revenue will jump to between $270 million and $290 million, higher than the average estimate of $270 million.

This guidance is notable because it excludes any Neutron revenue, which was expected to happen to start this quarter. In the earnings call, the management justified the Neutron delay to 2027 after it found voids in the propellant tanks forward dome. 

The team has surged to manufacture a replacement part. After this is done, it will go through several stages to ensure that it is safe for launch. The view is that a premature launch would be more costly than the delay. In his statement, Peter Beck, the founder and CEO said:

“The massive surge in Neutron bookings this quarter is the strongest signal yet of where the launch market is headed. We signed eight missions for roughly $515 million, with multiple flights sold at an elevated base price of $70 million per launch. Neutron's first 16 launches are booked.”

Analysts are bullish but skeptical about RKLB stock

Top analysts tracking the company are generally bullish on its stock, but have scaled down their targets until Neutron is up and running. Michael Filatov, a Berenberg Bank analyst maintained a bullish view and set a target of $85, up modestly from where it is today. 

Kristine Liwag, a Morgan Stanley analyst, lowered his target from $105 to $103, while Needham’s Ryan Koontz, slashed the target from $120 to $100. Other analysts who slashed their targets are from Barclays, KeyCorp, Cantor Fitzgerald, and Piper Sandler. Most of these analysts believe that the company will need to prove that Neutron works. 

Rocket Lab stock is reacting to the latest SpaceX rocket launch. The company caught part of its Starship rocket on return to earth, a move that will lower the cost of these launches. 

Also, investors are waiting for the closing of the Iridium transaction. It has already raised the funds through a combination of debt and equity.

Rocket Lab stock technical analysis

RKLB stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the RKLB stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months, moving from a high of $151 in June to a low of $44.30. It recently dropped below the important support level of $58.20, the lower side of the head-and-shoulders pattern. A H&S pattern is one of the most common bearish reversal patterns in technical analysis.

The stock has plunged below all moving averages and has retested the lower side of the H&S pattern. Therefore, there is a likelihood that the stock will resume the downward trend, potentially to this month’s low of $44.30. A move below that level will point to more downside.

headline: Take-Two Interactive stock jumps as this analyst sees upside beyond GTA VI launch
html_content:
Take-Two Interactive shares rose in premarket trading on Monday as excitement built ahead of the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Investors are continuing to bet on the commercial potential of the latest installment in one of gaming's biggest franchises.

The stock gained about 2.63% ahead of the opening bell and seemed set to open the week on a high prior to the November 19 launch, scheduled for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Gaming enthusiasts are eagerly awaiting GTA VI, while investors have also been piling into the game's developer. Take-Two Interactive shares have gained close to 20% in November.

The excitement has been building around the November 19 launch, which will mark the first mainline Grand Theft Auto release since 2013's GTA V, a game that has sold more than 235 million copies.

GTA VI pre-orders exceed expectations

Take-Two executives have indicated that demand for the upcoming game is already exceptionally strong.

CEO Strauss Zelnick said last week that pre-orders were running "far in excess" of the company's initial expectations, describing the momentum as extraordinary.

Research firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA VI has already generated more than $1 billion in sales, highlighting the enormous commercial expectations surrounding the release.

Pre-loading began earlier this month, while physical copies containing download codes reached retailers last week.

The scale of anticipation has also extended beyond the gaming community, with players making plans around the launch.

BambooHR, a workplace time-off platform, estimates that nearly one in five workers are planning to take time off for the game's release.

Trailers and marketing campaigns have generated substantial online engagement, while the game's setting in a modern-day Vice City-inspired Leonida has fuelled years of speculation and anticipation.

Strong outlook supports Take-Two shares

The latest investor enthusiasm follows Take-Two's fiscal second-quarter results, reported on November 9.

Net bookings fell 18% year over year to $1.60 billion, while revenue came in at approximately $1.50 billion. Both figures missed some analyst estimates amid softer performance from other titles, including NBA 2K27.

However, the company reiterated its full-year fiscal 2027 net bookings guidance of $8 billion to $8.2 billion.

Take-Two also projected a strong third quarter, forecasting net bookings of $3.35 billion to $3.50 billion, driven largely by the GTA VI launch.

The outlook has kept Wall Street focused on the potential revenue contribution from the new game and the longer-term opportunities that could follow its release.

Wall Street sees further upside for Take-Two

Analysts remain largely positive on Take-Two, with the stock carrying a Strong Buy consensus rating, as per TipRanks.

Fresh backing came from Jefferies over the weekend, as the brokerage reiterated its Buy rating and $300 price target, arguing that GTA VI could be just the beginning of a longer monetization opportunity.

"GTA VI is just the beginning," Jefferies said.

Analyst James Heaney believes the bigger opportunity lies in how Take-Two monetizes the franchise over several years rather than just the initial launch.

"While the launch itself is well understood, we believe the bigger opportunity is the duration of the GTA VI monetization cycle. GTA Online and an eventual PC release could provide meaningful incremental bookings into FY28, neither of which we believe is embedded in FY27 guidance.

"We continue to model FY27 bookings above the high end of guidance and see upside to our $10 FY28 EPS estimate as the GTA VI ecosystem scales," Heaney wrote.

JPMorgan has also maintained Take-Two as its top pick in the mid and small-cap space, with a price target of $310.

The brokerage continues to estimate that GTA Online could generate net bookings of approximately $2.6 billion in fiscal 2028 and $3.3 billion in fiscal 2029.

With the November 19 launch approaching, Take-Two is entering one of the most anticipated release weeks in the gaming industry's history.

headline: Nasdaq opens 1.5% lower as Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO weigh on AI stocks
html_content:
US stocks opened lower on Monday as technology shares came under renewed pressure ahead of Nvidia's quarterly earnings and Anthropic's highly anticipated stock market debut later this week.

Investors are assessing whether demand for artificial intelligence stocks can withstand recent market volatility, rising borrowing costs and uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership.

The Nasdaq Composite declined 1.54%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.95%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost around 91 points.

Nvidia stock leads AI-related selloff

Nvidia shares fell 2% in trading on Monday, extending a difficult period for the chipmaker following the resignation of founder Jensen Huang as CEO and board member.

The company is scheduled to report its third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday.

Analysts expect nearly 100% year-over-year growth in revenue and earnings, but investors are likely to focus on the company's forward guidance and its ability to maintain growth under new leadership.

Huang stepped down following reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing.

However, a Financial Times report on Monday indicated that he was considering a return as CEO.

The leadership controversy has added uncertainty to the AI trade.

Nvidia shares lost 13% last week, marking their biggest weekly decline since April 2025 and their longest losing streak since October 2012.

Other semiconductor stocks also declined in trading.

Intel and Advanced Micro Devices fell more than 6% and 3%, respectively, while Broadcom dropped 4.9% and Micron lost 7.3%.

The weakness extended to companies involved in AI infrastructure.

Neocloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius fell 5.2% and 8%, respectively.

Data-centre-linked companies IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific also recorded losses.

Anthropic IPO to test appetite for AI stocks

Investors are also watching Anthropic's expected public market debut later this week, which could provide another indication of appetite for AI-related investments.

The company is reportedly targeting a valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion, with shares expected to be priced between $70 and $78.

The IPO comes at a time when investors are reassessing valuations and spending commitments across the AI industry.

Its performance, alongside Nvidia's earnings and guidance, could influence whether the recent correction in technology stocks continues.

The broader AI trade has faced pressure from higher borrowing costs, concerns about slower economic growth and uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership.

Despite the latest weakness, Wall Street ended the previous week on a positive note.

headline: Ron Baron's $30T forecast for SpaceX: possibility or fantasy?
html_content:
Billionaire investor Ron Baron maintains that SpaceX (SPCX) could eventually be worth as much as $30 trillion – a prediction that appears wildly ambitious at first glance.

A move from about $1.9 trillion today to $30 trillion would require extraordinary execution across several business lines.

Yet history shows investors have repeatedly underestimated scale of transformative technologies, and SpaceX stock now sits at the intersection of “multiple trillion-dollar opportunities” – spanning launch services, satellite connectivity, AI, and advanced computing infrastructure.

Why Baron is uber bullish on SpaceX stock

Based on current valuations, SpaceX would need to compound at more than 30% annually over a decade to approach a $30 trillion market cap.

Critics of Baron’s forecast are correct about one thing – sustaining that sort of annualized returns from an already massive valuation is exceptionally difficult.

On the flip side, however, investors must remember that similar skepticism surrounded companies such as Amazon, Nvidia, and Tesla during their early hypergrowth phases.

Each appeared expensive relative to contemporary earnings before new markets dramatically expanded their addressable opportunities.

The central question is not whether SpaceX can continue selling rocket launches, but whether the company can leverage its tech lead to capture multiple high-growth industries simultaneously.

If Starlink, AI infrastructure, orbital computing and next-gen launch systems all scale successfully, Baron’s forecast for SPCX shares may ultimately prove less demanding than it appears.

SPCX shares to benefit from more than space business

Baron’s thesis for SpaceX shares increasingly rests on businesses that extend far beyond aerospace.

Starlink has become a global connectivity platform, serving consumers, enterprises, governments and defense customers.

At the same time, investors are paying increasing attention to the firm’s AI ambitions following its integration with Musk's broader artificial intelligence ecosystem.

Several analysts now view computing infrastructure as the largest long-term value driver.

Rather than relying solely on satellite revenue, SpaceX is investing heavily in terrestrial AI data centers while also advancing plans for orbital computing facilities that could become commercially viable later this decade.

This shift dramatically expands the company's potential revenue pool.

The appeal is straightforward.

Global demand for AI compute continues to outstrip supply, creating opportunities for operators capable of deploying large-scale infrastructure.

If SpaceX successfully combines launch economics, energy access, networking capabilities and AI services under one umbrella, investors could be looking at a business model unlike anything currently represented in public markets.

That possibility helps explain why some long-term shareholders remain comfortable with seemingly aggressive valuation assumptions.

Bernstein reiterates bullish view on SpaceX

Wall Street is not universally embracing a $30 trillion future, but analysts remain bullish on SPCX stock nonetheless.

Bernstein recently reiterated its Outperform rating on SpaceX and raised its price target to $268, citing the firm’s expanding AI infrastructure strategy and faster-than-expected computing capacity buildout.

Bernstein expects SpaceX’s terrestrial computing footprint to grow substantially over the next several years while also assigning value to planned orbital data-center initiatives.

The investment firm's updated forecasts include significantly higher revenue expectations as the company scales both AI and connectivity operations.

Importantly, the firm's bullish thesis does not require SpaceX to achieve its most ambitious management targets or complete a merger with Tesla.

Bernstein’s target reflects confidence that investors may still be underestimating the commercial potential of SpaceX’s emerging AI ecosystem.

While risks remain substantial, including execution challenges, capital requirements, and technological hurdles, Bernstein’s outlook suggests that Wall Street continues to see meaningful upside.

For investors evaluating Ron Baron’s $30 trillion prediction, that may be the strongest evidence yet that the idea belongs in the realm of possibility rather than fantasy.

headline: Why Micron and Sandisk stocks are falling on Monday?
html_content:
Micron Technology MU and SanDisk shares fell sharply on Monday as uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

Micron shares dropped around 7.5% in early trading, while SanDisk declined 8.5% as part of a broader pullback in AI-related semiconductor stocks.

Pressure also came from a report by semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis, which suggested that the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom could soon begin to lose momentum.

Why are Micron and SanDisk stocks falling?

The decline in memory stocks was driven partly by lingering uncertainty surrounding Nvidia following the resignation of longtime CEO Jensen Huang amid controversies involving multiple alleged affairs.

One of the reported relationships involved a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of acting as an intelligence asset for Beijing.

Micron is a key supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and other DRAM used alongside Nvidia's AI accelerators in data centers.

Any slowdown or shift in AI infrastructure spending linked to Nvidia's leadership transition could therefore weigh on sentiment toward memory manufacturers.

SanDisk also plays an important role in the AI ecosystem as a supplier of NAND flash memory and enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs).

Nvidia is not just a major chipmaker but also a significant financier in the broader AI industry, making developments surrounding the company relevant to investors across the semiconductor ecosystem.

The broader market also opened lower, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling more than 3% in early trading.

Korean memory chipmakers struggled in parallel. Samsung Electronics fell roughly 4.5%, while SK Hynix dropped about 6.7% in Seoul trading, contributing to a decline of more than 3.5% in the Kospi index.

Both companies face similar questions surrounding AI demand and the uncertainty stemming from Nvidia's leadership crisis.

SemiAnalysis cuts AI spending forecasts

Adding to the pressure, semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis said over the weekend that the AI boom could be heading toward a slowdown.

The firm cut its estimate for global AI accelerator capital expenditure in 2028 to $758 billion from $1.054 trillion, a reduction of 28%.

It also lowered its 2030 forecast to $923 billion from $1.531 trillion, marking a reduction of approximately 40%.

SemiAnalysis cited three major reasons for the sharp revisions.

First, the firm said demand-side momentum had weakened, raising questions about the pace at which AI infrastructure investments would continue expanding.

Second, the financing environment has tightened, with both debt and equity investors showing markedly less interest in funding AI projects.

This could make it more difficult for companies building data centers and expanding computing capacity to secure the capital required for their plans.

Third, the changing political environment and increased regulatory scrutiny could slow the pace of AI infrastructure development, potentially affecting the rollout of new data centers and related projects.

The revised forecasts add to concerns that the enormous investments made by technology companies in AI infrastructure may not translate into demand at the pace previously anticipated.

Micron faces additional pressure

Adding another layer of uncertainty for Micron, a US federal judge in California on November 14 rejected a motion to dismiss a class-action antitrust lawsuit against Micron, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

The lawsuit alleges that the three companies, which collectively control more than 90% of the global DRAM market, coordinated to restrict supplies of conventional memory products, including DDR4 and DDR5.

The plaintiffs allege that the companies' actions pushed memory prices sharply higher while shifting manufacturing capacity toward high-bandwidth memory used in AI infrastructure.

With the judge rejecting the motion to dismiss, the case will now proceed, adding another potential overhang for Micron as investors weigh the broader challenges facing the memory chip industry.
