headline: Disney earnings preview: why subscriber count may not be most important number
html_content:
Disney (DIS) reports fiscal Q4 earnings before the opening bell on November 17, with Wall Street expecting earnings of roughly $1.68 per share on revenue of $25.16 billion.

That implies more than 50% EPS growth from a year ago; but investors may be asking the wrong question.

After years of focusing on streaming losses, subscriber counts, and cord-cutting fears, Disney’s upcoming report could reveal whether the entertainment giant has entered a new phase: one where streaming, parks, and capital returns work together to drive sustained earnings growth.

Why subscriber count is less significant now for Disney

The most important number for DIS shares on Tuesday may not be subscriber growth at all.

During its most recent quarter, Disney's streaming business continued its profitability turnaround, with entertainment streaming revenue rising 11% and margin expanding into double-digit territory.

Management has repeatedly emphasized its goal of maintaining at least a 10% streaming margin, a milestone that would have seemed ambitious only a few years ago.

Investors should focus less on how many subscribers Disney adds and more on whether pricing power remains intact.

Disney has increasingly shifted from a "growth at all costs" strategy toward monetization through higher subscription prices, advertising-supported tiers, and tighter platform integration between Disney+ and Hulu.

If operating margins continue expanding, the streaming segment could become a meaningful contributor to earnings rather than merely a source of revenue growth.

That distinction matters because profitable streaming businesses generally command higher investor confidence than subscriber-chasing platforms.

Parks segment remains significant for DIS stock

While headlines often focus on Disney+, the Experiences division remains the company’s financial backbone.

In Q3, the segment generated nearly $10 billion in revenue – with domestic attendance rising 3% and per-capita guest spending increasing 4%.

Revenue from parks, cruises, and experiences came in up 10% despite broader concerns about consumer spending and travel demand.

That outperformance is particularly notable because several travel-related businesses have seen signs of softer consumer demand.

Disney, however, continues to benefit from premium pricing, cruise expansion, and strong brand loyalty.

Investors should watch management's commentary on forward bookings and guest spending trends.

If those metrics remain resilient, Disney could further strengthen the narrative that its parks business is less cyclical and more durable than many analysts once assumed.

Options traders expect fireworks, but guidance matters more

Options analysis highlights an interesting setup ahead of the quarterly release.

Various estimates suggest traders are pricing in about a 6.2% move following the report, implying expectations for a meaningful post-earnings reaction.

Yet history suggests the headline numbers may not be the decisive factor.

Disney has beaten EPS estimates in eight consecutive quarters, meaning investors largely expect another strong print.

Instead, the real catalyst could be fiscal 2027 guidance.

Management has already raised its fiscal 2026 share-repurchase target to at least $9 billion while maintaining confidence in earnings growth and streaming profitability.

If Disney couples another earnings beat with stronger cash-flow expectations and a shareholder-friendly capital allocation outlook, investors may begin viewing the company less as a turnaround story and more as a mature compounder.

That shift in perception could prove far more important for Disney shares than any single quarter's earnings result.

headline: Trump just gave Nvidia bulls a lifeline: find out more
html_content:
Nvidia (NVDA) remains in focus after the artificial intelligence (AI) darling found an unexpected ally in President Donald Trump on Monday.

As questions continue to swirl around former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and his relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, Trump dismissed suggestions that it compromised US national security.

The President further indicated that he would not oppose Huang eventually returning to NVDA.

For Nvidia, the comments provide a meaningful clue about how Washington views the giant’s role in the global AI race going forward.

Trump sees Nvidia as too important to sideline

While Trump's remarks focused on Jensen Huang, the bigger takeaway for markets is the administration's apparent unwillingness to treat Nvidia as a national security offender.

The president said the controversy did not put the US at risk and questioned whether allegations surrounding Alice Huang had been proven.

He even suggested he would not mind seeing Jensen Huang return to Nvidia, calling such an outcome “not a bad idea.”

For NVDA shares, this lowers the risk of an aggressive political backlash against the titan itself.

In recent weeks, fears had grown that the scandal could trigger harsher treatment from Washington, potentially affecting the company's strategic position in the AI industry.

Instead, Trump's comments suggest White House may view Nvidia as too important to America’s technological leadership to become collateral damage in a controversy surrounding its former chief executive.

That could help stabilize investor sentiment at a time when confidence has been shaken by management uncertainty and regulatory scrutiny.

The bigger issue is still China and export controls

Investors still should not mistake Trump's remarks for a clean bill of health for Nvidia shares.

The central question facing Nvidia has increasingly shifted from Huang's personal conduct to whether the company fully complied with US restrictions on advanced AI chip sales.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said over the weekend that regulators are more concerned with whether Nvidia's chips reached China through intermediaries than with the headline-grabbing allegations involving Huang.

That is a far more consequential issue for shareholders because it directly affects NVDA’s ability to participate in one of the world's most important AI markets.

Any evidence of compliance failures could invite stricter oversight, additional investigations, or tighter export rules.

Still, Trump's latest comments hint that Washington may focus on enforcing existing policies rather than targeting Nvidia as a company.

The president also said he could discuss Nvidia during meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping, underscoring the firm's growing importance in US-China technology negotiations.

What NVDA shares investors should watch next

Ultimately, NVDA's trajectory will be determined less by political headlines and more by regulatory outcomes.

Trump's defense of Huang removes some immediate pressure and reduces the likelihood of the most bearish scenario feared by investors: a broad political campaign against Nvidia.

Yet significant questions remain about export-control compliance, leadership succession, and future access to Chinese customers.

The key takeaway is that the White House appears eager to preserve Nvidia's status as a strategic American technology leader, even as scrutiny intensifies.

If that view holds, the market's focus is likely to shift away from scandal and back toward the factors that matter most: AI demand, execution, and Nvidia's ability to maintain its dominance in an increasingly geopolitical semiconductor industry.

headline: Why is Strategy (MSTR) stock falling 7% on Monday?
html_content:
Strategy (formerly known as MicroStrategy) shares (MSTR) fell 7% on Monday after Bitcoin fell below $65,000. The potential removal of Strategy from MSCI indices also weighed on the stock.

The Michael Saylor-led company also announced the acquisition of 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 million in the previous week.

Strategy buys 485 Bitcoin while repurchasing preferred shares

Strategy purchased 485 Bitcoin at an average price of $68,887 between Monday and Sunday, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday.

The acquisition brought the company's total Bitcoin holdings to 850,849 BTC.

The company raised $244.7 million by selling 2.09 million common shares during the week.

It allocated $33.4 million of the proceeds to Bitcoin purchases, $206.3 million to repurchasing its STRC preferred shares, and $5 million to its separate cash balance.

Strategy funded the remaining $21.8 million of its STRC buybacks with interest earned on its cash and short-term investments.

It repurchased 2.28 million STRC shares during the week.

STRC is Strategy's variable-rate preferred stock, which pays regular dividends to shareholders.

The company maintained its annual dividend rate at 12% for December, saying it intends to keep the rate unchanged until the shares demonstrate sustained trading near $100.

Strategy also reported a $4.75 billion US dollar reserve after using $18.9 million to pay preferred stock dividends.

Its separate cash balance stood at $151.2 million as of Sunday.

The latest figures follow a week in which the company spent $188.3 million repurchasing STRC shares and $81.9 million buying Bitcoin.

MSCI decision adds pressure on Strategy shares

The potential removal of Strategy from MSCI indices has added another source of uncertainty for investors.

MSCI confirmed on Wednesday that it was moving to delist Strategy from its USA Index under new eligibility rules for so-called "non-operating companies".

The rules assess companies' operating assets alongside five financial measures, replacing previous temporary restrictions on firms that held at least half of their assets in cryptocurrencies.

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor previously described the treatment as "discriminatory".

The proposed change could affect investor demand for the stock, as index-linked funds may need to adjust their holdings if the removal proceeds.

Bitcoin slump puts Strategy's holdings under pressure

Bitcoin fell around 12.6% last week, extending a multi-week decline that has taken the cryptocurrency from a peak of roughly $86,000 in early October to below $65,000 on Monday.

The decline has left Strategy with an estimated $9.6 billion paper loss on its Bitcoin holdings.

Saylor appeared to signal another purchase ahead of the latest announcement.

During the weekend sell-off, he posted Strategy's Bitcoin acquisition tracker chart with the message: "This dip could use a little orange."

The latest weakness in Strategy shares also follows a broader sell-off in crypto-linked stocks.

Strategy's and Coinbase's shares came under pressure on Friday as Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 amid a wider decline in technology stocks.

Investors moved away from riskier assets, while the 10-year US Treasury yield was on track for its largest weekly gain since April 2025.

headline: Why Oracle stock is declining on Monday?
html_content:
Oracle ORCL shares remained under pressure on Monday as investors weighed fresh financing risks surrounding the company's ambitious artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion.

The stock fell around 3.31% at 11:30 AM EDT, trading at $121.24, following a report that data center developer Applied Digital was demanding multi-billion-dollar financial guarantees from Oracle before signing new leases.

The development adds another challenge for Oracle, which has been spending heavily to expand its cloud infrastructure to meet demand from major AI companies.

The broader market also was under pressure with the tech-heavy Nasdaq sliding 1.4% at the time of writing.

Applied Digital demands billions in guarantees

The latest concern centers on Applied Digital's efforts to secure financial backing from its largest data center customers, including Oracle and Meta Platforms.

According to Bloomberg, the developer has asked the companies to provide multi-billion-dollar parent guarantees before finalizing new data center leases.

These guarantees are intended to provide financial backing for the electricity and transmission infrastructure needed to operate massive AI facilities.

Building new AI data centers increasingly requires developers to arrange their own power supply and transmission connections rather than relying entirely on existing utility infrastructure.

Applied Digital President Jason Zhang told Bloomberg that developers often have to build power facilities and transmission lines themselves for new locations.

The demand could create additional financial obligations for Oracle as it expands its AI infrastructure footprint.

Oracle's growing debt adds to pressure

The development comes as investors are already concerned about Oracle's financing requirements.

The company had $125.34 billion in borrowings as of August 31, while its AI infrastructure expansion continues to require substantial capital.

Earlier this month, Oracle announced a $20 billion fundraising through equity and debt offerings.

It raised approximately $10 billion through a share sale and another $10 billion through bond issuance, with interest rates ranging from 7% to 8.65%.

The company has also outlined plans to limit additional capital-market funding for its fiscal 2027-2030 investment cycle to $20 billion, excluding refinancing of existing debt.

Oracle expects capital expenditure to peak during fiscal 2027 and 2028, with free cash flow turning positive in the second half of fiscal 2028.

Nvidia controversy adds to AI sector pressure

Oracle is also facing pressure from a wider reassessment of AI-related investments.

Nvidia's leadership controversy, following the investigation into CEO Jensen Huang and his subsequent resignation, has added uncertainty to an industry already dealing with questions about elevated valuations, financing structures and the returns on massive infrastructure investments.

Investors have become increasingly cautious about companies whose growth depends on continued expansion of AI computing capacity.

Oracle's significant exposure to OpenAI and its debt-funded data center expansion make it particularly sensitive to changes in sentiment toward the AI trade.

Mizuho says buy the dip

Despite the pressure, Mizuho remains constructive on Oracle and has reiterated its Outperform rating.

"We view last week's broad selloff in AI stocks, including ORCL, as a buying opportunity, as we believe investors are overlooking several positive developments," the firm said.

Mizuho argued that Oracle is better positioned than some competitors to withstand potential delays in data center construction. All five of its major data center campuses are already under construction, while four have secured the necessary permits.

The firm also believes stricter permitting requirements could eventually benefit Oracle by limiting the supply of new AI computing capacity.

headline: Dell, HPE stocks fall: why Wall Street is seeing a buying opportunity
html_content:
Dell and HPE stocks stumbled on Monday as tech stocks fell on Monday. The Nasdaq Composite declined 1.63% on Monday.

Dell Technologies shares DELL fell 5.98% to $323.94, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) dropped 3.53% to $46.58.

Both companies have faced mounting pressure in recent weeks amid concerns about weakening personal computer demand, elevated memory costs and uncertainty surrounding artificial intelligence spending.

However, some Wall Street analysts believe strong demand for AI infrastructure and enterprise hardware could help offset weakness in the PC market.

Morgan Stanley sees buying opportunity in Dell, HPE

Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring said the recent decline in hardware stocks could present an opportunity for investors ahead of upcoming earnings reports.

In a research note on Monday, Woodring said Dell, HPE, NetApp and Everpure could benefit from strong enterprise spending and positive earnings revisions.

“We like DELL, HPE, NTAP and P into earnings as we believe recent de-rating vs. robust spending/EPS revisions is too punitive, too early,” Woodring said.

The analyst noted that storage and networking businesses remain relatively strong even as PC demand deteriorates quickly.

He expects Dell to deliver the strongest earnings and guidance among the companies, supported by demand for AI servers and storage.

However, Woodring highlighted several risks that could limit further gains in Dell shares, including its exposure to neocloud companies, a weakening PC market, and elevated margins in traditional servers.

He reduced his price target on Dell to $403 from $511 and cut his HPE target to $64 from $72.

Woodring maintains an Equal Weight rating on Dell and an Overweight rating on HPE.

Citi remains constructive on AI infrastructure demand

Citi analyst Asiya Merchant also identified Dell, HPE and Everpure as preferred stocks heading into their earnings reports.

Merchant said demand for AI infrastructure remains strong, while enterprise customers could increase spending as part of a broader infrastructure refresh cycle.

She noted that concerns about peak AI demand, potential demand pull-forwards and stabilising memory prices have weighed heavily on valuations and share prices.

“We lean constructive on HPE and DELL noting pent-up enterprise infrastructure demand, healthy AI backlogs, operational/supply-chain efficiencies to navigate volatility,” Merchant said.

Merchant also pointed to strong networking demand, improving storage trends and better supply availability as potential tailwinds for HPE.

For Dell, she expects continued support from AI and traditional server spending, alongside improved execution in storage.

Despite her positive outlook, Merchant reduced her Dell price target to $550 from $600 and her HPE target to $80 from $92.

She maintains Buy ratings on both stocks.

Citi also highlighted the potential for improved shareholder returns at HPE, noting management's target of resuming share buybacks in the fiscal fourth quarter, supported by strong free cash flow generation.

Barclays warns of limited AI-driven growth

Not all analysts share the optimistic outlook.

Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded Dell, HPE and NetApp to Equal Weight from Overweight last month.

Long argued that higher memory costs have supported revenue growth but questioned whether hardware companies are experiencing a meaningful AI-driven acceleration in product adoption and business performance.

The broader PC market also remains a concern.

Intel reported a contraction in its PC business during the third quarter, reinforcing worries about weaker demand across the sector.

Dell and HPE are scheduled to report their upcoming earnings on Nov. 24 and Nov. 23, respectively.

Despite their recent declines, both stocks have delivered substantial gains in 2026.

Dell shares had advanced 159% this year as of Monday, while HPE had gained 94%, putting it on track for its best annual performance, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

headline: SCHD yields 2.9% while Treasuries pay more: Is the dividend ETF still worth buying?
html_content:
The Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) has had a strong year and is now trading near its highest level on record. The fund has gained more than 30% so far in 2026, comfortably outperforming both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100. With US Treasury yields also extending their uptrend, is the dividend ETF still worth buying?

US Treasury yields are soaring

Income-focused investors are having a good year as global bond yields continue rising. The ten-year Treasury yield jumped to 5.15%, while the three-month yield rose to 4.23%. 

These yields have jumped as investors predict that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates in the next meeting in December. Indeed, the debate among analysts is whether the bank will hike rates by 0.25% or 0.50%.

Odds of a rate hike have escalated after the recent US macro numbers. A report showed that the US economy expanded by 3.4% last quarter, while the economy added over 165k jobs. Another one showed that the US inflation rate remained at an elevated level. 

As such, these numbers mean that the US economy is doing well, which may help to justify another rate hike. As such, a $10,000 invested in the ten-year Treasuries will generate about $510, while the same amount invested in three-month bill will make about $440 a year. 

Most importantly, corporate bond yields have continued to rise this year. THE ICE Bofa BBB US Corporate Index Effective Yield has jumped to 6.2%, much higher than what the Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF is paying.

The challenge of investing in these assets is that corporate and Treasury bonds offer little room for growth. This is unlike other assets such as stocks, which offer two ways of generating returns: dividends and stock return.

READ MORE: SCHD analysis: Here’s why the Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF is about to soar

SCHD ETF has a lower yield, but better fundamentals

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) has seen its dividend yield fall noticeably over the past few days as its share price has kept climbing. This is because an ETF’s price and its yield move in opposite directions. When the price rises, the yield falls, and when the price drops, the yield rises.

SCHD’s yield has dropped to 2.9%, much lower than other top dividend assets. This means that a $10,000 investment in the fund would generate just $290 in annual dividends. 

On the positive side, SCHD is generating stronger performance than US Treasury and corporate bonds. It has done well because of the ongoing demand from investors who are afraid of the artificial intelligence (AI) bubble. 

Data shows that the fund has had the best year in terms of its inflows and outflows. It has added over $27 billion in assets this year, much higher than other popular funds, including the State Street SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) ETF, which has added over $11.2 billion. It is slightly below what the iShares S&P 500 ETF (IVV), which has added over $33 billion. 

SCHD ETF technicals point to more gains

Technicals suggest that the Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF has more upside to go in the near term. It has jumped above the crucial resistance level of $35.32, its highest point on August 20th this year. The fund then retested that level, completing a break-and-retest pattern.

The ETF has held steady above the 50-day and 100-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA), a sign that bulls are in control. Therefore, the fund will likely continue rising in the near term, with the next target to watch being at $40.

headline: Hang Seng Index in focus ahead of Baidu, Alibaba, Tencent, Lenovo earnings
html_content:
The Hang Seng Index has remained in a correction after falling by over 15% from its highest point this year. This retreat will be put to the test this week as some of the biggest Chinese companies publish their earnings reports. Some of the most notable ones are Baidu, Trip.com, Alibaba, Tencent, and Lenovo Group.

Alibaba Group to publish earnings as stock crashes

Alibaba, one of the biggest companies in China, will be in the spotlight this week as it releases its financial results. BABA was trading at $90.5 in Hong Kong, down by over 50% from its highest point in October last year. It has slumped to its lowest level since June this year.

Alibaba has decoupled from Amazon, a company that uses a similar business model. Its stock has plunged by over 70% from its all-time high, even as Amazon has moved close to its all-time high. 

Alibaba’s performance has been dragged by the rising AI spending that has pushed the management to issue shares. It recently raised $10 billion in a fundraising that diluted its shareholders. Also, the company’s profits have dived in the past few quarters. Its net income dropped by 75% in the second quarter to $1.53 billion. 

Tencent Holdings to release earnings as its stock drops

Tencent Holdings, a top Chinese conglomerate that owns brands like Riot Games, WeChat, Funom, and stakes in Epic Games, Ubisoft, and PDD, has also plunged this year. It was trading at $386, down by over 43% from its highest point in October last year. It has slumped to its lowest level since January last year. 

Like Alibaba, Tencent’s business is being affected by the rising AI investments that have hurt its profits. The last results showed that its revenue rose by 11% in the second quarter to RMB 204.8 billion, while the net profit rose by 9% to RMB 70.6 billion. 

Notably, Tencent’s capital expenditure jumped by 176% to RMB 52.8 billion. The company raised $5.7 billion in debt to continue its AI spending. 

Lenovo Group stock has dropped because of AI jitters

Lenovo Group is another top Hang Seng stock to watch this week as it releases its earnings. These earnings come at a time when the company’s stock has plunged by 53% from its all-time high.

Lenovo has plunged because of the ongoing jitters surrounding the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. Its retreat has mirrored the performance of other popular companies like Dell and HP Enterprise. 

Unlike Alibaba and Tencent, Lenovo Group’s business is doing well, with revenue, profits, and backlog continuing to rise. Its last earnings report showed that its revenue soared to over $26.9 billion, up by 43% from a year earlier. This growth was driven by a 60% increase in its AI business. 

Lenovo’s business is benefiting from the ongoing data center spending that has pushed to a significant increase in demand for its servers and storage products. Based on the recent earnings by its hyperscaler clients and competitors, chances are that Lenovo will publish strong numbers.

The challenge, however, is that there are jitters that the AI bubble is about to burst, which will affect its revenue growth in the future. On the positive side, if these concerns are overblown, then there is a likelihood that the ongoing retreat has made it a good bargain.

Baidu stock has plunged ahead of earnings

Baidu, which is seen as China’s version of Google, has plunged to $74.20 in Hong Kong. It has fallen from the year-to-date high of $160 amid concerns about the AI industry and its impact on its business. 

One of the top concerns about the company is its Kunluxin IPO, which is expected to be delayed to next year. Also, investors are concerned about the impact of AI search on its business. In its recent results, Google said that AI search was more difficult to monetize than traditional search. 

Baidu will publish its earnings report on Monday, and analysts expect it to show that its revenue growth stalled, while AI costs soared.

headline: Meta shares slide over 2% on Monday: here's why
html_content:
Meta Platforms META shares fell about 2.4% on Monday, extending a multiweek decline for the Facebook parent.

The stock has lost roughly 12% over the past month as investors weigh its rising debt load and growing concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

The decline comes amid aggressive borrowing to finance AI investments and mounting legal pressures.

The broader market also remained under pressure, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq slipping more than 2%.

Meta continues to spend big

In early November, Meta completed approximately $25 billion in bond sales, comprising a $15 billion dollar-denominated offering and a €9 billion euro bond sale.

The borrowing comes as Meta ramps up investment in data centers and AI infrastructure, with its 2026 capital expenditure guidance standing at $135 billion to $145 billion.

The latest issuance adds to the company's approximately $84 billion in outstanding debt as of September 30.

The concerns follow Meta's third-quarter results, reported in October.

Revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.60 billion, but free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion as heavy spending continued. A large legal charge also weighed on profits.

Legal risks add to investor concerns

Legal pressures are also playing a part.

Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million, approximately $887 million, over its access to photos, videos and related metadata in the galleries of Android users through a Facebook feature.

The regulator said approximately 20 million users in Italy could be affected. Meta strongly disagreed with the findings and said it would appeal.

Separately, a coalition of nonprofits filed a lawsuit in San Francisco seeking an injunction against Meta and other major AI developers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceX entities.

The complaint argues that rapid AI advancement creates catastrophic risks and seeks restrictions on the development and deployment of more advanced AI models.

The lawsuit adds to growing scrutiny of the AI industry and the potential regulatory challenges facing companies investing heavily in frontier models.

JPMorgan adds Meta to its focus list

Despite the concerns surrounding Meta's spending and legal exposure, Wall Street remains constructive on the company's longer-term growth prospects.

JPMorgan added Meta shares to its focus list last week, citing the potential for AI to strengthen its advertising business and create new revenue opportunities.

“We see continued strong revenue growth for Meta on AI-driven ad improvements, & we are bullish on Muse expansion & monetization potential, along w/the enterprise opportunity for Meta Model API & Muse Code,” the brokerage said.

The assessment suggests that JPMorgan sees opportunities beyond Meta's core advertising business, particularly as it expands its AI products and enterprise offerings.

The broader technology and AI sector also remained under pressure on Monday amid continued fallout from the leadership controversy and resignation at Nvidia.

Uncertainty surrounding the chipmaker has weighed on related stocks as investors reassess AI spending plans and supply-chain risks.

headline: CoreWeave stock falls 6% as Nvidia leadership uncertainty weighs
html_content:
CoreWeave stock CRWV declined 6% on Monday as technology stocks continued to fall on Monday. Nvidia's fall also affected CoreWeave's decline, as Nvidia holds stakes in the neo cloud company.

Fellow neo cloud company Nebius also fell 6.7% in the session after analysts cut the target price on the stock.

CoreWeave shares have come under pressure throughout 2026, falling almost 30% amid concerns about the company's debt levels and substantial capital spending requirements.

However, Nvidia's leadership transition has added another layer of uncertainty for investors, given the chipmaker's financial and strategic relationship with CoreWeave.

Nvidia leadership uncertainty raises concerns for CoreWeave

Nvidia's leadership shock has emerged as a key factor weighing on sentiment towards CoreWeave.

The decline comes days after Nvidia announced the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang and began searching for his successor.

Huang's departure has raised questions about Nvidia's future hardware roadmap and its financing commitments to companies that rely heavily on its GPUs.

CoreWeave's AI cloud business is particularly exposed to these developments because of its dependence on Nvidia hardware.

Investors are also assessing the potential implications of tighter US restrictions on advanced chip exports to China.

Nvidia is expected to report revenue of $109.08 billion and earnings per share of $2.48.

The upcoming results have become an important event for investors as they assess the company's growth outlook following Huang's departure.

Concerns about a potential pullback in Nvidia's investments and expansion plans could also create financing challenges for AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave.

Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges lowered her price target on CoreWeave to $101 from $106 but maintained a Buy rating on the shares.

"We remain Buy rated and adjust our 12-month price target to $101 (from $106) based on 15x EV/EBIT to CoreWeave's SNTM non-GAAP EBIT," the Goldman Sachs analyst said.

Nvidia's financial and commercial ties with CoreWeave

Nvidia has established a significant financial and strategic position in CoreWeave through a series of investments.

The chipmaker first invested in CoreWeave during its 2023 Series B funding round.

It held approximately 6% of the company when CoreWeave went public in 2025.

Nvidia subsequently invested another $2 billion in January 2026, increasing its stake to approximately 9%.

Nvidia had committed more than $40 billion to AI investments in 2026, with Huang playing an active role in those deals.

The relationship extends beyond equity investments.

Nvidia has also committed to purchasing CoreWeave's unsold cloud-computing capacity under a multi-year agreement.

The agreement involves at least $6.3 billion in purchases through April 2032.

These commitments have helped support CoreWeave's business model, but they also highlight the company's dependence on Nvidia's financial and commercial support.

Huang previously defended CoreWeave's financing position

Huang had publicly defended CoreWeave's financial position during its October stock and bond selloff.

At the time, he said CoreWeave did not need "a backstop or a bailout" and argued that its "cost of capital is actually decreasing."

His comments sought to address concerns that CoreWeave's high borrowing costs could eventually force Nvidia to provide additional financial support.

However, Huang's departure has raised questions about whether the same level of strategic and financial support will continue under Nvidia's future leadership.

For CoreWeave investors, the key issues remain the company's ability to finance its substantial infrastructure expansion, manage its debt and maintain access to Nvidia's GPUs.

headline: Here’s why the Bill Holdings stock surging and what next
html_content:
Bill Holdings stock continued its strong rally, reaching its highest point since February this year after a top analyst upgraded the company. It jumped to $58.40, up by 82% from its lowest level this year. This rally may continue as the stock has formed an inverted head-and-shoulders pattern, a common bullish reversal sign.

Bill Holdings jumps as analysts turn bullish

The ongoing Bill Holdings surge happened after William Blair’s Andrew Jeffrey upgraded the company from a Market Perform to Outperform. He cited the company’s attractive risk/reward metric, which he believes has turned more constructive. 

Also, he believes that the company has improving monetization trends, margin expansion trends, and a good customer profile strategy. On the latter, the company is slowly moving to larger small and medium-sized businesses. 

The analyst joins other top Wall Street analysts who have boosted their forecasts for the company. Morgan Stanley’s Keith Weiss recently boosted the target from $60 to $64, while UBS Group’s Taylor McGinnis huked from $60 to $64. 

READ MORE: SCHD yields 2.9% while Treasuries pay more: Is the dividend ETF still worth buying?

Other analysts who hiked their targets after the recent earnings were from Citigroup, TD Cowen, Oppenheimer, and Keefe, Bruyette & Woods. In total, the average estimate among analysts is $59.30, up modestly from $58.67, where it was last month.

The most recent earnings report showed that Bill Holdings’ business did well, with its revenue rising by 13% to $353.8 million. Its core revenue, which is made up of its subscription and transaction fees rose by 14% to $316 million, with the float revenue hitting $37.4 million. Float revenue is made up of interest on funds held for customers. 

The company also made a $60 million profit during the quarter, a big reversal from the $3 million loss it made in the same period last year. This growth happened as the number of companies using the platfom jumped to 475,300, while the total payment volume jumped by 14% to $102 billion.

The management expects that its revenue will experience some modest growth this quarter. Its target is between $353 million and $363 million, representing an 11% annual growth rate at the upper side of the target. Its net income is also expected to be $102 million.

Further, there are signs that the company is highly undervalued, with its forward price-to-earnings ratio of 13.3 being much lower than the sector median of 19. Also, it has an attractive Rule-of-40 metric of 51. A figure above 40 is usually a sign that a company is undervalued.

Bill Holdings stock price technical analysis

Bill stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the Bill stock price has jumped in the past few months, moving from a low of $31.26 in June to the current $57.30. It formed a golden cross pattern in August as the 50-day and 200-day moving averages crossed each other. 

The stock has jumped above the crucial resistance level of $52.40, the highest swing on August 13 this year. Moving above that level confirmed that bulls have prevailed.

The stock has jumped above the Supertrend indicator, which is a bullish sign. It is also attempting to cross the 38.2% Fibonacci Retracement level. Therefore, the stock will likely continue rising as bulls target the 50% retracement level of $65.80. A move above that price will point to more gains towards the 61.8% retracement at $74. On the other hand, a move below the support level of $45 will invalidate the bullish outlook.

headline: Evening digest: Nvidia rules out Huang return, gold and oil prices fall
html_content:
Nvidia's board is reportedly not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, despite growing calls for his reinstatement.

Gold prices fell to their lowest level since October 2025 as a stronger dollar and rising interest rate expectations weighed on bullion.

Oil prices declined more than 2% amid signs of recovering supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

Intel shares dropped as investors filed a lawsuit alleging that executives concealed weakening PC demand ahead of the company's $23 billion share offering.

Nvidia board not considering Jensen Huang's return

Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as chief executive, despite growing calls for his reinstatement, CNBC reported on Monday, citing a person familiar with the matter.

The board is focused on an investigation into Huang's conduct and is not discussing his return, the person said.

Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate whether Huang's conduct compromised national security or company secrets.

Huang resigned last week after 33 years as CEO of the chipmaker.

His departure followed reports about alleged personal relationships, including claims involving an individual linked to an Nvidia customer and alleged contacts with Chinese intelligence.

The Financial Times reported over the weekend that Huang had discussed returning with allies.

However, Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him.

Calls for his reinstatement have gained traction in the technology industry.

An online petition has attracted 180,000 signatures, with support from figures including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

US President Donald Trump also said on Monday that he was open to Huang returning as Nvidia CEO.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's board said on Friday that it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the position.

Gold price falls to lowest level since October 2025

Gold prices declined on Monday, touching their lowest level in more than a year as a stronger US dollar and expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase weighed on bullion.

Spot gold fell 0.4% to $3,864.61 per ounce, after touching $3,830 earlier in the session, its lowest level since October 2025.

US gold futures for December delivery also declined 0.57% to $3,864 per ounce.

Expectations of tighter monetary policy strengthened following recent inflation data.

Traders were pricing in a 96% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase next month, while the probability of a 50-basis-point hike stood at 4%, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

The US dollar traded near its strongest level since April 2025, making gold more expensive for holders of other currencies.

Higher interest rates also increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as bullion.

Investors are awaiting remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the minutes of the central bank's October 27-28 meeting, scheduled for Wednesday.

Other precious metals also declined. Spot silver fell 3.6% to $46.98 per ounce, while platinum dropped 3.2% to $1,448.90 and palladium declined 2.6% to $974.07.

Oil prices fall as Hormuz flows recover

Oil prices dropped more than 3% on Monday as recovering supply flows through the Strait of Hormuz reinforced expectations of a global surplus.

Brent crude futures declined 3.43% to $92.56 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 3.3% to $85.64.

The International Energy Agency expects global oil supply to average 105 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, exceeding projected demand by 1.7 million barrels per day.

The agency had previously forecast a supply deficit.

Goldman Sachs expects Brent crude to average $88 a barrel next year before declining to $78 by December 2027.

However, geopolitical risks remain.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, while six tankers caught fire in similar incidents on Sunday and Monday.

Weakness in Chinese refining activity also pressured prices.

China's refinery throughput in October fell 2% from September and 8.1% year over year, according to official data.

Intel stock falls as shareholder lawsuit adds pressure

Intel shares declined 6.44% on Monday after investors filed a proposed class-action lawsuit alleging that company executives concealed worsening PC demand ahead of its $23 billion share offering in August.

The lawsuit, filed in California on November 13, names CEO Lip-Bu Tan and finance chief David Zinsner. It covers shareholders who purchased Intel stock between July 23 and October 29.

Intel issued approximately 242 million shares at $95 each on August 12, generating $23 billion in gross proceeds and $22.6 billion after expenses.

The plaintiffs allege that management understated the impact of weakening PC demand, excess inventories, and manufacturing constraints.

The legal action follows Intel's 28.6% share-price collapse on October 30, which erased approximately $140 billion from its market value.

The plaintiffs are seeking unspecified damages, rather than repayment of the share offering proceeds.

Intel's third-quarter results showed revenue rising 21% to $16.5 billion, while adjusted earnings reached 52 cents per share.

Its data-centre and AI revenue increased 78% to $7.3 billion.

However, its client computing division generated $8.1 billion, down 5% year over year.

The company also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analyst expectations of approximately $17.1 billion.

Weak PC demand, rising memory prices, and manufacturing constraints continue to complicate Intel's turnaround as the company faces renewed scrutiny over management's disclosures.

headline: Tesla stock falls 2.5% even as company plans $3.3B cybercab expansion
html_content:
Tesla stock TSLA fell 3.4% on Monday as investors assessed reports that the electric vehicle maker is planning a €3 billion ($3.3 billion) investment in its German manufacturing facility to expand Cybercab production.

According to Reuters, Tesla plans to construct an additional production facility at its Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg, with the aim of eventually manufacturing one million Cybercab robotaxis.

The company intends to submit a building permit application before the end of 2026, with construction expected to begin in the first half of 2027. Production could start in 2029.

The proposed expansion would mark a significant step in Tesla's efforts to scale its autonomous driving business beyond the US.

Tesla plans major Cybercab production expansion in Germany

The planned investment would expand operations at Tesla's only vehicle manufacturing facility in Europe.

Opened in 2022, the German factory primarily produces the Model Y SUV, supplying more than 30 markets.

Its existing installed production capacity exceeds 375,000 vehicles.

The facility also manufactures battery cells, battery packs, and electric drivetrains.

Tesla currently employs approximately 12,600 people at the site and plans to add another 2,000 employees to expand battery cell production by the middle of next year.

The proposed Cybercab facility would add another major production operation to the German site.

Tesla's Cybercab is a dedicated robotaxi designed without a steering wheel or pedals.

Production is currently limited to the company's Texas Gigafactory.

The expansion comes as Tesla seeks to increase its presence in the autonomous mobility market.

The company has also indicated plans to wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory by next summer to make room for increased Cybercab manufacturing.

Tesla opens Cybercab sales as robotaxi ambitions grow

Tesla has recently invited select customers to purchase Cybercabs for personal use at an upfront price of $29,990, alongside a monthly autonomous driving subscription costing $299.

The vehicles were previously limited to Tesla's own robotaxi fleet.

During its earnings call last month, the company said it was also looking to supply Cybercabs to fleet customers by the end of 2026.

However, management indicated that the vast majority of the vehicles would remain Tesla-owned.

The expansion plans align with CEO Elon Musk's broader ambition to transform Tesla into an artificial intelligence and robotics company alongside its existing automotive business.

JPMorgan has also become more constructive on Tesla's robotaxi opportunity, while maintaining a Neutral rating on the stock.

"TSLA's recent rapid ramp of its robotaxi fleet and ride-hailing operations, including this weekend's launch of customer Cybercab sales, is starting to present early validation of the company's unique advantage in physical AI, with deep vertical integration across software, manufacturing, and compute," JPMorgan said.

Tesla faces competition in Europe's EV market

The German investment comes as competition in Europe's electric vehicle market intensifies.

Traditional European automakers are facing sluggish demand, high production costs and competition from more affordable Chinese electric vehicle models.

Tesla's Model Y remains a major player in the region.

Nearly 42,000 units were registered in Europe in September, making it the continent's best-selling electric vehicle for the month.

BYD followed with 28,309 vehicle registrations, representing a 111.4% increase from the same period last year.

Tesla's proposed German expansion could strengthen its manufacturing presence in Europe while supporting its longer-term robotaxi ambitions.

However, the project remains at the planning stage, with building permits, construction and the eventual production ramp still ahead.

headline: Is Robinhood stock a buy after the crypto crash and new Kalshi competition fears?
html_content:
Robinhood stock extended its strong sell-off, reaching its lowest level since April 29 as Kalshi extended its business in stock trading. It also plunged as the crypto market continued its strong sell-off. HOOD dropped to a low of $72, down sharply from the September high of $126. 

Robinhood Markets drops amid rising competition from Kalshi

HOOD stock continued its strong sell-off after Kalshi expanded its business to the stock trading industry. The company, which has become the biggest player in the prediction market, has intensified its push into the stock market.

It launched perpetual stock futures earlier this month, and data suggests that the demand is growing. Perpetual stock futures differ from the traditional contracts because they don’t have an expiration date. They are mostly popular in the crypto trading industry.

The company is also working to bring more stock trading on its platform, a move that will challenge Robinhood. Indeed, SimilarWeb data shows that Kalshi’s website traffic has surged in the past few months. It jumped by 42% in October from a month earlier to 27.5 million.

On the other hand, Robinhood’s traffic dropped by 4.2% to 38.2 million. Polymarket, another top prediction platform, had over 38.2 million in visits, up by 58%. Traffic to Polymarket’s US ewebsite jumped by 47% to 5 million. 

Crypto winter is affecting Robinhood’s growth

HOOD stock also plunged because of the ongoing weakness in the crypto industry. The crypto marketweakness accelerated during the weekend, with Bitcoin nearing the important support level of $60,000. Other top coins, including Ethereum, XRP, and Solana all plunged. 

The market capitalization of all coins has dropped from over $3 trillion earlier this year to $2.1 trillion today. This is important for Robinhood because it is one of the biggest players in the crypto trading industry. Its volume and transaction revenue always drops whenever the crypto market is falling.

Indeed, data released earlier this month showed that its platforms handled cryptocurrencies worth $17 billion last month, down from $21.4 billion in September. Its volume stood at over $32.5 billion in the same month last year. 

Therefore, the ongoing crypto market weakness will likely lead to weak revenues in the current quarter. Indeed, its last earnings report showed that its crypto revenue continued falling in the third quarter. 

Analysts expect that Robinhood’s fourth quarter revenue will be under pressure. The average estimate among analysts is that its revenue will come in at $1.52 billion, up by 18% from a year earlier. This revenue growth, while good, is lower than what it has made historically.

Kyro AI data shows that analysts have slashed their targets for HOOD stock. Goldman Sachs’ James Yaro has reduced his target from $128 to $115, while Truist Financial slashed from $125 to $123. Other analysts from banks like UBS and Cantor Fitzgerald have also slashed their targets. 

Robinhood stock price technical analysis

HOOD stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the HOOD stock price has slumped in the past few months from a high of $126 in September to a low of $72. It has already formed a death cross pattern, which happens when the 50-day and 200-day moving averages cross each other. This pattern normally leads to more downside. It has also plunged below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level. 

Therefore, the path of the least resistance for the stock is bearish, with the next key target being at $60. A move above the resistance level of $80 will invalidate the bearish outlook and point to more gains.

headline: Samsung and SK Hynix stocks sink as a 20% chip price shock hits home
html_content:
Samsung Electronics stock fell on Tuesday as SK Hynix pared an early decline, with falling commodity NAND flash prices raising fresh doubts about the sustainability of the memory-chip boom.

Samsung traded 3.64% lower at 191,600 won. SK Hynix fell 1% to 1,119,000 won, after recovering from a sharper opening decline.

Both stocks suffered heavy losses on Monday, with Samsung shedding 4.47% and SK Hynix plunging 7.89%.

The renewed pressure follows a Bank of America warning that some NAND spot prices have dropped roughly 20% since late October, even as demand for memory used in artificial intelligence remains strong.

Samsung, SK Hynix stocks: Why NAND's 20% decline is troubling investors

The correction is concentrated in conventional NAND flash used in smartphones and personal computers, rather than across the entire semiconductor market.

Seoul Economic Daily reported that a 512-gigabit NAND wafer now costs about $14.30, down 32% from the previous quarter. One-terabit products have slipped 19% to $24.90.

Higher component costs are discouraging consumers from replacing devices. Manufacturers are responding by cutting storage specifications and reducing orders, leaving distributors to sell excess stock at discounted prices.

Counterpoint Research expects global smartphone shipments to fall 13.9% this year, while Gartner recorded a 22.4% annual decline in third-quarter PC shipments.

Competition is also intensifying. China's Yangtze Memory Technologies captured 14% of NAND revenue in the second quarter, against 28% for Samsung and 19% for SK Hynix.

Bank of America expects consumer NAND contract prices to fall another 5% to 10% in early 2027. Unlike spot transactions, those contracts govern much of the volume sold directly to major customers.

Meanwhile, broader anxieties about AI spending have unsettled technology shares.

“The risk is fueling concerns that the AI investment cycle and circular financing ecosystem led by Nvidia could lose momentum,” Kiwoom Securities analyst Han Ji-young told Pulse.

Why the two chipmakers face different pressures

Commodity NAND weakness does not necessarily signal the end of exceptionally profitable AI memory sales.

Bank of America still forecasts DRAM price increases of 8% this quarter and 5% in the first quarter of 2027, supported by high-bandwidth memory and server demand.

Both Korean manufacturers reported full operating-hour utilisation at their memory facilities through September, according to regulatory filings.

SK Hynix also reported a sequential NAND average selling-price increase in the mid-20% range last quarter.

Those figures measure company sales over different periods, not today's spot-market transactions.

The companies have distinct AI exposures. SK Hynix relies more heavily on Nvidia's HBM orders, while Samsung is developing business with Google, AMD and other chip designers.

KB Securities estimates Nvidia will account for 35% of Samsung's HBM shipments next year, compared with Macquarie's estimate of 65% for SK Hynix.

The shift could help Samsung “regain its HBM competitiveness and increase its market share”, KB Securities analyst Kim Dong-won told The Korea Times.

Can advanced memory withstand a broader downturn?

The next test is whether weakness in consumer NAND begins spreading into longer-term contracts and enterprise storage.

TrendForce warned on Tuesday that cuts to Chinese cloud companies' 2027 solid-state drive orders could push the wider NAND market into oversupply. It expects contract prices to start declining in the second quarter, earlier than previously forecast.

Still, LS Securities analyst Jung Woo-sung argued in a report cited by Seoul Economic Daily that tight server DRAM supply should limit the risk of a near-term memory glut, even if some data-centre investment is delayed.

The outlook leaves investors balancing two different markets: weakening consumer storage and resilient, higher-value AI memory.

headline: EUR/USD signal: forecast as the US Dollar Index rallies ahead of FOMC minutes
html_content:
The euro is in a strong freefall against the US dollar this week. The EUR/USD pair slumped to its lowest level since April last year, continuing a downward trend that started in September when it peaked at 1.2083. This retreat may continue as the pair targets the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level. 

US dollar strength ahead of FOMC minutes

The ongoing EUR/USD pair retreat is mostly because of the US dollar strength. The US Dollar Index (DXY) jumped to a multi-month high of 103.60, up sharply from the year-to-date low of 95.52. 

This surge has been driven by the rising optimism that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates in the next meeting. Odds that the bank will hike rates have jumped to 99% on Polymarket. 

The only disconnect among analysts is on the size of hikes. Some analysts expect the bank to hike rates by 0.50%, while others expect it to increase by 0.25%. Odds of a 50-basis-point hike increased after Christopher Waller, a top Fed official, hinted that he will support such a big increase if inflation remains steady. Still, most analysts expect the bank to deliver gradual rate hikes of 0.25%. 

The recent macro numbers support the case for a Fed rate hike. A report released earlier this month showed that the economy created 165k jobs last month, higher than the expected 60k. The unemployment rate dropped to 4.1% from the previous 4.2%. Also, the wage growth and the participation rates improved.

And last week, data showed that the country’s inflation rate remained strong last month. The headline consumer price index (CPI) jumped 0.4% in October, while the core CPI jumped 0.3%. These metrics jumped because of elevated energy prices amid the ongoing US-Iran war.

A report coming out later today, Nov. 17, is expected to show that US retail sales continued growing last month. These numbers explain why the US bond yields have continued rising, with the benchmark ten-year yield rising to 5.1% for the first time this year. The Federal Reserve will also publish minutes of the last meeting on Wednesday this week. 

Euro weakness persists

The EUR/USD pair has also slumped because of the ongoing euro weakness. The euro has slumped because of the ongoing challenges in some of the biggest European economies.

A good example of this is in France, where protesters have gone to the streets in the past few months. These protesters have been concerned about the cut in education spending, a situation that has been made possible by the rising public debt. 

Data shows that France’s ten-year yield jumped to 4.95%, its highest level since November 4. It has been in a strong rally after bottoming at 3.22% in February.

Bond yields in other European countries have also been rising. In Italy, the ten-year has jumped 4.46% from the year-to-date low of 3.27%. 

As a result, there are concerns on how further the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates in the next few meetings.

EUR/USD technical analysis

EUR/USD chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the euro has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has slumped from a high of 1.2083 in August to a low of 1.099 this week. Most notably, the pair has slumped below the 50% Fibonacci Retracement level of 1.1135. 

The pair formed a death cross pattern in September as the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). Such a move will confirm the bearish outlook in the near term.

The pair has slumped below the Supertrend and the Ichimoku cloud indicator. Therefore, the next key target to watch will be at 1.0908, the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level.

headline: Will XRP price crash below $0.90 as whale selling pressure intensifies?
html_content:
XRP remains under pressure on Tuesday despite adding 1% to its value as persistent selling activity and deteriorating market indicators continued to weigh on the cryptocurrency

XRP trades around $0.963 after falling to $0.893 on Saturday, revisiting price levels last seen in mid-November 2024.

According to CryptoQuant, XRP is experiencing sell-side dominance, with large whale orders contributing to cautious market conditions.

Technical indicators reinforce the bearish outlook for XRP, which remains significantly below its major moving averages despite entering oversold territory.

XRP faces growing whale selling pressure

On-chain and trading indicators suggest that large market participants remain active as XRP extends its decline.

According to CryptoQuant's summary data, XRP's spot and futures markets are experiencing large whale orders alongside sell-side dominance.

Both markets are also showing elevated trading conditions, indicating heightened activity during the ongoing correction.

The combination of large orders and aggressive selling suggests that market participants remain cautious about XRP's near-term prospects.

Whale activity can influence cryptocurrency prices, particularly during periods of reduced liquidity or heightened volatility.

CryptoQuant's indicators suggest that selling activity continues to outweigh buying demand in XRP's spot and derivatives markets.

XRP revisits November 2024 levels after falling to $0.893

XRP's latest correction has erased a substantial portion of the gains accumulated since November 2024. The cryptocurrency fell to $0.893 on Saturday before recovering modestly to trade around $0.963 on Tuesday.

The decline brought XRP back to price levels last seen in mid-November 2024, indicating the extent of the recent downturn.

Despite the slight recovery from its weekend low, XRP remains under considerable technical pressure. The cryptocurrency continues to trade below its major daily Exponential Moving Averages. The 50-day EMA stands around $1.217, while the 100-day EMA is positioned near $1.261.

Meanwhile, the 200-day EMA sits at approximately $1.325. These moving averages form significant resistance above the current market price, reinforcing the bearish near-term structure.

Trading below all three indicators suggests that sellers remain in control across multiple timeframes. The distance between XRP's current price and its major moving averages also indicates that a sustained recovery would require substantial buying momentum.

For now, the recent rebound from $0.893 has not been sufficient to reverse the broader downtrend.

Although XRP's price structure remains bearish, momentum indicators suggest that selling pressure may be becoming overstretched.

The daily Relative Strength Index stands near 27, placing the cryptocurrency in oversold territory. Meanwhile, XRP's Moving Average Convergence Divergence indicator remains below zero.

The negative MACD reading suggests that bearish momentum continues to dominate despite the possibility of a short-term rebound.

XRP's recent low at $0.893 represents an important downside reference as traders assess whether the cryptocurrency can stabilize.

With XRP trading around $0.963, the market has recovered approximately 7% from Saturday's low.

However, the rebound has not yet established a clear bullish reversal. A successful defense of $0.893 could encourage further consolidation and potentially support a temporary recovery toward $1.

The psychological $1 level represents the first major resistance barrier. Reclaiming this threshold would be an important early step toward improving short-term market sentiment.

However, a sustained breakdown below $0.893 would weaken XRP's technical outlook further. Such a move could expose the cryptocurrency to additional selling pressure, particularly if whale activity remains elevated and spot demand continues to deteriorate.

On the upside, a sustained move above $1 would suggest that short-term buying momentum is improving.

However, XRP would still face resistance around $1.160, a horizontal level that could limit further gains. Beyond this barrier, the 50-day EMA near $1.217 represents another important technical obstacle.

The 100-day EMA at $1.261 and the horizontal resistance around $1.300 form a broader resistance zone.

A decisive breakout above these levels would provide stronger evidence that XRP's bearish momentum is beginning to weaken.

Further resistance stands at the 200-day EMA near $1.325, followed by the higher horizontal barrier around $1.540.

headline: Why is Baidu stock crashing to a five-year low despite 94% AI cloud growth?
html_content:
Baidu stock tumbled to its lowest level in more than five years on Tuesday as a steep decline in advertising revenue overshadowed rapid growth in the Chinese technology company's artificial intelligence cloud business.

The Hong Kong-listed stock fell 5.45% to HK$71.15, after touching HK$70.25 during the session, according to Investing.com. The Hang Seng Index declined 2.60%.

The sell-off followed Monday's third-quarter results, which showed online marketing revenue falling 22% even as AI cloud infrastructure sales surged 94%.

A 22% advertising slump exposes Baidu's weakness

Baidu reported quarterly revenue of 30.81 billion yuan ($4.6 billion), down around 1% from a year earlier, as its core advertising business remained under pressure.

Online marketing revenue fell to 11.9 billion yuan from 15.3 billion yuan a year earlier. The contraction was deeper than the 19% decline reported in the second quarter.

Weak consumer spending in China has encouraged advertisers to restrain budgets, while rival internet platforms compete for marketing expenditure.

Baidu's own shift towards AI-powered search is also complicating the picture. New features may increase engagement, but they change how advertisements appear and how search traffic generates revenue.

Management has acknowledged that improving monetisation will take time, with user experience taking priority over immediate advertising returns.

The latest figure also missed Citi Research's forecast of 12.09 billion yuan for core advertising.

That matters because advertising historically helped finance Baidu's investment in newer technology. Its continued decline makes the company's transition more expensive and financially uncertain.

AI-native marketing revenue also fell 15%, suggesting the newer advertising formats are not yet compensating for losses.

Baidu stock: AI cloud growth offers promise but not yet relief

AI cloud infrastructure revenue jumped 94% to 8.2 billion yuan in the September quarter, while GPU cloud sales grew 191%.

Across Baidu's broader AI-powered business, revenue increased 37% to 13.2 billion yuan. The segment represented 53% of Baidu General Business revenue, up from 39% a year earlier.

Those gains demonstrate strong demand for computing infrastructure, although developing and operating AI systems requires substantial investment.

Baidu's adjusted operating margin was approximately 6%, and higher capital expenditure contributed to a free cash outflow of 4.6 billion yuan.

Operating cash flow remained positive at 2.8 billion yuan, underscoring the distinction between operating performance and spending.

Still, the brokerage's analyst Julia Pan noted that "AI cloud infra profit and margin improved both yoy and qoq."

Longer customer contracts and greater prepayments have also improved the economics of its cloud infrastructure, offering more visibility over returns.

The distinction is important, as cloud profitability is improving, but that progress has yet to reverse the pressure on earnings across the wider company.

Can Baidu stock recover from its five-year low?

The share-price collapse has sharpened disagreement over what Baidu's AI operations are worth.

UOB Kay Hian maintained a Buy recommendation on Tuesday but lowered its Hong Kong-listed share target to HK$100 from HK$136, reflecting more cautious expectations.

Morgan Stanley analyst Gary Yu retained a Hold-equivalent rating on Baidu's US-listed shares, with a reported $130 price target.

Competition from Alibaba and emerging AI developers adds another challenge.

Baidu recently previewed its ERNIE 5.5 Flash model, but stronger products will need to translate into paying customers and durable profits.

Further advertising weakness and heavy investment could prolong the sell-off. Stronger cloud margins, better cash generation and improved AI search monetisation could support a recovery.

headline: Brent crude price analysis: will oil crash below $90 as supply glut grows?
html_content:
Oil prices fell for a second consecutive session on Tuesday as recovering Middle East exports and weakening demand pushed Brent crude closer to $90 a barrel, despite continued threats to shipping around the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent futures declined 0.8% to $91.66 a barrel at 04:30 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate slipped 0.9% to $84.99.

The latest losses followed Monday's 3.6% slump, when Brent settled at $92.44.

The sell-off marks a striking reversal from the shortage fears that dominated trading during the US-Iran conflict.

Recovering oil supplies put Brent under pressure

The IEA expects global oil production to exceed demand by about 1.7 million barrels a day during the fourth quarter, reversing its earlier forecast of a deficit.

October supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day to 105.4 million as more Gulf barrels reached international markets.

Observed inventories increased by 52 million barrels, the first monthly build since June, while oil stored at sea climbed by 86 million barrels.

Demand is offering little resistance. Chinese refinery throughput fell 8.1% from a year earlier in October and slipped 2% from September, reinforcing doubts about consumption in one of the world's biggest oil markets.

The IEA expects global oil demand to fall by 2.7 million barrels a day in 2026 before rebounding next year.

"The geopolitical risk premium from the US-Iran conflict has not disappeared, but it is clearly taking a back seat for now," Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, told Reuters.

The issue is not that worldwide energy demand has suddenly collapsed. Supply routes are recovering faster than consumption, changing the balance that previously supported prices.

Why Middle East tensions are no longer lifting oil prices

The prospect of surplus crude has not made the Gulf safe. Tanker attacks and uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz continue to threaten shipments, while traders remain alert to further disruptions.

ANZ analysts said traffic through the strait was still only 49% of its pre-war level. Alternative routes have helped maintain exports but remain vulnerable to logistical problems and attacks.

Meanwhile, US Strategic Petroleum Reserve holdings have fallen to 276.4 million barrels, their lowest since August 1982. That leaves less emergency protection against another prolonged interruption to supplies.

The IEA also warned that global inventories remain 462 million barrels below levels at the start of the war. Diesel supplies are particularly tight, even as the overall crude balance improves.

Those shortages could bring buyers back quickly if regional tensions escalate. However, for now, the market appears more concerned about barrels returning than barrels potentially being lost.

Will Brent crude fall below $90 and head towards $85?

Religare Broking's Ajit Mishra told Moneycontrol that Brent could test $90-$92, with prices likely to remain "volatile with a downward bias". His forecast preceded Tuesday's decline.

Technical analysis from FXEmpire identifies $87.60 as a possible short-term support level.

A sustained move below $90 could therefore expose the $85-$87 area, while stronger selling might eventually bring $80-$82 into view.

But a recovery towards $95-$96 remains possible if another disruption to Gulf shipping restores the geopolitical premium.

"For 2027, we again expect a contest between high supply disruption risk and increasing market adaptation," Goldman Sachs analysts including Daan Struyven wrote, according to Bloomberg.

The bank forecasts Brent averaging $88 next year and easing towards $78 by December 2027, not immediately.

headline: Nvidia stock faces a $300 billion earnings gamble as options signal 8% swing
html_content:
Nvidia stock (NASDAQ: NVDA) face a potentially turbulent earnings reaction on Tuesday, with options traders pricing an 8% move in either direction as investors assess the chipmaker’s prospects following Jensen Huang’s resignation.

At Nvidia’s roughly $3.77 trillion valuation, such a move would add or erase about $300 billion in market value. It is a measure of expected volatility, not a prediction that shares will fall.

The stock closed Monday at $156.14, down 4.12%, extending a sell-off ahead of the company’s first results since its founder stepped down as chief executive.

Nvidia earnings: An unusually large swing takes shape

Cboe research published on Monday showed that Nvidia options implied a one-day post-earnings move of approximately 8%, above the average 4.8% movement recorded after its previous four quarterly reports.

“Options are implying a one-day move of 8% on earnings,” Mandy Xu, Cboe’s head of derivatives market intelligence, wrote in the exchange operator’s research.

The positioning also signals growing caution among smaller traders.

Purchases of bearish put options accounted for 32% of retail opening trades on Cboe exchanges last Thursday, compared with a year-to-date average of 21%.

Puts typically gain value when the underlying stock falls, although investors also use them to hedge existing positions.

The figures therefore suggest increased defensive demand, not a unanimous bet against Nvidia.

An 8% change from Monday’s close would place the shares near $143.65 or $168.63. Those figures illustrate the scale of the implied move, rather than technical targets.

Why strong earnings may not rescue Nvidia stock

Analysts surveyed by LSEG expect Nvidia to report approximately $109.08 billion in quarterly revenue and adjusted earnings of $2.47 per share.

The company previously guided for revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, and gross margins around 74%. Its preceding quarter generated $96.2 billion in sales, including $89 billion from data centres.

Investors will look beyond whether Nvidia exceeds those forecasts.

They want evidence that cloud providers can finance their computing projects without slowing orders, and that rising component costs will not undermine profit margins.

“We see investor willingness to invest in AI as a bigger risk to the buildout trajectory than anything Nvidia can control,” Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore said, according to TipRanks.

Moore maintained his Buy rating but cut his price target to $267 from $300, citing leadership uncertainty and regulatory risks.

Existing supply commitments may provide near-term protection. New projects, however, depend on customers securing capital and earning returns from AI services.

Nvidia earnings options trading: Leadership uncertainty raises the stakes

Huang’s departure last week has complicated a critical earnings announcement. Finance chief Colette Kress is acting as interim chief executive while Nvidia seeks a permanent replacement.

Nvidia's quarterly figures are scheduled for release at around 4:20 pm Eastern, followed by a scheduled 5 pm conference call.

Her challenge is to demonstrate continuity across Nvidia’s product roadmap, major customer relationships and financing arrangements.

Morningstar analyst Brian Colello told Reuters that investors would want “early insights on what Nvidia will do in the interim”, alongside updates on customers and partnerships.

Questions could also focus on the Vera Rubin platform, export restrictions and whether Nvidia can sustain its ambitious growth outlook.

That call could matter as much as the profit numbers, particularly if executives offer little meaningful detail about succession.

A strong report and credible guidance could restore confidence after Monday’s slide. Weak margins, softer forecasts or unanswered leadership questions could deepen the decline.

headline: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness in crisis as top portfolio stocks plunge
html_content:
Leopold Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness hedge fund, came under renewed pressure in October and early this month as most of the companies in its portfolio plunged amid the ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) rout. 

Situational Awareness made AI bets again after coming close to collapse

Leopold Aschenbrenner’s AI-themed hedge fund, has been under pressure this year. After strong returns earlier this year, it nearly collapsed a few months ago as its biggest investments tumbled. These investments include companies like SK Hynix and Samsung.

The fund experienced big losses and had to sell most of its portfolio companies to Citadel Securities at a loss.

Now, however, signs suggest the crisis accelerated in October as its biggest companies plunged. Its recent 13F filing shows that he invested in those same AI companies in October, a sign that he is convinced that it will bounce back.

The hedge fund invested in SharonAI, a top Australian data center company whose stock has plunged in the past few months. SHAZ dropped to $20.13 on Monday, its lowest level since March 11, and much lower than the all-time high of $97. It dropped by 58% in October and is down by 11% this month.

The company also invested in Bloom Energy, one of the top bets in the AI space. Bloom offers energy to data center companies. Its stock has tumbled to $177 from the year-to-date high of $350. This retreat continued amid the ongoing challenges at Oracle’s Project Jupiter, which is facing delays in New Mexico.

Situational Awareness also had calls on Nebius Group in October. Nebius, a top neocloud that counts Meta Platforms and Microsoft as clients, has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It dropped to $107, much lower than the all-time high of $301. Most recently, it plunged after the management lowered its guidance.

Leopold Aschenbrenner also invested in SanDisk, a top memory company that was the best-performing stock in the S&P 500 Index earlier this year. It has since reversed those gains and dropped to $809. This retreat will be in focus this week as the company conducts its stock split. 

The other companies in its portfolio are Cleanspark, Fermi, Bitdeer, and IREN. It also invested in the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM).

Most AI stocks have plunged amid rising risks

American investors have sold their AI stocks in the past few months. For example, the DRAM ETF has suffered substantial outflows in this period.

The ongoing sell-off happened as risks in the market rose. One of the risks is that the Federal Reserve has maintained a hawkish tone in the past few months. It hiked rates in September, and analysts expect that it will hike again in December. These fears have pushed US bond yields higher, with the ten-year crossing the crucial resistance of 5%.

AI companies are also at risk after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia last week. The board was forced to push him out because of his affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy known as Alice Huang. He also had affairs with his employees. 

His resignation is important because he has backed some of the companies in Situational Awareness’ portfolio, like IREN and Nebius. He was also viewed as the central banker of the AI space. 

Further, there are warnings that the AI bubble will burst soon. Some of the loudest warnings have come from executives like Citadel’s Ken Griffin and Bridgewater Associates’ Ray Dalio. One of the arguments for the AI bubble is that it resembles other bubbles that burst, including cannabis, dot-com, crypto, and electric vehicles. If it bursts, some of these companies will be the most affected.
