headline: Cathie Wood dumps $85M in Nvidia stock ahead of earnings to buy this instead
html_content:
Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest sold nearly $85 million worth of Nvidia stock (NASDAQ: NVDA) on Monday while buying about $52 million of SpaceX stock (NASDAQ: SPCX), a striking change in positioning ahead of the chipmaker’s quarterly earnings.

ARK sold 543,092 Nvidia shares across two exchange-traded funds and purchased 378,515 SpaceX shares, according to daily trading disclosures.

The transactions came as Nvidia fell 4.12% to $156.14 amid uncertainty following Jensen Huang’s resignation. Meanwhile, SpaceX had just completed a milestone in its Starship programme..

Why ARK cut Nvidia stock ahead of earnings

Most of ARK’s Nvidia disposals came from its flagship ARK Innovation ETF, which sold 501,733 shares. The remaining shares were sold through the ARK Next Generation Internet ETF.

The reduction followed an aggressive expansion of ARK’s Nvidia position during the third quarter. Its holdings rose about 85% to 2.56 million shares at the end of September.

Wood has not abandoned the chipmaker. ARKK still held roughly $367 million in Nvidia stock following Monday’s trades, according to portfolio data.

ARK’s retained stake leaves exposure if Tuesday’s earnings surprise investors.

The timing nevertheless stands out. Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, its first financial update since Huang left the chief executive role last week.

Finance chief Colette Kress is leading the business on an interim basis, with investors seeking clarity about the company’s strategy, major customers and financing commitments.

Morningstar analyst Brian Colello told Reuters that reassurance about Nvidia’s business and management changes was “probably the most important piece” of the earnings briefing.

The share sale could reflect portfolio rebalancing or a desire to reduce short-term volatility rather than a verdict on Nvidia’s long-term prospects.

SpaceX stock offers a different growth opportunity

ARK’s SpaceX purchases followed Saturday’s successful recovery of the Starship upper stage, which was caught by mechanical arms at the company’s Texas launch tower.

The spacecraft completed 14 orbits during a flight lasting more than 22 hours and deployed 26 Starlink satellites. However, its Super Heavy booster was not recovered after an aborted landing attempt.

The partial success matters commercially. Recovering and eventually reusing both stages could lower launch costs, increase flight frequency and support expansion of SpaceX’s satellite internet network.

Bank of America analyst Ronald Epstein said the achievement was “a huge step forward for the broader business”, according to Benzinga. He retained a Buy rating and a $275 price target.

Still, Starship’s heat shield needs further work, and neither stage has yet demonstrated the rapid, routine reuse central to Musk’s plans.

SpaceX closed Monday at $137.36, down 1.26%, showing that even a major engineering achievement has not shielded the stock from wider market caution.

Can Nvidia stock still reward patient investors?

Wall Street expects Nvidia to report around $109 billion in quarterly revenue and adjusted earnings of $2.47 a share.

Investors will scrutinise its outlook for AI infrastructure spending, profit margins and the succession process. Strong results alone may not settle worries about financing commitments or leadership stability.

UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri described Nvidia’s retreat as “an attractive buying opportunity”, according to Yahoo Finance, although he cautioned that investors might need patience while management uncertainty clears.

He expects Nvidia to exceed revenue forecasts by $3 billion to $4 billion and maintained his Buy rating.

headline: Bitcoin's $62,000 bottom may be an illusion: analysts sound the alarm
html_content:
Bitcoin (BTC) continued to struggle on Tuesday, trading around $64,270 after falling to reclaim the $65,000 level on Monday.

The cryptocurrency is down by less than 1%, but could extend its bearish run after losing 24% of its value since early October.

However, analysts are optimistic that the bottom is near, despite sellers still in control of the market. 

Bitcoin ETF outflows persist

Institutional demand for Bitcoin continued to deteriorate on Monday as US spot ETFs recorded another substantial round of withdrawals.

According to SoSoValue, spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $68.51 million on Monday. This latest development comes after the funds lost $2.35 billion over the last two weeks. 

Spot Bitcoin ETFs have become an important investment channel for institutions and traditional investors seeking exposure to the cryptocurrency.

Consequently, sustained withdrawals can contribute to selling pressure and weaken broader market confidence.

Despite Bitcoin’s weak price action, analysts are optimistic that a bottom is near. In an email to Invezz, Vik Sharma, CEO at Cake Wallet, noted that the $62,000 hit on Saturday looks less like a floor than a pause,

“Six down weeks with ETF outflows mean sellers are setting the price, and liquidations do the rest of the damage quickly. Strategy buying through it says institutions treat this as accumulation, not an exit, but one balance sheet buying does not offset passive money leaving,” Sharma added.

Bitcoin lost the $68,000 support level over the weekend.

According to Mitchell Askew, Head of Blockware Intelligence at Blockware, this loss means that Bitcoin could trade range-bound between $60,000 and $70,000 to close out the remainder of the year.

Widespread macro uncertainty around inflation and interest rate policy, coupled with the political uncertainty of the lame duck period, leaves little room for potential short-term bullish catalysts, even as Bitcoin enters 'oversold' RSI territory for the third time in 2026 (where both previous instances proved to be local lows). That being said, with Bitcoin reaching its power law floor price, this is an incredible opportunity for long-term investors to stack Bitcoin at highly discounted prices, and dip-buying opportunities like this only show up every four years.

Head of Blockware Intelligence at Blockware
Mitchell Askew

Bitcoin technical outlook: Bitcoin remains below its 200-week SMA

Bitcoin’s technical structure hasn’t changed as it remains weak on the weekly and daily timeframes. 

The cryptocurrency opened the new weekly candle on Monday below its 200-week Simple Moving Average (SMA), currently positioned around $68,194.

This resistance holds as Bitcoin has failed to rally past the $65,000 level over the last 24 hours. 

If selling pressure persists, Bitcoin could extend its decline toward the psychological $60,000 support level.

The technical indicators on the daily chart also remain extremely bearish. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands near 23, indicating that Bitcoin is currently in the oversold territory.

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) histogram also remains within the negative region, adding further bearish confluence to BTC/USD. 

Together, these indicators suggest that Bitcoin's broader downtrend has not yet reversed.

However, a recovery above $65,616 could allow buyers to challenge the 200-week SMA near $68,194. Reclaiming these levels would represent an early improvement in Bitcoin's technical structure.

In the event of an extended rally, Bitcoin could encounter further resistance at the 200-day EMA of $75,946, while the 100-day EMA is positioned near $76,470.

Bitcoin's next major move will likely depend on whether buyers can defend recent lows and reclaim previously broken resistance levels.

The bulls would look to defend the nearest support level (last week’s low) at $62,006. 

A sustained breakdown below this level could encourage further selling and expose BTC to the psychological $60,000 mark.

For now, Bitcoin's near-term outlook remains bearish while BTC trades below $65,616 and the 200-week SMA at $68,194.

headline: SanDisk stock faces 8-for-1 split after 65% crash, but a bigger risk looms
html_content:
SanDisk stock (NASDAQ: SNDK) are heading towards an eight-for-one stock split after losing nearly 65% of their value since June, as investors question whether the memory-chip maker can sustain its profit margins.

The stock closed Monday at $809.11, down 8.58%, against a record closing price of $2,335 on 25 June.

The sell-off contrasts with SanDisk’s latest results, which showed quarterly revenue surging 378% and gross margins reaching 85%.

The split takes effect this week, but the bigger concern is that SanDisk’s earnings boom has depended heavily on rising NAND flash prices.

Why the SanDisk stock split will not reverse slide

SanDisk will issue seven additional shares for each existing share after Thursday’s market close, with split-adjusted trading beginning on Friday, 20 November.

The change makes each share cheaper to purchase without altering the value of an investor’s holding or the company’s market capitalisation.

It cannot improve future cash flow or reduce exposure to the memory industry’s recurring pricing cycles.

At Monday’s closing price, an eight-for-one adjustment would produce an indicative share price of about $101.14. Someone holding one share would instead hold eight, with the same combined value before market movements.

SanDisk announced the split on 29 October, partly to make shares more accessible through employee ownership programmes.

But the lower sticker price cannot resolve uncertainty surrounding memory-chip demand, AI infrastructure spending or the durability of high selling prices.

Daniel Sparks, an investor and chief investment officer at Sparks Capital Management, wrote in The Motley Fool that concerns about the decline made sense for a business whose recent growth had come “almost entirely from price”.

SanDisk stock: A 378% revenue surge conceals a pricing problem

SanDisk generated $11.03 billion in revenue during its fiscal first quarter, compared with $2.31 billion a year earlier.

Yet the volume of storage shipped, measured in exabytes, increased by almost 10%, according to the company’s regulatory filing.

Data-centre revenue reached $4.8 billion, up 61% sequentially, reflecting demand for storage infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence.

In its Edge division, revenue per gigabyte jumped more than 450% even as shipment volumes fell 20%. Rising prices therefore accounted for much of the dramatic sales growth.

Gross margins climbed to 85% from 29.8% a year earlier. Such profitability is attractive, but also exposes SanDisk to sharp reversals if manufacturers expand capacity or customers push back against prices.

There is a counterargument. SanDisk’s longer-term customer agreements create clearer revenue commitments, with $88.9 billion in remaining performance obligations reported at the quarter’s end.

Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani told MarketWatch that investors remain “overly focused on how long NAND pricing can stay elevated” rather than appreciating structural changes, including supply discipline and multiyear contracts. He maintained an Outperform rating and $2,500 price target.

Can NAND prices hold up through the next cycle?

SanDisk expects second-quarter revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion, implying roughly 12% sequential growth at the midpoint, slower than the previous quarter’s 23% expansion.

Its non-GAAP gross-margin forecast of 84.5% to 85.5% nevertheless suggests management expects pricing conditions to remain favourable near term.

Manufacturing partner Kioxia anticipates more moderate NAND price increases this quarter, while forecasting tight supply through 2027.

Morningstar analyst William Kerwin is less convinced the gains can last. “We still expect a severe downcycle after the peak,” he wrote, cutting SanDisk’s fair value estimate to $870 from $1,000.

Morningstar expects additional industry capacity to pressure prices from 2029, with weakness continuing through 2031. If prices turn sooner, profits could fall even as physical shipment volumes remain stable.

headline: Here's how Donald Trump traded Nvidia stock in his second term
html_content:
US President Donald Trump's investment accounts sold as much as $1 million in Nvidia NVDA stock just days after he was reportedly informed that then-CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of working for Beijing.

The sale took place on May 18, just five days after Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly briefed Trump about intelligence concerning Alice Huang, according to a CNBC analysis of financial disclosures.

Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, has been identified as a Chinese government agent by the US intelligence.

Trump has denied receiving the briefing, saying he had not heard of it and did not know whether Alice Huang was a spy.

Trump's trades in Nvidia stock attracted renewed attention following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO last week amid the controversy and additional reports of relationships with company employees.

Trump's reported Nvidia stock trades

CNBC's review found that Trump's investment accounts executed at least 103 Nvidia transactions since he returned to the White House in 2024.

The combined value of purchases and sales ranged from $27 million to $97.5 million, based on the trading ranges disclosed in financial filings.

In addition to the May 18 sale, valued between $500,001 and $1 million, the accounts purchased smaller positions in the days immediately before and after the transaction.

During the first eight months of 2026, the accounts also conducted 38 Nvidia transactions valued between $9.4 million and $28.3 million.

CNBC's analysis further showed that the president's accounts made Nvidia stock purchases valued at up to $1.6 million and sales of up to $1 million in August.

The White House has maintained that independent portfolio advisers manage Trump's investments without his input.

Representatives of the Trump Organization have also emphasized that the arrangement is designed to avoid even the "appearance of conflicts of interest."

Critics, however, remain unconvinced.

The financial disclosures do not establish that Trump directed the specific trades or that his advisers had access to classified intelligence concerning Alice Huang.

Trump continues to back Jensen Huang

Despite the controversy, Trump has publicly defended Jensen Huang and said he would not object to the former Nvidia chief returning as CEO.

He has also described Huang as an honorable person.

However, Huang's return appears unlikely following his resignation.

Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation, while the controversy has intensified congressional scrutiny and raised questions about potential national security implications.

CNBC and Reuters have reported that the board is unlikely to bring Huang back as CEO.

The developments have also attracted attention because of the previously close relationship between Trump and Huang.

The Nvidia chief emerged as an important Silicon Valley ally and informal AI adviser to the president.

He accompanied Trump on a state visit to China in May and received high-profile recognition, including a national science medal.

Nvidia's stock has been hit hard amid the controversy, falling more than 28% in last one month. The stock was down 0.6% in premarket trading on Tuesday.

headline: Ethereum price crashes below $1,800 as Tom Lee makes an $11B bet
html_content:
Ethereum (ETH) treasury company BitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) continued accumulating the cryptocurrency last week despite a prolonged market downturn that has pushed ETH below $1,800.

The company purchased an additional 7,653 ETH, bringing its total holdings to approximately 6.077 million tokens as it moves closer to its target of controlling 5% of Ethereum's circulating supply.

Meanwhile, Ethereum's technical outlook remains uncertain, with the cryptocurrency facing resistance near $1,827 despite signs of deeply oversold conditions.

BitMine expands Ethereum holdings to 6.077 million ETH

BitMine Immersion Technologies continued its Ethereum accumulation strategy last week, adding 7,653 ETH to its corporate treasury.

According to the company's Monday announcement, the purchase increased its total holdings to approximately 6.077 million ETH.

The Connecticut-based firm has maintained an aggressive accumulation strategy despite Ethereum's recent price decline.

BitMine said its holdings place it just 0.03% away from its target of acquiring 5% of Ethereum's circulating supply.

ETH has declined approximately 28% over the past two weeks, raising concerns about whether the cryptocurrency has established a sustainable price floor.

Nevertheless, BitMine's continued accumulation indicates that the company views the downturn as consistent with its longer-term investment strategy.

BitMine Chairman Thomas Lee attributed part of Ethereum's recent weakness to external developments affecting broader financial markets.

In a Monday statement, Lee suggested that developments involving Nvidia and the anticipated Anthropic IPO could be contributing to selling pressure.

According to Lee, investors may be liquidating cryptocurrency holdings to raise cash ahead of the expected equity offering.

He also pointed to potential margin-related selling, particularly among investors in Asian markets, following recent developments involving Nvidia.

Lee compared Ethereum's current correction with a previous decline that he associated with the period leading up to SpaceX's IPO.

He noted that Ethereum has followed a similar pattern recently, declining 39% over the past eight weeks and 28% over the past two weeks.

Institutional demand for Ethereum has continued to weaken as US spot ETFs experience sustained withdrawals.

According to SoSoValue, spot Ethereum ETFs recorded an outflow of $8.31 million on Monday. This comes after the funds lost $398.85 million last week.

The withdrawals marked the seventh consecutive week of negative net flows, highlighting persistent caution among investors.

If ETF outflows continue, Ethereum could face additional pressure as investors reduce exposure to cryptocurrency markets.

Conversely, a sustained return to positive net inflows would provide stronger evidence that institutional sentiment is improving.

Ethereum price forecast: ETH must reclaim $1,827 to target $1,971

Ethereum's immediate technical outlook depends on whether buyers can establish a sustained recovery above $1,827.

The cryptocurrency recently rebounded from the $1,714 support region over the weekend but has struggled to maintain upward momentum. At press time, ETH is trading at $1,792.

The $1,827 horizontal level now represents an important resistance barrier. A sustained daily close above this level could encourage buyers to target the next resistance around $1,971.

Beyond this barrier, the 20-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) near $2,097 represents another significant technical obstacle.

The $2,101 horizontal resistance level sits just above the moving average, creating a concentrated resistance zone.

A decisive breakout above this area would provide stronger evidence that Ethereum's short-term bearish momentum is beginning to weaken.

However, the cryptocurrency would need substantial buying demand to overcome these levels, particularly given the continued ETF withdrawals and broader market uncertainty.

On the downside, $1,714 remains the most important immediate support. A sustained breakdown below this level could expose Ethereum to further losses toward $1,600.

If selling pressure intensifies, the next significant downside target stands near $1,523.

These levels could become increasingly important if institutional demand remains weak and the broader cryptocurrency market continues to decline.

Ethereum's momentum indicators suggest that the recent correction may be becoming overstretched.

The 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands near 24, placing ETH in oversold territory.

Meanwhile, the Stochastic Oscillator has fallen to approximately 11, reinforcing the view that selling pressure has become unusually strong.

Both indicators suggest that a temporary recovery is possible if sellers begin taking profits or buyers return near support. However, oversold conditions do not guarantee that a market bottom has formed.

headline: US stock futures fall ahead of Nvidia earnings: 5 things to know before market opens
html_content:
US stock futures declined on Tuesday as investors prepared for Nvidia's closely watched earnings and fresh consumer-spending figures following a sharp technology-led sell-off.

Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were each down approximately 0.4%.

The retreat followed Monday's losses, when the S&P 500 fell 1.92%, the Nasdaq Composite sank 2.49% and the Dow dropped 1.41%.

Washington's tighter restrictions on access to advanced AI chips also unsettled overseas markets.

Investors face a busy calendar of corporate results, economic figures and Federal Reserve developments as they assess whether Wall Street's latest decline will deepen.

5 things to know before Wall Street opens

1. Nvidia faces a $109 billion earnings test

Nvidia reports after Tuesday's closing bell, with analysts expecting quarterly revenue of approximately $109 billion. Its shares fell 4.12% to $156.14 on Monday, extending a sell-off following Jensen Huang's resignation.

Interim chief executive Colette Kress faces questions about customer demand, export restrictions and the company's product roadmap.

S&P Global analyst Melissa Otto estimates data-centre revenue will reach about $101.8 billion, underscoring Nvidia's dependence on AI infrastructure spending.

2.US retail sales put consumers under scrutiny

October retail sales figures arrive at 8:30 am ET, with economists forecasting a 0.2% monthly increase after September's 0.8% gain.

Excluding automobiles, sales are expected to climb 0.4%. A disappointing reading could suggest inflation and elevated borrowing costs are beginning to constrain household spending.

Stronger numbers might support growth expectations but also reinforce bets on further Federal Reserve tightening.

3.New AI-chip restrictions deepen the global sell-off

The US Commerce Department has introduced rules designed to prevent restricted buyers from accessing advanced American computing through data centres in third countries.

The measures add uncertainty for semiconductor manufacturers and cloud providers.

Europe's STOXX 600 fell 0.64% in early trading, while Dutch chip-equipment maker ASML declined 1.32%.

Investors are increasingly concerned that tighter access restrictions could reduce international demand for advanced computing equipment.

4. Home Depot and Disney face another earnings test

Both companies are scheduled to report before Tuesday's opening bell.

Analysts expect Home Depot to deliver approximately $42.81 billion in revenue and earnings of $3.84 a share, putting housing-related spending in focus.

Disney is expected to post sales of around $25.2 billion, with investors watching streaming profitability, theme-park demand and management's outlook.

Their results could reveal whether consumers are cutting discretionary purchases or continuing to spend despite persistent inflation.

5. Dollar strength intensifies pressure on Fed expectations

The dollar index touched 103.66, its highest level in 19 months, as persistent inflation reinforced expectations of another interest-rate increase in December.

A stronger currency and elevated borrowing costs can weigh on multinational earnings and technology valuations.

Investors will examine minutes from the Fed's October meeting, scheduled for Wednesday at 2 pm ET, for clues about policymakers' willingness to tighten further.

headline: Gold gains slightly to recover from one-year low: what's next?
html_content:
Gold prices edged higher on Tuesday, although gains remained limited as expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike continued to weigh on the precious metal.

Gold futures for December delivery were trading at $3,862.80 at 6:30 AM EST, up around 0.25% from Monday's close.

Prices had fallen to $3,830 on Monday, their lowest level since October 2025, as investors continued to reassess the outlook for US monetary policy.

Rate-hike odds near 96%

According to the CME FedWatch Tool, markets were assigning roughly a 96% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December meeting.

A hike would mark the second increase since the first one in September, and the near-consensus expectation has continued to weigh on gold.

Higher interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding gold, which does not pay interest or dividends. This makes the metal less attractive compared with yield-bearing assets such as government bonds.

Oil prices provided mixed signals for gold on Tuesday.

Energy prices had slipped earlier in the session but subsequently recovered, with West Texas Intermediate crude trading above $86 a barrel and Brent crude near $93.

The rebound came as investors assessed developments in the Middle East, where vessels have continued to come under attack.

headline: Home Depot beats earnings and names new CEO: the bigger test is still ahead
html_content:
Home Depot HD delivered an earnings beat and a CEO succession announcement on Nov 17, giving investors two reasons to reassess the home-improvement giant.

Q3 revenue exceeded Wall Street expectations while finance chief Richard McPhail was named to succeed Ted Decker.

Yet, Home Depot stock is slipping in premarket trading on Tuesday, suggesting the announcements offered less reassurance than investors wanted.

The challenge now is turning resilient sales into stronger profit growth while giving shareholders confidence in the leadership transition.

Home Depot stock yet to see renovation boom

Home Depot’s quarterly revenue came in up 4.9% on a year-over-year basis at $43.4 billion, while adjusted earnings increased to $3.86 per share.

Comparable sales climbed 2.2%, including an identical increase in the US. Those figures showcase improving demand within the existing business, alongside growth in the broader company.

In Q3, professional contractors and smaller repair projects helped offset “continued weakness” in discretionary spending.

That distinction matters: necessary repairs can support revenue even when homeowners postpone ambitious renovations.

For investors, the quarterly print strengthens the case that HD can grow through a difficult housing environment. But it offers less evidence that consumers are ready to unleash a sustained wave of expensive remodeling projects.

McPhail inherits a strategy he helped finance

In its press release, Home Depot said Richard McPhail will become its chief executive and join its board on Nov. 23.

Decker, returning from temporary medical leave, will relinquish the chief executive role but remain chairman. Meanwhile, the company named Ann-Marie Campbell as president and chief operating officer, while Jordan Broggi takes over as CFO.

The appointment puts an architect of Home Depot’s expansion in charge of delivering its returns. CFO since 2019, McPhail oversaw acquisitions including HD Supply, SRS Distribution and GMS, which expanded the company’s capabilities serving professional customers.

His promotion therefore signals continuity, shifting the investment question toward execution: can those businesses generate enough additional sales and earnings to justify the capital committed?

Familiarity with the assets should help, but responsibility for proving their value now sits squarely with McPhail.

The number HD stock investors should watch next

Home Depot now sees fiscal 2026 revenue growth of about 4.5% – the top of its previous range –  and comparable-sales growth of about 1.4%.

Adjusted earnings per share, however, are expected to increase only around 2%.

That gap is the central issue for those invested in Home Depot shares. Expanding sales has value, but a stronger investment case requires more of that growth to reach earnings.

In short, today’s announcements give HD an experienced incoming leader and evidence of commercial resilience.

Neither alone establishes that profit growth is about to accelerate. The next convincing catalyst would be stronger demand accompanied by better earnings conversion – a combination that would make the company’s expansion more rewarding for shareholders.

Wall Street currently has a consensus Overweight rating on HD shares.

headline: Grvt launches Stable Funding Perps to reduce trading costs for real-world assets
html_content:
Grvt has launched Stable Funding Perps (SFP), a new perpetual trading model designed to reduce execution costs and improve funding predictability for traders seeking exposure to real-world assets (RWAs).

The self-custodial trading platform is introducing the product with commodities before expanding into other traditional asset classes, including equities.

The new contracts combine financing-linked funding, liquidity sourced from established financial markets and zero trading fees, offering an alternative to conventional cryptocurrency perpetual contracts.

Grvt said the launch is part of its broader ambition to become a leading platform for trading real-world assets onchain, with plans to expand from seven initial markets to more than 100 over time.

The move comes as cryptocurrency exchanges increasingly introduce traditional financial assets to blockchain-based trading platforms while continuing to use funding mechanisms originally developed for crypto derivatives.

These mechanisms can create unpredictable holding costs, particularly when market positioning becomes heavily one-sided or liquidity is fragmented.

Grvt targets unpredictable funding costs in perpetual trading

Traditional cryptocurrency perpetual contracts rely on funding payments to keep contract prices aligned with their underlying reference markets.

However, funding expenses can rise significantly when traders take concentrated positions in one direction, potentially reducing returns even when their predictions about the underlying asset prove correct.

The problem also extends to tokenised exposure to traditional assets, including commodities and equities.

Although these markets already have established spot, futures and financing infrastructure, blockchain-based perpetual contracts can experience funding volatility because of exchange-specific liquidity conditions and positioning.

Research published by BitMEX in the second quarter of 2026 documented considerable differences in funding rates across derivatives trading venues, including extreme annualised funding readings in oil perpetual contracts.

Grvt also highlighted the impact of funding uncertainty on trading decisions.

According to a survey conducted by the company in June 2026, 56% of 134 participating traders said they had either avoided opening a perpetual position or closed an existing one because funding costs were unpredictable.

SFP seeks to address the issue by linking funding rates to market makers' costs of hedging positions through established traditional financial markets.

Rather than relying primarily on premium-driven funding mechanisms used by conventional crypto perpetuals, the model draws on existing market pricing, financing and hedging infrastructure.

The company believes this approach can provide more predictable holding costs while reducing exposure to volatility in crypto-native funding mechanisms.

Funding payments are settled once per weekday, typically at market close, with separate rates applying to long and short positions.

Depending on prevailing funding rates, traders may either pay or receive funding. The rates remain variable, with adjustments for market holidays and weekend financing.

A triple funding charge applies on a designated weekday to account for weekend financing costs.

"As more real-world assets move onchain, we need to rethink how they're traded, not simply replicate the mechanics of crypto perpetuals," said Hong Yea, co-founder and chief executive of Grvt.

"If you're trading gold, oil or equities, your returns should primarily reflect your view of the underlying market, not unpredictable funding costs or unnecessary trading fees," Hong added.

Traditional markets already have deep liquidity and established financing infrastructure. We're bringing those advantages onchain, with competitive execution costs, more predictable funding and self-custody.

Co-founder and chief executive of Grvt
Hong Yea

Traditional market liquidity underpins Grvt's execution model

Alongside changes to funding, Grvt is introducing a different approach to sourcing liquidity for perpetual contracts linked to traditional assets.

Instead of creating an independent liquidity pool for each market, the platform uses a request-for-quote (RFQ) model that connects traders with market makers drawing on existing financial-market infrastructure.

Under this structure, market makers provide live buy and sell quotes while using traditional exchanges, prime brokers and other established market infrastructure to source liquidity and hedge their exposures.

Grvt said this arrangement allows liquidity providers to benefit from deeper underlying markets, established financing arrangements and competitive hedging costs.

These factors can help market makers offer tighter spreads and execute larger trades without maintaining a separate order book.

The RFQ structure also includes quote acceptance controls, such as last-look mechanisms, which allow liquidity providers to manage execution and hedging risks.

According to Grvt, the ability to manage these risks can support more competitive pricing, particularly when market makers are dealing with changing liquidity conditions.

The company said traders should assess execution costs by considering the quoted spread alongside any trading fees, rather than focusing solely on spreads.

Grvt charges 0% trading fees on SFP contracts and does not apply an additional markup to market-maker spreads.

However, this does not mean trading is entirely cost-free.

Execution costs are incorporated into the quoted buy and sell prices, while funding charges are accounted for separately when positions remain open through the daily funding settlement.

Actual execution costs and available liquidity will continue to depend on market conditions, trade sizes and quotes supplied by liquidity providers.

"We don't believe every onchain market needs to recreate liquidity that already exists elsewhere," Hong added.

If market makers can hedge more efficiently in established markets, they can pass those efficiencies on through better pricing and deeper liquidity. That's the advantage we're building around.

Co-founder and chief executive of Grvt
Hong Yea

Commodity trading hours, leverage and funding arbitrage opportunities

The initial SFP offering follows the trading schedules of the underlying commodity markets rather than providing continuous cryptocurrency-style trading.

Contracts are available for trading approximately 23 hours a day, five days a week, subject to the CME Globex calendar and applicable market holidays.

Grvt said the schedule reflects the availability of reliable reference prices and sufficient hedging liquidity in established commodity markets.

When traditional markets close, market makers can face reduced liquidity, wider spreads and increased risks associated with hedging their positions.

The company is therefore prioritising execution quality during established trading hours while developing plans to extend access.

The initial contracts also have larger minimum trade sizes, reflecting the requirements of the traditional-market liquidity providers supporting the platform.

Grvt said it is working towards introducing smaller minimum trade sizes, additional liquidity providers, broader trading hours and eventually 24/7 availability.

Beyond directional commodity trading, the funding structure could also create opportunities for traders pursuing funding-arbitrage strategies.

Where matching instruments and sufficient liquidity are available, a trader could take a position that receives funding in a conventional perpetual contract while opening an opposing SFP position to hedge the underlying market exposure.

Such arrangements could potentially allow traders to benefit from differences between the funding mechanisms used by the two products.

However, Grvt acknowledged that these strategies remain exposed to changes in funding rates, basis movements, execution costs and the risks associated with maintaining both positions.

The platform also said traders may be able to reduce directional exposure when an SFP market is closed by taking an opposing position in an equivalent Grvt perpetual market, where one is available.

This would allow traders to manage their exposure without necessarily closing their existing SFP positions.

Grvt is additionally exploring lower margin requirements for qualifying hedged positions as a future product enhancement.

All SFP contracts settle in USDC through the company's zero-knowledge blockchain infrastructure, allowing traders to retain self-custody of their funds.

Leverage is available up to 20 times on supported contracts, although silver is limited to 10 times leverage.

Lower leverage limits also apply to larger positions.

Grvt plans expansion to more than 100 RWA markets

The launch represents another step in Grvt's expansion beyond cryptocurrency derivatives and into trading and investment products linked to real-world assets.

While the initial offering focuses on seven commodity markets, the SFP model is designed to support a broader range of traditional financial instruments.

Equities are among the asset classes being targeted as the company works towards expanding its offering to more than 100 markets.

The longer-term strategy centres on combining traditional financial-market liquidity and financing infrastructure with blockchain-based settlement and self-custody.

Grvt is also seeking to improve trading accessibility through smaller minimum positions, expanded trading hours and a wider network of liquidity providers.

The company believes these developments could make perpetual contracts better suited to traditional assets, where financing structures, market hours and hedging requirements differ from those of cryptocurrencies.

Hong said the commodity launch was only the first stage of the company's broader RWA ambitions.

Bringing real-world assets onchain shouldn't mean forcing them to trade like crypto, our ambition is to build the best venue for trading RWAs onchain, combining the efficiency and liquidity of established financial markets with the accessibility and self-custody of blockchain infrastructure. Commodities are just the beginning.

Co-founder and chief executive of Grvt
Hong Yea

headline: Anthropic receives its first 'Buy' rating
html_content:
Anthropic has secured a bullish Wall Street endorsement even before investors can trade its shares.

New Street Research initiated coverage of the Claude developer with a Buy rating and $105 price target, putting a valuation marker well above the company’s proposed $70 – $78 IPO range.

Analyst Pierre Ferragu’s argument reaches beyond enthusiasm for this week’s listing – he sees AI capturing a growing portion of what businesses spend on knowledge work.

With pricing expected on Wednesday and trading beginning a day after, investors must decide how much of that opportunity the opening share price already reflects.

Why is New Street bullish on Anthropic stock?

Ferragu dubbed Anthropic a “generational IPO” – framing artificial intelligence as a decades-long shift in corporate spending.

He compared it to cloud computing, which captured an enormous 30% of incremental IT spending between 2010 and 2025.

AI could spread twice as quickly across an addressable market 10x larger, he noted.

Ferragu’s forecast puts AI’s share of knowledge-work spending near 7% in 2030, with about 25% of incremental spending flowing toward the technology through 2040.

The investment implication is substantial: Anthropic’s opportunity would extend beyond existing software budgets into spending on tasks people perform.

However, those projections describe AI’s potential market – they do not establish how much of it will Anthropic capture.

Significance of IPO price for the bullish case

In his research report, Pierre Ferragu also said that Anthropic’s comparatively cautious IPO pricing reduces downside risk.

His $105 target implies about 35% upside from $78 – an attractive spread, provided investors can buy near the proposed range.

Anthropic’s announced offering comprises 825 million shares, including Anthropic stock sold by existing shareholders.

At $78, that represents $64.35 billion in gross offering proceeds, before any underwriter option; the company would receive only the proceeds attributable to its own shares.

For prospective buyers, the distinction is crucial: the advertised upside is measured against an indicative offering price.

A sharp opening jump would consume part of the return Ferragu’s target suggests before public-market buyers even establish a position.

Anthropic shares have an execution test ahead

New Street’s endorsement gives investors a framework for valuing Anthropic beyond its debut.

The harder question is whether growing demand can produce durable returns after the infrastructure bill.

Anthropic’s prospectus discloses roughly $900.9 billion in purchase and lease commitments –  overwhelmingly tied to computing and infrastructure, with about $451.6 billion expected before the end of 2030.

Those obligations make the pace of customer spending especially consequential.

Ferragu’s thesis therefore rests on two judgments: AI adoption will expand rapidly, and Anthropic’s entry valuation leaves sufficient room for shareholders to benefit.

Investors should assess both separately.

A vast market can support extraordinary growth, but the price paid determines how much of that success reaches a portfolio.

headline: Tilray Brands stock has crashed to a record low: is this fallen angel a buy?
html_content:
Tilray Brands stock extended its sell-off this week, sinking to a record low as concerns about the company intensified. The shares fell to $2.34, leaving them down 74% so far this year, 55% over the past six months, and 98% over the past five years. That makes Tilray one of Wall Street’s biggest laggards. The question now is whether this crash presents a buying opportunity.

Tilray Brands has fallen as cannabis rescheduling process stalls

TLRY stock has been in a strong sell-off, mirroring the performance of other companies in the cannabis industry. The AdvisorShares Pure US Cannabis ETF (MSOS) has slumped by 16% in the last six months and 23% this year. 

Similarly, companies like Curaleaf, Truelieve, Green Thumb Industries, and Verano Holdings have all dropped by double digits this year. 

These stocks have plunged as the cannabis rescheduling process that President Donald Trump started in April stalls. In that month, the Justice Department moved marijuana covered by state medical licenses from Schedule 1 to Schedule III. Adult-use cannabis remained in Schedule 1. 

At the same time, a separate DEA hearing moved all cannabis to Schedule III, with hearings continuing to date. Also, several lawsuits have been filed challenging the hearings and the rescheduling as a whole. 

As such, while industry players are optimistic that the rescheduling will go on well, there are also concerns about the pace. 

On the positive side, Democrats won the midterm elections by a large margin. They now control the Senate by about 56 seats and the House of Representatives by over 250 seats. As such, the Senate likely has the votes it needs to pass the SAFE Banking Act, which will make it easy for cannabis companies to access banking services.

READ MORE: Tilray Brands stock analysis ahead of earnings: will it rebound or fall further?

Tilray Brands is not active in the United States but the management has said that it will do so once there is regulatory clarity. Such a move would let it use its experience in Canada and other countries to expand in the country.

Tilray Brands' business is growing

Despite the ongoing weakness in Tilray Brands’ stock, there are signs that the company’s business is doing well. The last earnings report showed that its net revenue rose by 23% to $257 million, with its gross profit hitting $77.5 million. 

Most of its businesses grew during the quarter. Its beverage revenue jumped by 82% to $101.5 million, making it the biggest part of its business. This growth was driven by its recent acquisitions, including BrewDog.

The distribution business made over $84.3 million, up by 14%, while its wellness segment made $15.3 million. These metrics were offset by its cannabis business, which made $56.1 million, down from $64 million in the same period last year. The company also made a net loss of over $40 million. 

TLRY stock price technical analysis

Tilray Brands stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the Tilray Brands stock has been in a strong sell-off this year. The sell-off accelerated after the stock hit a crucial resistance level of $4.96 in August this year.

It has remained below the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA), a sign that bears have prevailed. Also, the stock has slumped below the Supertrend indicator. 

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has also dropped to the oversold level of 30. Therefore, the path of the least resistance for the stock is downwards, with the next level to watch being at $2.0. A drop below that level will point to more downside, potentially to $1.50. 

However, it is worth noting that Tilray Brands stock tends to have some short squeezes, especially when there is cannabis regulation news.

headline: Interview: Nvidia's crisis could metastasize into broader selloff: B2BROKER CEO
html_content:
The past couple of weeks have been dramatic for the US tech stocks.

Earnings from companies like Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta revealed that these companies turned cash flow negative as the AI infrastructure bill is finally hitting the tech giants.

Then the US mid-term elections caused a sell-off in AI stocks as markets feared a Democratic victory would slow down the AI build-up.

Anthropic then announced it will raise $62 billion at a price range of $70 to $78 apiece.

Then AI's poster boy, Nvidia, got pulled into a storm with its CEO, Jensen Huang, resigning after revelations about his romantic relationships with multiple women, including a business executive who is suspected to be a Chinese intelligence agent.

Even though the selling in the week has abated, with Nvidia shares trading down around 7% this week, the stock is down almost 30% in the last month.

Investors are also digesting the possibility of the AI trade without its charismatic leader, Jensen Huang, captaining the ship.

Arthur Azizov, CEO and Founder at B2BROKER Group, says that big tech companies could sustain their AI buildout for a couple more years if they can show that they can monetise the investments.

In a conversation with Invezz, Azizov also shared the risks surrounding an Nvidia without Huang and his views about Anthropic's IPO.

Excerpts:

Invezz: Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta all reported free cash flow going down or going negative. How long can big companies burn cash until they see returns?

I believe these large technology companies can keep spending cash for several years without a break, but it’s important for them to pay attention to investor sentiment.

Investors won’t wait that long unless they see evidence that the spending actually produces results.

First things first, we need to draw the line between negative free cash flow and a business that can’t generate cash whatsoever.

Alphabet, for instance, generated roughly $42 billion in operating cash flow in the third quarter, but high capital expenditure resulted in negative free cash flow.

So, the company is still generating substantial cash; it has simply decided to reinvest large amounts.

What’s interesting is whether investments on such a scale will lead to profitable demand. If cloud revenue and AI-related sales continue to grow while margins remain healthy enough, investors may tolerate weaker free cash flow for some time.

If spending keeps rising and the additional capacity isn’t able to generate enough revenue, by contrast, financing costs and pressure on shareholder returns might eventually force companies to revisit their plans.

Given this, I’d expect investors to wait two to three years for measurable progress. This scenario could play out even if the full returns take longer.

Invezz: Alphabet and Microsoft didn’t raise their capex guidance. Is that a sign demand is slowing, or are the companies just getting cautious?

Basically, if they didn’t raise their capex guidance, I can’t claim that this is proof that demand is slowing. The thing is that these companies have already committed to exceptionally large investments, so keeping their forecasts unchanged can simply mean they’re working within the plans they had already announced.

As for Alphabet, it kept its 2026 capital expenditure guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion, while saying it expects spending to grow significantly in 2027.

Its Google Cloud business, meanwhile, reported strong growth in the third quarter, which doesn’t make it seem like the company is getting ready for a collapse in demand.

Well, the companies may be cautious with their spending, yet I don’t think that preserving capex guidance at previous levels necessarily means they’re experiencing weaker demand.

Invezz: Cloud revenue growth has been a positive for Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet. Is that becoming a crux for companies to monetise AI services? What operating signals would you watch over the next two quarters, such as cloud growth, margins, or capex guidance?

Yes. I find cloud services to be a kind of crux for these companies to monetize their AI services.

Businesses require computing capacity to build and run AI products, so major providers like Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet can charge fees for providing that capacity alongside other services.

Over the next two quarters, I’d pay close attention to cloud revenue growth and operating margins.

The former gives us an idea of how strong customer demand is, although it also includes services apart from AI. Where possible, I’d also look at what companies say about the contribution of AI to that growth.

The latter may show how much companies earn from providing those services after covering their costs.

Still, it’s important to note that drawing conclusions from a single quarter wouldn’t be right, as margins can be affected by investments and the cost of adding capacity.

Invezz: Are US stocks finally trading at expensive valuations? Is the dip after the elections a buy-the-dip situation, or is more pain coming for investors?

Parts of the US market, to my mind, especially companies priced for years of non-stop AI growth, have been expensive for a while.

And a fall in share prices doesn’t make them cheap right away, as we also need to consider investors’ expectations of what those businesses will earn and how much capital they must spend to get to that point.

So, while the post-election dip could be a chance to buy some shares of strong companies at a better price, I don’t think that investors should assume that the decline is over.

More pain is fairly likely if upcoming earnings don’t meet expectations or companies continue to spend heavily without showing real progress towards returns.

Personally, I’d look at individual businesses in this situation instead of “blind-buying” because the market has gone into a decline.

Invezz: Nvidia has been the poster child for AI. Now Nvidia is in the middle of a controversy. How do you view the controversy affecting Nvidia and the AI trade?

What we already witness is uncertainty. And it tends to appear in such situations.

Jensen Huang has stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO, and investors are now paying close attention to the case.

Let’s face the truth: his departure could dramatically affect the company’s future leadership and strategy.

He’s not only a CEO, but also the company’s high-profile, charismatic face at events and meetings.

So, even a company that has been the poster child for AI results could face a difficult transition.

Since Nvidia is a major supplier of AI chips and an important part of many investor portfolios, the wider AI sector could also be affected.

A decline in Nvidia’s shares could hurt investor confidence and “metastasize” into a broader sell-off in other AI companies.

Yes, there is still strong demand for AI computing, but the situation is serious. I’d keep monitoring it.

Invezz: Recent reports said Blackstone views Anthropic may struggle to get an investment-grade credit rating immediately. Is tech companies’ reliance on debt starting to bite them back? What is your outlook for Anthropic’s IPO? What is the valuation you think is fair?

Since AI companies tend to take on large commitments even before they have established a record of consistent profitability, reliance on debt could come back to bite them.

A lower credit rating could make borrowing more expensive and difficult, for sure.

And Blackstone’s reported view, by the way, is an expectation. It can’t yet be treated as a rating decision.

As for Anthropic, I’m mostly positive about its prospects.

Despite its IPO filing showing substantial losses and long-term computing commitments, it also reveals revenue of $33.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026. This is a considerable amount.

Given the picture, I would estimate its value at around $1 trillion.

That’s lower than the roughly $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion valuation implied by its proposed IPO price range, but still about 15 times the latest quarter’s revenue annualized, which already forecasts enormous future growth.

What is worth watching is the number of shares available for public trading.

As we saw with other IPOs (say, SpaceX’s), strong demand and a limited supply of shares can result in sharp price moves before the market settles on a valuation.

headline: Disney shares slip despite earnings beat and $3B cost cutting plans
html_content:
Disney shares fell on Tuesday despite the entertainment giant reporting better-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter results.

The stock initially gained around 2% in premarket trading following the earnings announcement but subsequently reversed course, falling more than 2%.

Tuesday's decline came after a strong run-up of approximately 17% since October, as investors positioned for growth under new CEO Josh D'Amaro.

Streaming and parks deliver strong results

Disney reported revenue of $25.9 billion for the quarter, up 16% year over year and above analyst expectations of approximately $25.2 billion.

Adjusted earnings came in at $1.77 per share, beating estimates of $1.67. Total segment operating income increased 43% to $4.97 billion.

The quarter also benefited from an additional 53rd week in the company's fiscal calendar.

Disney's Entertainment division delivered one of its strongest quarters, with revenue increasing 17% to $11.9 billion and operating income nearly doubling to $1.3 billion.

Its streaming business was particularly encouraging. Disney+ and Hulu generated combined operating income of $824 million, more than double the $402 million recorded in the year-earlier quarter.

Streaming revenue increased 19%, reflecting improved profitability and continued subscriber engagement.

The Sports segment, led by ESPN, also performed well. Revenue rose 16% to $4.6 billion, while operating income jumped 53% to nearly $1.4 billion, supported by strong NFL and college football viewership.

Disney's Experiences division, which includes theme parks and cruises, reported record revenue of $10.1 billion, up 15%, with operating income increasing 20% to around $2.3 billion.

Higher spending raise concerns

Despite the strong results, management's plans for further cost reductions have attracted attention.

Disney is targeting $3 billion in annual operating expense savings by fiscal 2029.

CFO Hugh Johnston confirmed that the program will involve additional layoffs, although the company has not disclosed the number of employees who could be affected.

At the same time, Disney plans to increase cash content spending by approximately 9% to $26 billion in fiscal 2027, with additional investment in international programming and sports rights.

Weakness at its international parks is another concern. Attendance at Hong Kong Disneyland and Shanghai Disney Resort deteriorated during the quarter, and management expects the pressure to continue into fiscal 2027.

Disney offers upbeat 2027 outlook

Disney attempted to reassure investors with its outlook for the coming fiscal year.

The company expects double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share in fiscal 2027, excluding the benefit from the additional week in fiscal 2026.

It also anticipates total segment operating income growth of approximately 8%.

Disney's board approved a 33% increase in its annual dividend to $2 per share, to be distributed in two installments.

headline: Capital.com study finds only 21% of European investors are confident making decisions
html_content:
A majority of prospective investors in Europe want to succeed in financial markets, but relatively few feel confident making investment decisions independently, according to a new study by Capital.com.

The online trading and investment platform's Beyond Access study, based on a survey of 3,613 prospective investors across the UK, Germany, Italy, Spain, Poland, the Netherlands and a wider EU sample, found that 71% consider investment success personally important.

However, only 21% said they felt very confident making investment decisions on their own.

Another 42% described themselves as somewhat confident, highlighting a gap between investors' ambitions and their confidence.

The findings suggest that behavioural barriers and uncertainty around investment decisions remain significant challenges, even as access to financial products improves across Europe.

Investment confidence remains a challenge for European investors

The study found that many prospective investors understand the importance of investing but struggle when it comes to making decisions.

Around 66% of respondents recognised that savings earning less than inflation lose purchasing power over time.

Meanwhile, 60% understood that keeping most of their savings in low-risk cash accounts could mean missing out on long-term investment returns.

However, concerns about making the wrong decisions remain widespread.

Approximately 54% worry about making investment decisions they might later regret, while 47% frequently second-guess their choices.

Another 44% delay investment decisions because they fear getting them wrong.

Information overload is also a concern, with half of respondents saying they feel overwhelmed by the amount of investment information available.

Furthermore, 58% said experiencing substantial losses would make them less likely to invest again.

Confidence is particularly limited when it comes to mainstream investment products, including pensions, bonds, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and mutual funds.

Only between 8% and 14% of respondents said they felt very confident investing in these products.

Clear information and risk guidance could improve confidence

The survey identified clearer information and practical decision-making support as important factors that could help investors become more confident.

Two-thirds of respondents said clear explanations reduce their anxiety about investing.

Meanwhile, 64% said receiving a clear explanation of investment risks before confirming a decision would be extremely or very helpful.

Other forms of support also attracted considerable interest.

Around 60% valued the opportunity to speak with an expert when uncertain about an investment decision.

Another 59% wanted a simple explanation of whether an investment might be suitable for them, while 57% said simulations showing potential losses would be helpful.

More than half of respondents also valued reminders of their long-term financial goals (54%).

Meanwhile, 50% supported having a short cooling-off period before completing a transaction or receiving a risk prompt on an online investment platform.

Capital.com CEO Europe Christoforos Soutzis said the findings highlighted the importance of supporting investors beyond simply providing access to financial products.

Policymakers across Europe are working to make investing more accessible, and savings and investment accounts will lead many people to look again at whether investing has a place alongside their savings. The question Capital.com's study asks is what happens once people have access. Most Europeans understand why investing matters, yet only one in five feel very confident deciding on their own. Supporting investors beyond access means giving them clear information, a clear view of risk and the room to take their time, including when the right decision is to wait.

CEO Europe, Capital.com
Christoforos Soutzis

Investment confidence varies across European countries

The study also identified differences in investment behaviour and confidence across the countries surveyed.

Poland recorded the highest proportion of respondents who considered investment success very important, at 43%, compared with the European average of 30%.

However, 66% of Polish respondents said they frequently second-guess their investment decisions, 19 percentage points above the European average.

In Germany, 18% felt very confident investing in ETFs, compared with the 10% European average. Additionally, 52% said they felt prepared for investment downturns, above the overall figure of 47%.

Spanish respondents demonstrated particularly strong demand for investment guidance.

Around 79% said investment success was important to them, while 76% said clear explanations reduced their investment anxiety.

In the UK, 66% recognised that keeping money in cash could mean missing out on long-term returns.

However, 55% reported feeling anxious when making investment decisions, compared with 47% across Europe.

The Netherlands presented a different picture.

Although only 30% of respondents struggled to open an investment account, below the European average of 35%, just 53% trusted their own investment judgement, compared with 63% overall.

In Italy, 41% felt overwhelmed by investment information, the lowest proportion among the surveyed markets. However, only 7% felt very confident investing in ETFs, below the European average of 10%.

Soutzis said the differences highlighted the need to address country-specific challenges while providing investors with clearer risk explanations and more time to consider their decisions.

The findings come as the European Union advances its Savings and Investments Union initiative, including recommendations for member states to introduce accessible savings and investment accounts for retail investors.

Spain has approved its Financia Europa savings and investment account, while Poland's Personal Investment Accounts are scheduled to launch in January 2027.

Soutzis added that "A confident investor is someone who understands when to act, when to wait, and when to seek guidance. The differences between countries show that each market has its own pressure point, and in all of them people decide better when risks are explained clearly and they have time to think. At Capital.com, our role, within the regulatory frameworks we operate under, is to help build that kind of decision environment."

headline: Can the bull market extend into a fifth straight year in 2027?
html_content:
US stock market’s next rally is broadly expected to depend on whether corporate America can turn resilient demand and artificial intelligence (AI) spending into stronger profits.

Morgan Stanley senior strategist Mike Wilson believes it can, raising his 12-month S&P 500 target to 8,700 from 8,000, signaling roughly 15% upside from recent levels.

His forecast offers investors a bullish roadmap into 2027, although the recent sell-off shows how quickly confidence can unravel when interest rates and technology valuations come under scrutiny.

What could drive US stocks higher in 2027?

Wilson’s optimism rests on an economy settling into a steadier expansion – with corporate profits continuing to grow even as the initial benefits of stronger operating leverage fade.

Morgan Stanley forecasts S&P 500 earnings of $420 per share in 2027, compared with an expected $369 this year, suggesting an increase of about 14%.

That makes earnings delivery central to the bank’s bullish case.

Lower oil prices could ease business costs and support household spending, while reduced interest-rate volatility would make future profits easier to value.

Continued AI investments and adoption offer another potential growth engine.

For investors, the distinction matters: Wilson’s outlook requires companies to produce stronger earnings, giving share prices fundamental support as the market advances.

Industrials could broaden the rally next year

The more revealing part of Wilson’s outlook may be his preference for industrials, rather than another blanket endorsement of technology stocks.

He sees improving earnings revisions, expanding backlogs and more attractive valuations supporting the sector.

Selected financial and consumer discretionary companies also feature among his preferred opportunities.

That positioning suggests the next advance could draw strength from a wider range of businesses.

Broader participation would give the market additional sources of earnings growth when enthusiasm for individual AI companies weakens.

Still, Wilson’s appetite for cyclical exposure comes with a quality filter.

Strong balance sheets, durable margins and cash generation remain priorities – characteristics that could help companies withstand higher financing costs or a slower spending environment.

A bullish destination with an uncertain route

Mike Wilson views the correction as an opportunity, but his S&P 500 index forecast leaves room for further turbulence.

He has identified 7,100 – 7,300 as an important support range and acknowledges that another test could precede a sustained recovery.

Note that Morgan Stanley isn’t alone among Wall Street firms in keeping bullish on US stocks.

Barclays strategist Venu Krishna also targets 8,700 for 2027, offering another bullish assessment, although agreement between banks cannot guarantee returns.

The crucial test is whether earnings growth materializes while oil and interest rates become less disruptive.

Persistent inflation or more aggressive monetary tightening could undermine that combination.

A fifth year for the bull market is therefore plausible.

Investors should judge the case through profit revisions, margins, and broader market participation as 2027 approaches.

headline: Deutsche Bank stock falls as leak exposes Epstein payments, Russian dealings
html_content:
Deutsche Bank shares fell on Tuesday after a massive leak of more than 15 million internal records exposed alleged historical failures in the German lender's risk management and financial crime controls, bringing its past dealings with Russian oligarchs, Jeffrey Epstein and US President Donald Trump back into focus.

The records, comprising confidential reports, emails and meeting minutes, were obtained by Indian author and journalist Josy Joseph and South African journalist Khadija Sharife.

A consortium of more than 200 journalists from dozens of international media organisations, including Daraj, Der Spiegel, Manager Magazin, El Universal, Financial Mail, Kyodo News, Le Monde, The New York Times, Financial Times and Paper Trail Media, analysed the material.

The documents point to alleged systemic weaknesses across different business functions at the Frankfurt-listed lender, with incidents stretching back as far as two decades.

Deutsche Bank shares fell nearly 4% in Frankfurt and were down nearly 4% in US premarket trading as well.

"The matters which are in focus of the media reports date back many years and in some cases as much as two decades. Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators," Deutsche Bank said in a statement.

Russian oligarch dealings and Epstein payments come under scrutiny

According to the Financial Times, the relationship between Deutsche Bank, Russian money and oligarchs was a major factor behind the whistleblowers' decision to copy the cache of documents and share it with the journalists.

The records provide an unusually detailed account of the lender's years-long cultivation of wealthy Russian clients, even as some of its risk managers warned that maintaining these relationships could expose the bank to financial crime risks.

The documents indicate that Deutsche Bank continued pursuing business in Russia, including with prominent oligarchs, right up until Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, despite concerns raised by some managers.

The bank's clients included Russian billionaires Oleg V. Deripaska and Viktor F. Vekselberg.

According to The New York Times, internal records show that risk managers repeatedly raised concerns about the relationships, but the profits associated with retaining these clients prevailed.

Even after the invasion, bank executives initially resisted calls to exit the Russian market.

The lender eventually decided to withdraw after competitors announced their departures, the NYT reported.

In response to questions, Deutsche Bank said it had acted lawfully and never helped clients evade financial sanctions.

"Following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Deutsche Bank acted promptly to implement the rapidly evolving sanctions imposed by the relevant authorities," the bank said.

The leaked records also revealed that Deutsche Bank processed $582 million in suspicious payments linked to late financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, considerably more than previously known, according to the FT.

Suspicious payments, however, do not in themselves establish that every transaction was criminal.

Deutsche Bank has previously acknowledged its relationship with Epstein and said it ended the association at the end of 2018.

Trump tax document accidentally disclosed in 2017

Another revelation concerns the accidental disclosure of Donald Trump's tax information in March 2017, when he was serving his first term as US president and was a Deutsche Bank client.

According to the Financial Times, the bank inadvertently sent a document containing Trump's tax information to another client's accountant.

The incident, which was not previously publicly disclosed in detail, was described by Christian Sewing, who was then Deutsche Bank's head of private banking and is now its chief executive, as "an awful mistake".

The error was reportedly kept secret from the White House.

Asked about the incident in Manila, Trump criticised the bank for disclosing the information.

"They shouldn't have done it. It's illegal for them to do it," Trump said.

Investigation reveals wider failures in risk management

The investigation also found that the lender had failed to offboard around 28,000 problematic investment banking clients who had been identified for removal by early 2018.

The documents also allege that the bank concealed information relating to cost targets in 2021, when external monitors in New York reportedly warned that its appetite for risk was running ahead of its controls.

The revelations add to a long history of regulatory scrutiny and financial penalties faced by the German lender.

Deutsche Bank has paid approximately 18.6 billion euros ($20.5 billion) in settlements since 2012 over alleged market manipulation, money laundering, mis-selling and misrepresentation, among other issues, the FT reported.

The bank has also been raided multiple times by German authorities this year.

"The articles accuse [Deutsche Bank] of putting profit and risk-taking ahead of controls. The articles illustrate the issues and settlements paid by DBK since 1999 to 2025 with most of the issues in the period 2007-2015," said Anke Reingen, an analyst at RBC Capital Markets.

Reingen noted that while Deutsche Bank's relationship with Epstein was already known, the revelation that it had processed around $600 million in suspicious payments was particularly significant, representing roughly twice the amount previously known.

Investors assess the fallout from the revelations

The latest disclosures have renewed concerns about whether Deutsche Bank has adequately addressed weaknesses in its risk management framework, particularly given the number of historical incidents now coming to light.

Jochen Stanzl, chief market analyst at Consorsbank, said the sheer volume of leaked documents raised questions about what else could emerge.

"In the short term, these revelations are not helping the stock price. When faced with uncertainty, investors’ first instinct is to sell, and this case is no exception," Stanzl said in a Reuters report.

headline: Alibaba stock flashes the risky death cross pattern as earnings loom
html_content:
Alibaba Group stock has come under heavy selling pressure this month and now trades at its lowest level since January last year, as the company’s capital spending continues to ramp up. BABA fell to $87.25 in New York, more than 54% below its peak for the year. The shares have also formed a death cross on the weekly chart, just ahead of the company’s upcoming earnings report.

Alibaba stock has fallen amid costs concerns

Alibaba Group stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months, moving from a high of $192.43 in September last year to $87. The decline is a big contrast to what Amazon Group has done. Amazon was trading at $257 on Monday, a few points below the year-to-date high of $287. 

In the past, Alibaba and Amazon shares had a close correlation because of the similarity of their services. Indeed, there were signs that Alibaba had a better business model than Amazon because of the asset-light nature of its operations. Unlike Amazon, it did not need to invest heavily in warehouses. 

The relationship between the two ended a few years ago as Jack Ma’s profile grew. After he criticized Chinese regulators, authorities stepped up their crackdown on the company. At the same time, competition in China has intensified in recent years, with rivals such as JD.com and PDD pushing to gain market share.

Alibaba stock has also plunged because of the ongoing investments in the AI space that is consuming billions of dollars. Just recently, the company raised $10 billion by selling shares. This raise happened as the company’s capital expenditure soared. It spent $9.975 billion in the second quarter, up by 75% from the same period last year.

The most recent results showed that Alibaba’s profits have plunged. Its net profit plunged by 75% in the second quarter to 10.4 billion yuan, which is equivalent to $1.5 billion. Revenue rose by 9% to 268 billion yuan, even as its AI Cloud and Compute Services from external clients jumped by 45%. The company attributed this growth to the increased adoption of its AI-related products.

Meanwhile, while Qwen AI usage is growing, there are concerns about the rising competition from models like Kimi, MiniMax, and DeepSeek.

The next important catalyst for Alibaba shares is the upcoming earnings report this week. Yahoo Finance data shows that the average revenue estimate has jumped to 269 billion yuan, up by 8.90% from a year earlier. 

Investors will focus on its cloud computing business, which has emerged as its most important this year. Analysts have a mixed outlook of Alibaba shares. Wells Fargo recently set a target of $190, representing a 73% upside. Citigroup and Jefferies also boosted their targets. On the other hand, companies like JPMorgan and Piper Sandler reduced their targets.

Alibaba Group stock has formed a death cross pattern

BABA stock chart | Source: TradingView

The weekly chart shows that Alibaba stock has been in a strong sell-off this year. It has now formed a death cross pattern, which happens when the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA) cross each other. This death cross is important as it has formed on the weekly chart.

The stock has slumped below the important support level of $91.8, its lowest level on June 22nd. Moving above that level invalidated the double-bottom pattern. It has also plunged below the 61.8% retracement and is now eyeing the 78.2%. 

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling in the near term, with the next key target being at $80. A move above the resistance at $100 will invalidate the bearish outlook.

Investors will focus on its cloud computing business, which has emerged as its most important this year. Analysts have a mixed outlook of Alibaba shares.
