headline: Nasdaq slips as Wall Street awaits Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO
html_content:
Wall Street opened lower on Tuesday as investors turned their attention to Nvidia’s quarterly results and Anthropic’s highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO).

The Nasdaq Composite fell around 0.09%, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.24%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 313 points.

Investors are assessing whether demand for artificial intelligence-related companies can support valuations following recent declines.

Anthropic maintained its proposed IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share in an updated filing on Tuesday.

The company is expected to set its final offering price on Wednesday before beginning trading on the Nasdaq on November 19.

Nvidia earnings in focus after leadership turmoil

Nvidia shares fell 0.72% in trading as investors prepared for the chipmaker’s quarterly results, due after the closing bell.

The company has been under pressure since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive last week following revelations about extramarital affairs, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Beijing.

Nvidia has lost approximately $410 billion in market value since the developments emerged.

Its shares have fallen nearly 24% this month, putting the stock on track for its largest monthly decline since April 2022.

The company's board is reportedly not considering Huang's return as CEO, despite a campaign supported by several prominent figures in the technology industry.

The leadership uncertainty has also raised questions about Nvidia's margins and cash outflows, given its influence across the artificial intelligence ecosystem.

Other semiconductor stocks recovered in trading.

Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices gained 1.4% and 0.6%, respectively, while Marvell Technology advanced 2.58%.

Intel shares, however, fell 2% after Nvidia reduced its stake in the company by 25%.

Cloud infrastructure providers CoreWeave and Nebius gained 0.11% and 3.39%, respectively.

Technology stocks recover as investors assess AI demand

The recovery extended to companies supplying components for data centres.

Photonic product makers Coherent and Lumentum rose 5.8% and 4.4%, respectively, following reports that the Trump administration plans to proceed with efforts to block imports of Chinese data-centre equipment despite opposition from US technology companies.

The developments come as investors reassess the outlook for AI-related investments following recent losses in major technology stocks.

Monday's session highlighted the extent of the pressure.

The Dow fell more than 700 points, or 1.4%, while the S&P 500 declined 1.9%.

The Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.5%, marking its biggest one-day decline since November 5.

Fed outlook and economic data add to market focus

Investors are also monitoring economic releases and comments from Federal Reserve officials for clues about the interest-rate outlook.

October retail sales increased 0.2% to $748.2 billion, in line with expectations.

However, sales excluding gas and automobiles rose 0.6% from September, exceeding the 0.4% forecast.

Markets are also awaiting comments from Fed officials Christopher Waller, Beth Hammack and John Williams.

Recent remarks from policymakers have indicated openness to a more aggressive rate-hike path as price pressures increase.

According to CME FedWatch, markets are pricing in a 90.7% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December.

Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's latest meeting, due on Wednesday, will provide further insight into policymakers' thinking.

Among individual stocks, JPMorgan fell 1.22% after announcing that insider Bregje de Best would succeed Jeremy Barnum as chief financial officer in early 2027.

Home Depot also declined 2.55% ahead of a leadership transition, despite reporting better-than-expected quarterly results.

Disney shares traded 0.49% higher after the company reported better-than-expected results.

headline: Why is SLS stock soaring over 220% on Tuesday?
html_content:
Shares of Sellas Life Sciences surged more than 220% at market open on Tuesday after the drug developer reported positive results from a late-stage trial of its experimental cancer vaccine, which significantly extended survival among patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

The vaccine, called galinpepimut-S (GPS), reduced the risk of death by 41% compared with the best available treatment in a study involving 126 patients, the company said.

Patients who received GPS recorded a median overall survival of 24 months, against 14.7 months among those in the control group.

Trading in Sellas shares was halted during premarket hours following the sharp rise.

Vaccine shows survival benefit in AML patients

The trial evaluated GPS in patients with AML who had achieved remission following cancer treatment but were unable to undergo a bone marrow or stem cell transplant.

AML is an aggressive cancer affecting the blood and bone marrow.

Patients whose disease returns after treatment often have limited therapeutic options, making the development of treatments that can prolong survival particularly important.

GPS is designed to train the immune system to identify and attack residual leukemia cells carrying a protein known as WT1.

Sellas said the vaccine was generally well tolerated and did not raise any new safety concerns.

Most reported side effects were mild to moderate, with injection-site reactions being the most common.

"The magnitude of the survival benefit observed with our investigational GPS immunotherapeutic cancer vaccine represents a defining milestone for Sellas," CEO Angelos Stergiou said.

The scale of the potential patient population is significant.

According to the American Cancer Society, about 22,720 people in the US are expected to be diagnosed with AML in 2026, while approximately 11,500 are projected to die from the disease, Reuters reported.

AML accounts for one in three adult leukemia cases.

Sellas targets FDA discussions and 2027 filing

Sellas plans to meet with the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to discuss the trial findings and an accelerated regulatory strategy.

The company is preparing for a Biologics License Application (BLA) submission in the first half of 2027.

"Given the significant unmet need in this patient population, we look forward to engaging with the FDA to discuss the results and the regulatory path forward, with the goal of making this therapy available to patients as rapidly as possible," Stergiou said.

The regulatory discussions will be an important next step as the company seeks to translate the trial results into a potential treatment option.

The findings do not, however, mean that GPS has received regulatory approval.

Company advances another leukemia drug candidate

The latest development comes as Sellas continues to advance its broader oncology pipeline.

Earlier this month, the company reported a net loss of $10.1 million, or $0.05 per share, compared with a loss of $6.8 million, or $0.06 per share, a year earlier.

Sellas reported no revenue, in line with analyst expectations.

Its smaller loss per share came despite the increase in its overall loss, as weighted-average shares outstanding rose to approximately 202.4 million from 108.4 million.

Last week, Sellas also said that 40 patients had enrolled in an 80-patient Phase 2 trial of tambiciclib, also known as SLS009, in newly diagnosed AML.

Preliminary results are expected in the fourth quarter.

Separately, the company plans to present completed Phase 2 findings for SLS009 in relapsed or refractory leukemia at the American Society of Hematology meeting in December.

Sellas has reported response rates of 54% among patients with monocytic disease and 57% among those with TP53-mutated disease.

The GPS results have given Sellas a significant clinical milestone, although the company's next challenge will be securing a regulatory pathway for the vaccine and demonstrating that the survival benefit can support its eventual approval.

headline: Why is Intel stock falling on Tuesday?
html_content:
Intel shares INTC fell more than 2% at Tuesday's market open after a regulatory filing revealed that Nvidia had reduced its stake in the chipmaker by 25% in the third quarter, adding to pressure on a stock already struggling with concerns over its turnaround.

The decline extended Monday's losses, when Intel shares dropped more than 7% amid a broader selloff in chip stocks.

The stock also came under pressure on Monday following reports of a shareholder lawsuit accusing the company of concealing the impact of a prolonged slowdown in personal computer sales.

The complaint alleges that the disclosures led to investor losses when Intel's shares plunged nearly 29% in a single day.

Nvidia cuts Intel stake, increases SpaceX holding

According to Nvidia's latest 13F filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, the company sold approximately 53.69 million Intel shares during the third quarter, reducing its holding to 161.1 million shares as of September 30, from 214.8 million at the end of June.

At the same time, Nvidia increased its SpaceX holding to 130.5 million shares from 122.8 million.

The move made SpaceX its largest disclosed equity investment, with the stake valued at approximately $19.7 billion at the end of September, slightly above the $19.4 billion value of its remaining Intel position.

The two investments account for more than 80% of Nvidia's disclosed $48.3 billion portfolio, underscoring the concentration of its equity holdings.

Nvidia also reduced its investments in Nokia and Synopsys by 56% and 10%, respectively.

It maintained its positions in CoreWeave, Coherent, Nebius Group and Generate Biomedicines.

The reduction in Intel's stake comes as other major investors have taken a different view.

Soros Fund Management, the family office of billionaire George Soros, built a position of 2.83 million Intel shares worth $340.3 million in the third quarter, according to its latest regulatory filing.

The fund had held only 100,000 shares at the end of June.

Weak PC demand delays Intel turnaround

Intel has faced mounting pressure after warning of significant cash burn this year, driven by a weakening PC market, manufacturing bottlenecks and heavy investment in expanding production capacity.

The stock has lost about 40% over the past month, although it remains up roughly 40% year to date.

Bank of America recently downgraded Intel to Neutral from Buy and lowered its price target to $100 from $145, citing weaker PC shipments and supply constraints that have pushed back the company's recovery.

The downgrade followed Intel's third-quarter results, which included a disappointing outlook and triggered a post-earnings share decline of more than 25%.

Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analysts' expectations of $17.08 billion.

At the midpoint, the guidance implies a shortfall of about 9%.

The company also projected adjusted earnings of $0.25 per share, compared with the consensus estimate of $0.44.

"In our view, the stock has not communicated enough traction with external foundry customers, while its data center strength is offset by a surprisingly sharp drop in PC shipments (down 25-30% QoQ in Q4, further inventory correction expected in 1H27)," analyst Vivek Arya wrote.

The latest reduction by Nvidia adds another concern for Intel investors as the company tries to convince the market that its manufacturing expansion and turnaround strategy can deliver sustainable growth.

headline: AMD shares open higher on Tuesday: here's why
html_content:
AMD shares opened higher on Tuesday as semiconductor stocks staged a modest rebound following a bruising session a day earlier.

The stock gained roughly 0.5% in early trading, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index also moved into positive territory, up 0.6%.

The recovery provided some support to the broader chip sector, even as Nvidia remained under pressure ahead of its third-quarter earnings report, due after the market close.

However, gains remained limited amid persistent concerns about AI valuations and the sustainability of heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

At the time of publication, the stock had pared gains and was up only 0.27% as broader market sentiment weighed in. However, AMD investors still had some good news to factor in.

AMD expands AI capabilities with acquisitions

AMD has been advancing its AI strategy through a series of acquisitions and partnerships.

The company closed its roughly $8.2 billion all-stock acquisition of World Labs, the AI research firm founded by Fei-Fei Li.

The deal adds expertise in spatial intelligence, computer vision and 3D world models. Li will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist.

CEO Lisa Su said the combination would help the company "optimize compute platforms and models together" for the open AI ecosystem.

Separately, AMD completed its acquisition of Taalas, a specialist in AI inference silicon.

The technology is expected to be incorporated into AMD's accelerator roadmap and system-level offerings alongside Instinct GPUs, EPYC processors, ROCm software and the Helios rack-scale platform.

AMD said the acquisition would strengthen its ability to deliver differentiated performance and efficiency for specialized inference workloads while expanding its engineering presence in Canada.

AMD also received a boost from news that TensorWave, an AMD-backed AI cloud provider, had signed a six-year agreement to supply OpenAI with 457 megawatts of dedicated computing capacity.

The infrastructure will run on AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs housed in Helios racks. Capacity is expected to begin coming online in the first half of 2027, with full deployment targeted for early 2028.

The agreement is the first publicly named neocloud arrangement under the broader OpenAI-AMD partnership and highlights the growing demand for AMD's AI infrastructure.

Analysts remain bullish on AMD

Analyst sentiment remains strong, with firms pointing to AMD's competitive position and growth prospects in server CPUs and AI accelerators.

William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform last Thursday, although it did not assign a price target. The firm said the risk-reward profile had shifted in the company's favor.

The brokerage noted that Intel's Xeon roadmap continued to face delays and supply shortages, while the shift toward Arm-based hosts had proved less decisive than previously expected.

It also highlighted that AMD's valuation multiple had declined even as earnings estimates moved higher.

"We see a runway for shares to work from here, with Instinct share gains offering additional upside as AMD stays focused on execution while its largest competitor, Nvidia, contends with a growing leadership and regulatory imbroglio," William Blair analyst Sebastien Naji wrote in a note to clients.

Naji added that the Lisa Su-led company was "in the early innings of a multiyear earnings growth trajectory as it continues to execute in server CPUs."

Oppenheimer also upgraded Advanced Micro Devices to Outperform from Perform and assigned the stock a price target of $600.

headline: Coherent, Lumentum stocks gain on Tuesday: here’s why
html_content:
Shares of US optical technology companies rallied on Tuesday after reports that the Trump administration plans to proceed with restrictions on imports of Chinese data centre equipment, despite opposition from major US technology companies.

Coherent Corp. shares COHR rose 3%, while Lumentum Holdings climbed 2.2% and Corning advanced 1.4%.

The proposed restrictions target new models of Chinese optical transceivers, which transmit data over fibre-optic cables within data centres, reported Reuters.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has raised national security concerns, arguing that the equipment could potentially be used to steal data, install malware or disrupt US data centre operations.

According to the Reuters report, the initiative is moving forward despite lobbying by Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave, Cisco and Microsoft.

The companies reportedly warned White House officials that replacing Chinese suppliers could take up to a decade, highlighting the challenges facing US data centre operators.

US technology companies raise concerns over restrictions

The proposed measure has faced resistance from some of the largest US technology companies, which rely on optical equipment from Chinese manufacturers.

Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave and Cisco joined Microsoft in discussions with White House officials earlier this year.

Executives reportedly highlighted the time required to comply with a potential mandate and the difficulty of replacing existing suppliers.

The lobbying had raised doubts about whether the restrictions would proceed.

However, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the initiative was moving forward.

The latest push for restrictions comes amid renewed concerns in Washington about Chinese technology and potential security threats.

Revelations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reported affair with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Beijing have added to calls for a tougher approach.

The White House declined to comment on the lobbying or the measure's progress.

However, an official said recent FCC actions restricting Chinese and other foreign equipment had resulted in billions of dollars in US manufacturing investment and thousands of new American jobs.

China dominates the optical transceiver market

China accounts for approximately two-thirds of the global optical transceiver market, according to Counterpoint Research.

Chinese manufacturers, including Eoptolink and Zhongji Innolight, dominate global supply and count major US hyperscalers among their customers.

US-based Coherent and Lumentum also manufacture competing optical technology.

However, a report by the Foundation for American Innovation found that they currently lack the scale to fully replace Chinese suppliers.

This concentration could create challenges for US data centre operators if restrictions force them to shift orders to domestic manufacturers.

It could also provide an opportunity for American suppliers to expand their market share.

However, the industry has raised concerns about possible retaliation from Beijing.

US companies reportedly warned officials that China could restrict exports of indium phosphide, a critical material used to manufacture optical transceivers.

Such restrictions could complicate efforts by US manufacturers to increase production and replace Chinese suppliers.

FCC restrictions extend beyond data centre equipment

The proposed optical transceiver restrictions would follow several similar measures introduced by the FCC over the past year.

The regulator has already moved to block imports of new models of Chinese drones, robots, power inverters and routers.

The broader policy push comes as the Trump administration balances its approach to China with ongoing disputes over technology and critical materials.

Beijing has previously imposed export controls on rare-earth minerals, which are important to technology manufacturing.

The latest developments could benefit US optical equipment manufacturers if data centre operators are required to source more equipment domestically.

However, China's dominant position in the market and the potential for export restrictions on key materials remain significant challenges for the industry.

headline: Why SpaceX stock is rising on Tuesday?
html_content:
SpaceX shares rose on Tuesday even as the broader market remained under pressure.

The stock gained over 2% at 11:00 AM EST and was trading at $140.26, recovering ground after being under pressure in the previous two sessions.

The gains came as broader technology shares faced pressure and the controversy-hit Nvidia remained in focus ahead of its earnings report later in the day.

$40 billion AI financing deal supports SpaceX expansion

A key driver was a report that Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management are preparing to underwrite and sell portions of roughly $40 billion in debt financing earmarked for Nvidia's next-generation AI chips.

Bloomberg reported that part of the package could begin hitting the market as soon as this week.

The financing structure routes the obligation through a special-purpose vehicle managed by Apollo-backed entity Atlas SP. The vehicle will purchase the chips and issue asset-backed securities.

The arrangement is designed to keep the debt off SpaceX's own balance sheet while allowing the company to rapidly expand its AI computing capacity.

The chips, expected to be delivered in the first half of 2027, will support SpaceX's terrestrial computing buildout and related Super Intelligence infrastructure.

The financing has been described as one of the largest GPU-related deals on record.

Adding to the positive sentiment, Nvidia disclosed that it had increased its stake in SpaceX to 130.5 million shares, providing another signal of confidence from one of the company's most prominent technology partners.

Starship Flight 15 draws bullish analyst commentary

SpaceX also received support from analysts following Starship Flight 15 over the weekend.

The mission achieved the first-ever recovery of an orbital-class upper stage, with the launch tower's mechanical arms successfully catching the returning Ship.

The achievement was widely viewed as a major milestone in the company's efforts to make Starship fully reusable.

Morgan Stanley reiterated its Overweight rating on SpaceX on Tuesday and encouraged investors to keep buying the stock.

However, the bank noted that the market's muted response to the successful mission reflected lingering concerns about SpaceX's business model, AI and neocloud ambitions, customer concentration and strategy involving Tesla.

"The market's reaction to a near flawless Flight 15 and historic ship catch? Meh," the analysts wrote. They added that investors were not necessarily indifferent to the achievement but remained focused on the uncertainties surrounding the company's broader strategy.

Cantor Fitzgerald also reiterated its Overweight rating and $345 price target.

The firm argued that the successful catch provides a clearer pathway toward improved free cash flow, a higher launch cadence and faster satellite deployments.

Citi was similarly bullish. Analyst John Godyn said in a Monday note to clients that Flight 15, particularly the successful recovery of Starship using the Mechazilla arms, represented one of the key milestones along a multiyear path toward the bank's upside scenario of more than $900 per share.

The analyst also said the mission had strengthened the firm's conviction in the outlook for SpaceX's Super Intelligence business.

"We walked away from the event with greater conviction in the outlook for the company’s Super Intelligence segment as well," Godyn said.

Citi maintained its Buy rating and raised its price target to $280 from $240.

headline: Nike outlines $5B growth plan as turnaround faces challenges in China and sportswear
html_content:
Nike unveiled a long-term strategy aimed at restoring sustainable growth and improving profitability.

The plan, called “Full Stride Ahead”, focuses on concentrating investments in key sports, brands and markets while reducing costs and streamlining operations.

The company outlined the strategy at its Investor Day, setting preliminary financial targets for fiscal 2031.

Nike aims to generate $5 billion in additional annual revenue by the end of that financial year, using fiscal 2027 as its starting point.

Although the stock gained initially, it gave up most of the gains and was trading at 0.02% at the time of writing.

The stock has fallen approximately 37% this year, including Tuesday's gains, as the company continues to face challenges in China and its sportswear business.

Nike focuses on five core sports and three lifestyle brands

Under the new strategy, Nike plans to concentrate resources on five core sports: running, training, global football, basketball and outdoor activities.

It will also prioritise three lifestyle businesses: Nike Sportswear, Jordan and Converse.

The company expects these categories, across 23 priority countries, to account for more than 90% of its revenue growth through 2031.

Performance sports are expected to contribute approximately $4 billion of the targeted $5 billion in additional revenue.

The remaining $1 billion is expected to come from the sportswear business.

Nike plans to introduce more new products and strengthen the cultural relevance of its lifestyle brands.

It also intends to position Jordan as a more premium brand and sharpen Converse's focus on lifestyle offerings.

Chief Executive Elliott Hill said the company was concentrating resources on areas with the greatest growth potential.

He added that Nike was changing its operating model to deliver new products, build stronger local connections and respond more quickly to demand.

Cost reductions and AI to support turnaround

Nike plans to simplify its organisation, improve supply chain flexibility and accelerate product innovation as part of the strategy.

The company also intends to use artificial intelligence and data to improve decision-making and streamline operations.

These measures are expected to help it respond more effectively to consumer demand while improving productivity.

Nike aims to reduce annual costs by $2.5 billion by 2031.

However, the restructuring is expected to involve approximately $1.3 billion in pretax charges.

The company also plans to return around $12 billion to shareholders through dividends over the five-year period.

For fiscal 2027, it expects to distribute approximately $2.4 billion in dividends.

The strategy builds on Hill's ongoing turnaround efforts, which have included rebuilding relationships with retailers after Nike shifted towards direct-to-consumer sales.

The company has also been reducing costs through cuts to warehouse and corporate roles.

Nike maintains cautious fiscal 2027 outlook

Despite its longer-term ambitions, Nike expects another difficult year in fiscal 2027.

The company reaffirmed its forecast for revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range.

Operating income is expected to fall faster than revenue, resulting in an adjusted operating margin of approximately 6%.

Nike forecasts adjusted earnings per share of between $1.15 and $1.35, compared with the analyst consensus estimate of $1.28.

The company expects revenue declines to moderate in the following financial year before returning to market-level growth.

It then anticipates faster growth as investments in its priority categories begin to contribute.

By fiscal 2031, Nike is targeting adjusted earnings per share of $3 to $3.50 and an operating margin of 12% to 14%.

The targets provide a longer-term framework for the turnaround, although the company will need to address its current challenges in China and lifestyle products while executing its cost-reduction and growth plans.

headline: Jensen Huang keeps door open to return as Nvidia CEO in first statement since exit
html_content:
Jensen Huang has signaled that he would be willing to return as Nvidia NVDA CEO if the company's board of directors decides that his reinstatement would be in the company's best interest.

In his first public statement since stepping down, Huang said he took full responsibility for his personal mistakes and would cooperate with the board's independent investigation.

The statement came hours before Nvidia was scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings following the closing bell on Tuesday.

Nvidia shares continued their descent on Tuesday, falling 1.43% at the time of writing.

The 63-year-old resigned last week after leading the chipmaker since its founding in 1993.

His departure followed reports that he had been involved in multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence.

What Jensen Huang said

In a statement posted on X, Huang acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected of Nvidia employees and said he regretted the problems it had caused the board.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang said.

"I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation," he added.

Huang, one of the most prominent figures in the artificial intelligence industry, also thanked employees, investors, business partners and others who had reached out to him and his family over the past week.

"Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me," he wrote.

Huang says he would be honoured to return

The former CEO said he had received calls from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers urging him to return to the company's top position.

He added that people had continued to contact him directly as Nvidia navigated technological, competitive, market and geopolitical challenges.

"NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang said.

Nvidia appointed former CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO following Huang's departure.

However, CNBC and Reuters reported on Tuesday that the board was unlikely to reinstate him.

Huang to testify on December 1

Meanwhile, Huang has agreed to appear before Congress on December 1 for a transcribed interview involving the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee.

The committees said they wanted answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese entities access to advanced US chips and the alleged involvement of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in the controversy.

"The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia's role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal," Republican committee chairmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford said in a joint statement.

headline: Micron stock falls 2%, why this analyst cut target price
html_content:
Micron Technology shares MU fell more than 2% on Tuesday as investors assessed concerns about a potential oversupply in the NAND memory market next year.

GF Securities lowered its NAND price forecasts, warning that weaker consumer demand and slower server deployments could reverse the current supply-demand balance.

The Hong Kong-based investment firm expects NAND prices to remain flat in the first quarter of 2027 before declining in the following three quarters.

Its previous forecasts had called for price increases of 6% in the first quarter, 3% in the second quarter, and no change in the final two quarters.

The revised outlook also put other memory-chip companies in focus, including SanDisk and South Korea's SK Hynix.

GF Securities warns of NAND market oversupply

GF Securities expects weaker demand for smartphones and personal computers to weigh on NAND consumption in 2027.

The firm projects double-digit shipment declines for both product categories, putting pressure on client solid-state drives and mobile storage demand.

Analysts also pointed to constraints in the availability of graphics processing units and high-bandwidth memory, which have slowed server deployment momentum.

This has weakened procurement demand for enterprise solid-state drives, partly offsetting increased orders from US cloud service providers in September.

In a note to clients, GF Securities said these factors were easing the supply constraints that had previously supported NAND prices.

The firm also expects NAND demand bit growth to decline next year, reaching 47.8 exabytes.

It cited weaker consumer electronics demand and slower procurement of enterprise storage products in China.

On the supply side, Chinese manufacturers are continuing to expand capacity, while the share of quad-level cell (QLC) production is increasing.

GF Securities forecasts NAND supply bit growth of 21% in 2026, 28% in 2027 and 30% in 2028.

The combination of slower demand and expanding supply could result in a reversal of the market's supply-demand balance, putting further pressure on prices.

SanDisk faces greater earnings volatility than Micron

GF Securities sees SanDisk as more exposed to the potential downturn because it is a pure-play NAND manufacturer.

The analysts expect its earnings to experience greater volatility if NAND prices weaken.

Separately, recent regulatory filings revealed a significant change in Micron's institutional shareholder base.

The completion of the sale could reduce some of the trading volatility associated with the fund's exposure to memory stocks.

headline: Nebius stock is falling: Here’s why NBIS may plunge to $50 soon
html_content:
Nebius Group stock continues its strong downward trend, reaching a low of $102, its lowest level since April 6 this year. NBIS has slumped by over 64% from its all-time high, with its market capitalization falling from over $75.7 billion in August to the current $29.29 billion. This retreat may continue as concerns about the industry remains.

Nebius Group under pressure as AI jitters remain

NBIS stock continues its strong freefall as investors remain pessimistic about the industry escalated. These concerns rose amid the ongoing challenges at Nvidia, a company that evolved into the central bank of the AI industry.

Huang’s exit presents a big challenge for the industry because of the role he played at Nvidia, including by leading investments in neocloud companies, including Nebius, CoreWeave, and IREN. 

There are also concerns about the artificial intelligence (AI) bubble, which some analysts believe will burst soon, especially as interest rates jump. Some popular analysts like Ken Griffin and Ray dalio have warned that the bubble could burst. The AI Stock Index has moved to the extreme zone of 72.

Nebius is also facing other challenges. Meta Platforms, its top client, has announced that it plans to lease its extra storage to other customers. Microsoft, another top client, has started to reassess its relationships with Nebius and other neocloud companies, citing project delays and costs. 

There is a risk that the company has not announced major deals with hyperscalers recently. One of this is the fact that the industry has become highly saturated, with hundreds of neoclouds. For example, Nscale has landed large deals with Anthropic. Other top companies in the industry are SpaceX, Riot Platforms, and MARA Holdings. 

Additionally, there are concerns about future spending as clients start prioritizing newer chips from companies like Nvidia and Google. Gartner has estimated that neocloud companies will need to announce substantial impairments in the next few years.

Nebius slashed its guidance

NBIS stock has also dropped because of the recent earnings report, in which management slashed the forward guidance. The company expects that its revenue will be in the low end of its $3.0 billion and $3.4 billion range. In the statement, the management cited the fact that a portion of this year’s revenue moving into the first part of next year.

The management also refuted the fears that demand is fading. It pointed to the fact that its customers had committed over $12 billion in contract value in the third quarter of the year. It is also using customer prepayments to fund most of its operations.

The results showed that its revenue rose by 571% in the third quarter to $980 million, with its nine-month figure hitting $1.962 billion. This revenue included $325 million of non-recurring revenue. Excluding this, its third quarter revenue was $655 million.

Analysts still expect that Nebius Group’s business will continue to thrive over time. Kyro AI data shows that the annual revenue will be $3.17 billion this year, followed by $12.32 billion next year. 

Nebius Group stock technical analysis

NBIS stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that NBIS stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has already dropped below the important support level of $145.20, its lowest level on July 29 this year. 

The stock has dropped below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level. Falling below that retracement often confirms a bearish breakout. It has remained below the 50-day and 100-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA).

The Average Directional Index (ADX) has jumped to 36, a sign that the sell-off is gaining momentum. Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the psychological level of $50.

headline: Salesforce stock slides as technology outages rattle software sector
html_content:
Salesforce shares CRM fell more than 8% on Tuesday as a series of high-profile technology outages heightened investor concerns about software reliability and security, weighing on the broader software sector.

The stock's decline put it on track for its lowest close since August 17 and its biggest one-day percentage decline since May 2024.

Other software companies also came under pressure.

ServiceNow shares fell 6.12%, Datadog declined 5%, and Workday lost 4.15%.

Intuit, the maker of TurboTax, dropped 5.19%.

The declines came amid a growing number of technology disruptions affecting government agencies, airlines, banks and businesses.

Although there is no publicly established link between the outages and the software companies whose shares fell, investors are increasingly concerned about the sector's exposure to technology and security risks.

NSA communications outage adds to technology concerns

The latest disruption involved a highly classified communications network used by the US National Security Agency for internal communications.

CNN reported on Tuesday that the network was down, with the agency working to understand the scope of the problem.

The report said there was no immediate evidence of a cyberattack.

The incident followed a series of outages across other parts of the US technology infrastructure, including aviation and banking services.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria said the recent disruptions had increased investor concerns about software security, even though the companies experiencing share price declines were not publicly connected to the incidents.

“The concern is that it is possible bad actors are using AI tools to cause harm and that software companies are particularly vulnerable,” Luria said.

His comments highlight concerns that artificial intelligence tools could potentially increase security risks for software providers, although the reported outages have not been attributed to AI-related attacks.

Airline and banking disruptions add to investor jitters

The NSA incident came after a nationwide ground stop disrupted US air travel late last Friday.

The Federal Aviation Administration had cited a communication issue affecting air traffic control centres, alongside extraordinary circumstances.

The government lifted the ground stop after several hours, but thousands of flights were delayed or cancelled.

Airline disruptions continued into Monday, when United Airlines said it had resolved a system outage that had delayed some flights.

Meanwhile, customers of major US banks and peer-to-peer payment service Zelle reported service disruptions on Monday.

The incidents affected access to banking services and contributed to declines in bank shares.

The banking problems followed a widespread Microsoft outage that began on Thursday and disrupted services used by businesses.

Microsoft said the incident was caused by a technical issue and was not related to cyberattacks or artificial intelligence agents.

US officials say banking system remains secure

The succession of outages has raised questions about the reliability of technology infrastructure supporting critical services.

However, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on Monday that the incidents did not indicate a broader threat to national security or the banking system.

“Well, breathe. The homeland is secure. Our banking system is secure and when something like this happens, we’re able to react and react fast,” Mullin said during an appearance on Fox News' “Hannity”.

Mullin also said the incidents were unrelated.

For investors, the immediate concern remains whether the disruptions will lead to greater scrutiny of software security and reliability.

headline: Netflix stock analysis: what next for this fallen angel?
html_content:
Netflix extended its steep sell-off, with the once-hot media company now a fallen angel. The stock dropped to $59.65, its lowest level since August 2024, and has plunged 55% from its all-time high. Its market capitalization has fallen from a peak of $568 billion to $244 billion, a loss of $324 billion. The decline may continue as the company transitions from a growth stock to a value stock.

Netflix has evolved from growth to value

Netflix, a member of the FAANG group of companies, has become a fallen angel. In finance, the term refers to a company that was once a market darling but has lost its shine over the years.

Netflix’s business is facing major challenges as its revenue growth slows and engagements slow. Engagements is a major issue, especially now that the company is becoming a major player in the advertising space. 

The most recent results showed that Netflix’s business continued experiencing double digit growth, but this trend is highly unlikely to continue. Its revenue rose by 12%, mirroring its forward guidance.

READ MORE: Netflix stock is falling after earnings: why Morningstar sees it rising 30%

The revenue rose to $12.8 billion, with its operating margin rising to 34.6%. The management expects that its fourth quarter revenue will be $13.4 billion, representing a 11.58% from a year earlier. If this view is correct, its annual revenue will come in at $51.12 billion, up by 13% from a year earlier.

Yahoo Finance data also expects that its annual revenue will jump by 1o% to $56.6 billion next year. After that, after the company is expected to grow by single-digits, making it a value company. 

Netflix is struggling to supercharge its growth, which explains why the management attempted to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. Some of its main options for growing its business are increasing prices and expanding its advertising services. It is also moving more into gaming and sports.

Netflix is still overvalued

There are also signs that Netflix is relatively overvalued. Kyro AI data shows that the forward non-GAAP price-to-earnings ratio stands at 17, higher than the communications sector average of 13. The GAAP metric of 16.95 is also higher than the communications sector of 14.

The same trend is happening with the Rule-of-40 metric, which looks at a company’s revenue growth and profit margin. Netflix has a forward revenue growth of 12% and a profit margin of 27%, giving it a multiple of 38%.

Analysts have scaled back their NFLX stock forecasts. Philip Securities downgraded the stock from strong buy to moderate buy. Argus slashed the stock target from $120 to $95, while Citigroup slashed it from $100 to $95. 

Netflix stock price technical analysis

NFLX stock chart | Source: TradingView

The weekly chart shows that the NFLX stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has slumped from $134 in June last year to the current $59.6. The stock has formed a series of lower lows and lower highs. 

Most notably, it is about to form a death cross pattern as the spread between the 50-week and 200-week moving averages narrow. A death cross pattern often leads to more downside over time. 

The stock has also dropped below the important support level of $64.82, invalidating the double-bottom pattern. Most notably, it has just dropped below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level. 

Therefore, the path of the least resistance for the stock is bearish, with the next key target being at $50. A drop below that level will point to more downside towards the 78.6% retracement level of $41.

headline: Evening digest: Huang says he is prepared to return, Anthropic wins first buy rating
html_content:
Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return as Nvidia CEO if the company's board considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest.

Anthropic has received its first Wall Street Buy rating ahead of its planned stock market debut, with New Street Research setting a $105 price target.

Gold prices edged higher but remained close to a 13-month low as a stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields weighed on demand.

Oil prices gained around 1% as concerns about attacks on shipping in the Middle East offset expectations of a global supply surplus.

Jensen Huang issues first statement after Nvidia departure

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said he would be prepared to return to the company if its board of directors decides that his reinstatement would benefit shareholders, employees and the business.

In his first public statement since stepping down, Huang took responsibility for his personal conduct and said he would cooperate with an independent investigation by the board.

Huang said he had not met the standards expected of Nvidia employees and regretted the problems his actions had created for the board.

He also thanked employees, investors, business partners and others who had supported him and his family over the past week.

The 63-year-old resigned last week after leading Nvidia since its founding in 1993.

His departure followed reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one involving a woman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence.

Huang said he had received calls from employees, investors, business partners and customers urging him to return.

However, CNBC reported on Tuesday that Nvidia's board was unlikely to reinstate him.

Former CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO.

Huang has also agreed to appear before Congress on December 1 for a transcribed interview involving three House committees.

Lawmakers are seeking answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese entities access to advanced US chips and the alleged involvement of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in the controversy.

Nvidia shares were down 1.6% on Tuesday ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings report, scheduled for after the market close.

Anthropic receives first Buy rating ahead of IPO

Anthropic has received a bullish assessment from New Street Research ahead of its planned initial public offering.

Analyst Pierre Ferragu initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $105 price target, above the company's proposed IPO range of $70 to $78.

The analyst described the listing as a “generational IPO”, arguing that artificial intelligence could capture a growing share of corporate spending.

Ferragu compared the potential expansion of AI with cloud computing, which accounted for around 30% of incremental IT spending between 2010 and 2025.

He believes AI could spread twice as quickly across an addressable market ten times larger.

His forecasts suggest AI could account for nearly 7% of knowledge-work spending by 2030, with around 25% of incremental spending directed towards the technology through 2040.

However, the analyst's projections relate to the broader AI market and do not establish how much of that opportunity Anthropic will capture.

Ferragu also argued that the proposed IPO valuation offers a degree of downside protection.

His $105 target implies approximately 35% upside from the top of the proposed price range.

Gold falls as dollar and Treasury yields weigh

Gold prices were mixed on Tuesday. However, they remained near their lowest level in 13 months as investors assessed the outlook for US interest rates.

Spot gold fell 0.09% to $3,852.67 per ounce, barely above Monday's low of $3,830.74.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.07% to $3,856.

The US dollar remained near its highest level in 19 months, while benchmark 10-year Treasury yields climbed amid expectations of further interest rate increases.

Markets were assigning a 95.4% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Investors were also awaiting minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, due on Wednesday.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday that the central bank may need several rate increases to bring inflation under control.

Rising interest rates tend to reduce gold's appeal because the metal does not generate interest income.

headline: Why this analyst sees a 30% upside for Meta stock?
html_content:
Meta Platforms shares META edged lower on Tuesday, falling 0.65%, despite receiving a bullish assessment from UBS.

Analyst Karl Keirstead initiated coverage with a Buy rating and an $815 price target, arguing that growing enthusiasm around the company's artificial intelligence initiatives could offset concerns about rising investment costs and financing requirements.

Keirstead believes Meta's Muse AI models and Meta Business Agents could strengthen investor sentiment as the company expands its AI strategy.

The analyst's price target implies approximately 30% upside from Monday's closing price.

The UBS assessment comes as Meta increases spending on computing infrastructure and AI development, raising questions about its ability to sustain investment while maintaining positive cash flow.

UBS sees upside from Meta's AI strategy

Keirstead said Meta trades at approximately 20 times estimated 2027 GAAP earnings per share, a valuation he considers attractive given recent progress in its AI models and applications.

The analyst described CEO Mark Zuckerberg and the company's leadership as building an “AI maximalist version of Meta” following a significant overhaul of its AI strategy over the past 18 months.

UBS plans to focus on three main areas as it evaluates the company's progress: the development and training of Muse AI models, the rollout of Meta's personal AI agent, and the expansion of business and enterprise applications.

The firm will also assess the computing infrastructure needed to support these initiatives, including the scale of investment and associated costs.

UBS said its existing coverage of cloud infrastructure providers would help inform its analysis of Meta's AI spending.

These companies include Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Oracle and CoreWeave.

Keirstead's assessment suggests that the commercial potential of Meta's AI products could become an important factor in how investors evaluate the company's expanding investment programme.

Rising capital expenditure weighs on cash flow

Meta's AI ambitions come with substantial infrastructure costs, which have become a key concern for investors.

The company reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year.

Advertising remained an important contributor to growth, with impressions increasing 10% and average advertising prices rising 14%.

However, capital expenditure reached $34.91 billion during the quarter. Meta also reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion.

The figures highlight the financial pressure associated with the company's investment plans.

While revenue growth remained strong, spending on infrastructure and other investments exceeded the cash generated after capital expenditure during the quarter.

UBS acknowledged that mounting capital expenditure, negative free cash flow and the potential need for additional financing could weigh on investor sentiment.

The analyst nevertheless believes enthusiasm around Meta's AI products and applications could help counter these concerns.

Meta expects aggressive AI investment in 2027

Meta expects its capital expenditure to remain elevated as it continues expanding its AI infrastructure.

The company forecasts fiscal 2026 capital expenditure of between $135 billion and $145 billion.

It narrowed the range from its previous forecast of $130 billion to $145 billion.

Management has also indicated that investment in the core business and emerging AI initiatives will continue aggressively in 2027.

headline: Nvidia stock rises after hours as revenue forecast beats estimates
html_content:
Nvidia shares NVDA rose 2.47% in after-hours trading on Tuesday after the chipmaker delivered a stronger-than-expected revenue forecast for its January quarter, signalling that demand for artificial intelligence hardware remains robust despite leadership uncertainty and concerns about industry spending.

The company forecast revenue of $130 billion for its fiscal fourth quarter, plus or minus 3%, compared with the $125.3 billion expected by analysts tracked by FactSet.

The outlook does not include any data-centre revenue from China.

The forecast followed another record quarter for Nvidia, with revenue and earnings both exceeding Wall Street expectations.

Investors had been closely watching the results amid the departure of longtime CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week following reports about his personal relationships.

Nvidia delivers stronger-than-expected revenue outlook

Nvidia expects revenue of approximately $130 billion in the quarter ending in January.

The forecast exceeded analyst expectations and suggests that demand for the company's AI chips and computing systems remains strong.

The company also expects a gross margin of around 71.5% in the quarter.

The outlook was particularly important given speculation about whether Nvidia would provide a quarterly forecast amid the uncertainty surrounding its leadership.

Nvidia's third-quarter revenue increased 103% year-over-year to $115.8 billion, surpassing the approximately $109 billion expected by analysts.

Net income reached $65.3 billion, while earnings per share came in at $2.68, above the FactSet consensus estimate of $2.48.

Demand for Nvidia's AI hardware remained strong during the quarter as the company began shipments of its latest Vera Rubin systems.

The results provide further evidence of continued investment in AI infrastructure, although concerns remain about whether spending across the industry can maintain its current pace.

Nvidia returns record $28.1 billion to shareholders

Nvidia returned $28.1 billion to shareholders during the quarter ended October 25 through share repurchases and dividends.

The figure exceeded the previous quarterly record of $26 billion, set in the preceding quarter.

Share buybacks accounted for $22.1 billion of the latest shareholder returns.

Nvidia has now spent $62 billion on repurchases during the first three quarters of its fiscal year, significantly more than the $40.4 billion spent during the previous fiscal year.

The company still has $227.3 billion available under its existing share repurchase programme.

The scale of the buybacks highlights Nvidia's ability to return substantial capital to shareholders while continuing to invest in its AI hardware business.

Leadership uncertainty remains after Huang's departure

Nvidia's strong results came during a period of significant leadership uncertainty.

Huang resigned last Thursday following reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one involving a company employee and another involving a woman suspected by US officials of having links to Chinese intelligence.

Former CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while Nvidia looks for a permanent replacement.

The company has also elevated board member Harvey Jones to chairman, marking the first time Nvidia has had someone in that role.

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be willing to return if the board decided that his reinstatement would be in the company's best interests.

However, a person familiar with the board's thinking told Wall Street Journal that it was not considering bringing him back.

Nvidia's board has also formed a committee to oversee national security policies and compliance with US export controls.

Huang and General Counsel Tim Teter have agreed to brief three House committees in early December as lawmakers seek answers about the company's exports to Asia.

headline: Bitcoin stalls below $65k as bears maintain control
html_content:
Bitcoin (BTC) continued to struggle on Wednesday as the cryptocurrency market showed limited signs of recovering from last week's sharp sell-off.

Bitcoin trades around $64,620, consolidating below the psychological $65,000 level as buyers struggle to regain control. 

Meanwhile, Ethereum and XRP are also facing resistance, reflecting persistent weakness across the largest cryptocurrencies.

Although Bitcoin's technical indicators suggest that selling pressure has become overstretched, the broader market structure remains bearish.

BTC continues to trade significantly below its major daily moving averages, while momentum indicators show little evidence of a sustained reversal.

The current setup suggests that any near-term recovery could remain a corrective rebound within the broader downtrend unless buyers reclaim important technical levels.

Bitcoin consolidates below $65,000

Bitcoin remained relatively subdued on Wednesday, trading around $64,620 after experiencing substantial losses during the previous week.

The cryptocurrency has struggled to recover above $65,000, suggesting that buyers remain hesitant to establish larger positions following the recent correction.

While consolidation can sometimes indicate that selling pressure is easing, it does not necessarily confirm that a market bottom has formed.

For Bitcoin, the broader technical structure continues to favor sellers. BTC remains well below its 50-day, 100-day, and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages, indicating weakness across short, medium, and longer-term trends.

The three moving averages are concentrated between approximately $75,700 and $76,000, forming a substantial resistance zone above the current market price.

This difference between Bitcoin's spot price and its major moving averages shows the extent of the recent sell-off.  It also suggests that a meaningful recovery would require stronger buying demand to overcome the technical barriers created during the sell-off.

For now, Bitcoin's inability to reclaim $65,000 reinforces the cautious outlook. Bitcoin's momentum indicators suggest that the cryptocurrency remains under significant selling pressure, although the decline may be becoming overstretched.

The daily Relative Strength Index stands near 23, placing BTC deep in oversold territory. An RSI reading below 30 generally indicates that selling pressure has been unusually strong relative to recent buying activity.

Meanwhile, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence indicator remains negative and depressed. This suggests that bearish momentum continues to dominate despite the possibility of a short-term rebound.

The combination of deeply oversold RSI conditions and negative MACD readings presents a challenging technical environment.

While a temporary recovery cannot be ruled out, the broader downtrend remains intact until buyers establish stronger momentum.

Bitcoin technical forecast: BTC faces major resistance near $76,000

Bitcoin faces several important technical barriers if buyers attempt to reverse the recent decline. The first significant resistance stands at the 200-day EMA near $75,723.

A sustained recovery above this level could encourage buyers to challenge the 50-day EMA around $75,767. Beyond this barrier, the 100-day EMA at $76,003 represents another important resistance level.

Together, these moving averages form a concentrated resistance zone that could limit any short-term recovery.

A decisive breakout above the $75,723–$76,003 resistance cluster would provide stronger evidence that bearish momentum is beginning to weaken. Beyond this zone, the next major resistance stands around $85,000.

On the downside, the primary support stands at $61,101. Failure to protect this support level could see Bitcoin drop below the $60,000 psychological level, with another demand zone around $57,000. 

Until Bitcoin reclaims its major moving averages, the technical outlook remains bearish.

headline: Why Samsung, SK Hynix shares rebounded on Wednesday?
html_content:
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix shares rebounded on Wednesday after several sessions of losses, as Nvidia's stronger-than-expected earnings helped restore confidence in the artificial intelligence trade.

Samsung Electronics climbed 2.31% to close at 194,700 won, while SK Hynix advanced 4.19% to 1.14 million won.

The gains followed a difficult start to the week. SK Hynix had fallen for four consecutive sessions, while Samsung had been in the red for three straight sessions.

The rebound helped lift South Korea's benchmark KOSPI, which rose 1.99% to finish at 5,067.44, reclaiming the 5,000 level after slipping below it in the previous session.

The junior KOSDAQ index also advanced, gaining more than 2% in early trading and holding on to its gains through the close.

Nvidia results revive confidence in AI demand

Controversy-hit Nvidia, the dominant supplier of AI accelerators, reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double its year-earlier figure and above analyst estimates of roughly $109 billion.

Adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.68, beating the consensus estimate of $2.47.

Nvidia expects revenue of approximately $130 billion in the quarter ending in January.

The forecast exceeded analyst expectations and suggests that demand for the company's AI chips and computing systems remains strong.

The company also expects a gross margin of around 71.5% in the quarter.

The results reinforced expectations that demand for AI computing infrastructure remains robust, despite recent uncertainty surrounding the company's leadership.

They also provided relief for South Korea's two largest memory chipmakers, which occupy a central position in the AI supply chain.

Samsung and SK Hynix are leading producers of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), a specialized form of DRAM stacked alongside processors to deliver the high data throughput required by modern AI training and inference systems.

SK Hynix has long been Nvidia's primary HBM supplier, while Samsung has been expanding its market share and securing additional contracts with other AI chip designers.

"Nvidia's results were reassuring and gave investors a reason to refocus on earnings, but they haven't resolved the broader questions around AI spending returns, financing sustainability and leadership uncertainty," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore told Reuters.

"So we are seeing an initial relief rally, but not necessarily the conviction needed for a sustained recovery."

Seo Sang-young, managing director of Mirae Asset Securities, told Maeil Business Newspaper that concerns remained over delays in data-center investment, weakness in US AI and semiconductor stocks, and export restrictions. However, he said the impact was limited because those concerns had already been reflected in the market.

Asian markets mixed

The rebound in South Korean chip stocks came as broader Asian markets showed a mixed response to Nvidia's results.

Japan's Nikkei 225 traded between modest gains and losses to close marginally higher, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng finished lower. China's Shanghai Composite also see-sawed to remain flat.

Taiwan's Taiex also showed early strength before giving back some of its gains.

Meanwhile, US stock index futures pointed higher during Asian trading.

S&P 500 futures rose around 0.25%, while Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.68%, suggesting that Nvidia's results could help stabilize the recent sell-off in technology shares.

Samsung Electronics climbed 2.31% to close at 194,700 won, while SK Hynix advanced 4.19% to 1.14 million won. The gains followed a difficult start to the week. SK Hynix had fallen for four consecutive sessions, while Samsung had been in the red for three straight sessions. The rebound helped lift South Korea's benchmark KOSPI, which rose 1.99% to finish at 5,067.44, reclaiming the 5,000 level after slipping below it in the previous session. The junior KOSDAQ index also advanced, gaining more than 2% in early trading and holding on to its gains through the close. Nvidia results revive confidence in AI demand Controversy-hit Nvidia, the dominant supplier of AI accelerators, reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double its year-earlier figure and above analyst estimates of roughly $109 billion. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.68, beating the consensus estimate of $2.47. Nvidia expects revenue of approximately $130 billion in the quarter ending in January. The forecast exceeded analyst expectations and suggests that demand for the company's AI chips and computing systems remains strong. The company also expects a gross margin of around 71.5% in the quarter. The results reinforced expectations that demand for AI computing infrastructure remains robust, despite recent uncertainty surrounding the company's leadership. They also provided relief for South Korea's two largest memory chipmakers, which occupy a central position in the AI supply chain. Samsung and SK Hynix are leading producers of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), a specialized form of DRAM stacked alongside processors to deliver the high data throughput required by modern AI training and inference systems. SK Hynix has long been Nvidia's primary HBM supplier, while Samsung has been expanding its market share and securing additional contracts with other AI chip designers. "Nvidia's results were reassuring and gave investors a reason to refocus on earnings, but they haven't resolved the broader questions around AI spending returns, financing sustainability and leadership uncertainty," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore told Reuters. "So we are seeing an initial relief rally, but not necessarily the conviction needed for a sustained recovery." Seo Sang-young, managing director of Mirae Asset Securities, told Maeil Business Newspaper that concerns remained over delays in data-center investment, weakness in US AI and semiconductor stocks, and export restrictions. However, he said the impact was limited because those concerns had already been reflected in the market. Asian markets mixed The rebound in South Korean chip stocks came as broader Asian markets showed a mixed response to Nvidia's results. Japan's Nikkei 225 traded between modest gains and losses to close marginally higher, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng finished lower. China's Shanghai Composite also see-sawed to remain flat. Taiwan's Taiex also showed early strength before giving back some of its gains. Meanwhile, US stock index futures pointed higher during Asian trading. S&P 500 futures rose around 0.25%, while Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.68%, suggesting that Nvidia's results could help stabilize the recent sell-off in technology shares. headline: Gold slips back below one-year low but Goldman Sachs sees long term recovery
html_content:
Gold prices extended their decline on Wednesday, falling below $3,800 an ounce as expectations of further Federal Reserve interest rate increases strengthened the US dollar and weighed on bullion.

Spot gold fell 2.3% to $3,770 an ounce, while US gold futures declined more than 2% to $3,773.

The precious metal continues to be near its lowest level in 14 months as investors keep an eye on the outlook for monetary policy following a series of hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials.

Markets see a 96.4% chance of a rate hike in December, according to CME Fedwatch.

Goldman Sachs sees gold at $5,600 by 2028

Despite continued pressure, Goldman Sachs sees scope for a significant recovery over the longer term, forecasting that gold could reclaim $5,600 by the end of 2028.

In a research note published Tuesday, Goldman Sachs analysts led by Lina Thomas said gold could reach $4,650 by the end of 2027 before climbing above $5,600 in 2028.

The bank expects central banks to purchase an average of 60 tonnes of gold per month between 2026 and 2028, compared with a pre-2022 average of 17 tonnes.

Goldman described the increase as a structural shift in reserve management and does not expect central banks to reverse their buying trend anytime soon.

The bank's longer-term outlook also depends on the Federal Reserve eventually returning to interest rate cuts.

It expects four quarter-point reductions between November 2027 and September 2028, potentially bringing the federal funds rate to 3.25%-3.5%.

The latest analysis follows Goldman's forecast reduction last week, when it lowered its year-end 2026 gold target to $4,150 from $4,650.

Fed's Williams signals another rate hike

The immediate pressure on gold comes from expectations that the Federal Reserve will continue raising interest rates to contain persistent inflation.

New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that another rate increase would likely be necessary but pushed back against calls for more aggressive monetary tightening.

"I don't think the situation calls for dramatic policy action," Williams said at the Axios BFD Summit in New York.

He added that the approach taken by the central bank over recent months was working, although inflation remained stubbornly high and was moving in the wrong direction.

“We still have our work to do to ​make sure that we bring inflation back down to 2% in a timely way and ​in a sustained manner,” Williams said.

Dollar and yields add to gold's weakness

A stronger US dollar and elevated Treasury yields have added to bullion's difficulties.

Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding gold, which does not pay interest, while a stronger dollar makes the metal more expensive for international buyers.

The combination of persistent inflation and expectations of further rate increases has therefore weighed on investment demand, even as central banks continue accumulating bullion.

Goldman's longer-term bullish outlook rests on the expectation that this pressure will eventually ease, allowing institutional and ETF investors to return to the market.

Investors now await minutes from the Fed's October 27-28 meeting for further clues on the policy outlook.

headline: XRP reclaims $1, aided by massive Binance whale withdrawals
html_content:
XRP is up 4.5% on Wednesday, making it the best performer among the top 10 cryptocurrencies by market cap.

The rally has allowed the cryptocurrency to reclaim the $1 psychological level, with the bulls now eyeing higher supply zones. 

The rally comes as on-chain data suggests that large investors may be changing how they manage their XRP holdings.

Meanwhile, US spot XRP exchange-traded funds (ETFs) continue to experience withdrawals, while broader cryptocurrency market sentiment remains deeply pessimistic.

XRP whale withdrawals from Binance reach $127 million

Large XRP holders have significantly increased their withdrawals from Binance following the cryptocurrency's decline below $1.

According to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost, whales withdrew approximately $21 million worth of XRP from the exchange on Monday.

Daily net outflows have ranged between $12 million and $33 million over the past week, reflecting a noticeable shift in large-holder activity.

Since November 10, cumulative net whale withdrawals from Binance have reached approximately $127 million.

The pattern contrasts with activity recorded in August, when XRP was experiencing a price rally. During that period, large investors deposited an average of approximately $75 million worth of XRP into Binance daily.

Darkfost believes the recent increase in withdrawals could indicate that whales are accumulating XRP despite the market downturn.

If these tokens are being moved into long-term storage, the reduction in readily available exchange supply could eventually support price stabilization.

Institutional demand for XRP remains weak despite signs of potential accumulation among large exchange users.

US spot XRP ETFs recorded approximately $6.14 million in net outflows on Tuesday, after $19 million was redeemed from the funds last week. 

The withdrawals reflect continued caution among investors seeking exposure to XRP through regulated investment products.

The broader cryptocurrency market remains under significant pressure as investor sentiment deteriorates. According to CoinMarketCap, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index stood at 13 on Wednesday, rising only slightly from 10 the previous day.

Both readings fall within the extreme fear category, indicating widespread caution among cryptocurrency investors.

XRP reclaims $1 as buyers seek to regain control

XRP's short-term price action suggests a bullish recovery, but the broader technical structure remains bearish.

The cryptocurrency has reclaimed the $1 psychological level after consolidating between $0.94 and $0.98 in recent days. 

However, XRP remains significantly below its major daily Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs). The 50-day EMA stands around $1.22, while the 100-day EMA is positioned near $1.26.

Meanwhile, the 200-day EMA sits at approximately $1.33. These moving averages form several layers of resistance above the current market price.

Trading below all three indicators suggests that the broader trend remains bearish across multiple timeframes.

The SuperTrend indicator also reinforces the negative outlook, with its resistance line positioned near $1.13. It is commonly used to identify prevailing price trends and potential reversal levels.

With XRP trading below the indicator, the current setup suggests that sellers continue to dominate.

A sustained recovery above the SuperTrend line would represent an early improvement in the technical outlook, although additional resistance would remain overhead.

XRP's momentum indicators suggest that the recent decline may be becoming overstretched. The daily Relative Strength Index stands near 27, placing the cryptocurrency in oversold territory.

Meanwhile, XRP's Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator remains in negative territory. The negative reading suggests that bearish momentum continues to dominate despite the possibility of a short-term rebound.

The combination of an oversold RSI and negative MACD indicates that XRP could experience temporary upward price movements without necessarily reversing its broader downtrend.

XRP faces several important technical barriers if buyers attempt to reverse the current decline. After surpassing the $0.98 resistance, buyers would be encouraged to push XRP towards the SuperTrend level near $1.13. 

A daily candle close above $1 would represent an important improvement in short-term sentiment, although the broader technical outlook would remain bearish.

Beyond $1.13, XRP faces resistance at the 50-day EMA around $1.22. The former ascending trendline near $1.24 represents another important obstacle.

Further resistance stands at the 100-day EMA around $1.26, followed by the 200-day EMA near $1.33. Reclaiming the 200-day EMA would provide stronger evidence that XRP's broader bearish structure is beginning to improve.

On the downside, $0.94 remains an important immediate level to monitor. A sustained breakdown below this support could expose XRP to further selling pressure. 

However, the recent increase in whale withdrawals could become supportive if it reflects genuine long-term accumulation rather than internal exchange transfers.

headline: Oil price today: Brent slips as fresh data shows rise in US crude inventory
html_content:
Oil prices fell on Wednesday, November 18, after industry data showed a large rise in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although ongoing US-Iran fighting and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz limited the drop.

Brent crude futures for January delivery, the front month, were down $0.94, or 1.07%, at $92.21 a barrel at 11:30 AM BST.

US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) for December delivery was down $1.65, or 1.42%, at $84.60.

What happened to oil prices today?

Both benchmarks had settled higher on Tuesday, with Brent up 0.76% at $93.14 and WTI up 0.34% at $86.01, as US-Iran strikes and shipping attacks kept a bid under the market.

That rebound faded once traders digested Tuesday evening's American Petroleum Institute figures.

US crude stocks rose by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13, CNBC reported. Gasoline inventories increased by 5.12 million barrels and distillate stocks by 351,000 barrels.

A Reuters poll had pointed to a decline in crude inventories, Economy Middle East reported, so the API build was a bearish surprise. Official figures from the US Energy Information Administration are due at 15:30 GMT (UK time) on Wednesday.

Why is oil falling?

The API estimate extends a rebound in US commercial crude stocks.

Official EIA data show inventories rose by 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million in the week ended November 6, from 409.8 million the week before, though they remained 13.2 million barrels, or 3.1%, below the year-earlier level of 427.6 million, according to the agency's Weekly Petroleum Status Report.

The inventory news lands on a market already repricing a broader surplus.

The International Energy Agency said last week that supply would exceed demand by about 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, as Invezz noted in its Friday IEA report and Tuesday analysis.

Geopolitics is still capping how far prices can fall.

Bahrain's defence force said on Wednesday that it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, a day after the US and Iran traded strikes.

An LPG tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman on Monday, and Yemen's Houthis said they had launched drones towards pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which has been used to bypass the strait.

Although regional supply may continue to recover through alternative routes, the latest vessel data suggests that normalization of flows through Hormuz is still not possible under current conditions, LSEG analysts said in a note on Tuesday, according to Reuters.

What happens next?

The EIA report at 15:30 GMT will show whether the official data confirm the API's large crude and gasoline builds.

A Wall Street Journal survey of nine analysts and traders put the average forecast for official crude stocks at a 1 million barrel increase, with estimates ranging from a 4 million barrel build to a 1.5 million barrel draw.

If the EIA print is closer to the API's 5.28 million-barrel crude rise, it would be well above that consensus and could keep pressure on prices.

OPEC+ ministers also meet on November 29 to set 2027 output policy.

Should you buy oil now?

US inventories are rebuilding from last month's draws, and the IEA already sees a fourth-quarter surplus. But Hormuz shipping remains disrupted, and today's EIA numbers could still surprise.

If you are considering exposure to crude, compare the best commodity trading platforms before you decide.

Whether official stocks confirm the API's 5.28 million-barrel build will be the next test of how quickly US supply is loosening.
