headline: Morgan Stanley predicts this event to be the final stage of market correction
html_content:
Wall Street's prolonged correction could be approaching its final stage, according to Morgan Stanley's chief US equity strategist Mike Wilson.

Speaking to CNBC on Tuesday, Wilson said the correction, which began in June, could reach its final low over the next two to three weeks.

The market's six-month performance highlights the extent of the damage, particularly in technology stocks.

Through November 17, the Nasdaq Composite had lost approximately 6.8%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.8%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which has relatively less exposure to technology companies, gained around 2.2%.

'Market correction to end soon'

Wilson identified the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision as the biggest remaining obstacle that needs to be cleared before the market can establish a durable recovery.

"We've been talking about three clearing events for this correction to get over. One is midterms and that is behind us and that is kind of priced. Second is all this capital raising that's going on and that kind of slows down naturally in the seasonal time of the year in December and January so that is a positive."

Morgan Stanley's chief US equity strategist
Mike Wilson

Wilson said that one of the biggest sources of uncertainty was the November 3 midterm elections, which Democrats won by taking control of both chambers of Congress.

The results initially unsettled technology investors over concerns about tighter regulation of AI infrastructure and data center construction. Wilson believes much of that uncertainty is now reflected in stock prices.

Wilson expects capital raising activities to slow naturally during December and January, a seasonal development that could ease pressure on liquidity and equity markets.

This makes the Federal Reserve the biggest hurdle that remains.

"The big one is still the Fed," he said.

"I think the market is concerned about that because you don't really want to raise rates into year-end when liquidity is tight. So this is the final hurdle, but I can see it's 2, 3 weeks away. This is where I think we are going to make our final low for this correction."

He pointed out that investors are anxious right now but that is actually a good sign as the outlook for next year remains strong.

"People are really uncomfortable right now and that is a good sign when you feel uncomfortable as long as your fundamental work is telling you that we still have pretty good growth next year. Stocks are not expensive anymore... it looks like double-digit growth again for 2027."

Nvidia earnings offer temporary relief

One development offering some encouragement to investors is Nvidia's latest quarterly performance.

The chipmaker reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double the year-earlier figure. Data center revenue climbed 110% to $107.6 billion, while adjusted earnings reached $2.68 per share.

Nvidia also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above Wall Street expectations.

Its shares initially gained around 4% in after-hours trading, helping revive sentiment across AI-related stocks.

Futures linked to all three major indexes were in the green on Wednesday.

However, the relief may prove temporary.

Nvidia remains down around 25% this month, with investors still concerned about its leadership transition following Jensen Huang's departure, regulatory scrutiny and the sustainability of enormous AI infrastructure investments.

Through November 17, the Nasdaq Composite had lost approximately 6.8%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.8%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which has relatively less exposure to technology companies, gained around 2.2%. 'Market correction to end soon' Wilson identified the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision as the biggest remaining obstacle that needs to be cleared before the market can establish a durable recovery. "We've been talking about three clearing events for this correction to get over. One is midterms and that is behind us and that is kind of priced. Second is all this capital raising that's going on and that kind of slows down naturally in the seasonal time of the year in December and January so that is a positive." Morgan Stanley's chief US equity strategist Mike Wilson Wilson said that one of the biggest sources of uncertainty was the November 3 midterm elections, which Democrats won by taking control of both chambers of Congress. The results initially unsettled technology investors over concerns about tighter regulation of AI infrastructure and data center construction. Wilson believes much of that uncertainty is now reflected in stock prices. Wilson expects capital raising activities to slow naturally during December and January, a seasonal development that could ease pressure on liquidity and equity markets. This makes the Federal Reserve the biggest hurdle that remains. "The big one is still the Fed," he said. "I think the market is concerned about that because you don't really want to raise rates into year-end when liquidity is tight. So this is the final hurdle, but I can see it's 2, 3 weeks away. This is where I think we are going to make our final low for this correction." "People are really uncomfortable right now and that is a good sign when you feel uncomfortable as long as your fundamental work is telling you that we still have pretty good growth next year. Its shares initially gained around 4% in after-hours trading, helping revive sentiment across AI-related stocks. Futures linked to all three major indexes were in the green on Wednesday. However, the relief may prove temporary. Nvidia remains down around 25% this month, with investors still concerned about its leadership transition following Jensen Huang's departure, regulatory scrutiny and the sustainability of enormous AI infrastructure investments. headline: Bitget launches Agentic Account Airdrop
html_content:
Bitget has launched a new round of Agentic Account Airdrop.

The Agentic Account is a dedicated subaccount that lets traders connect an AI agent of their choice to research markets and execute trades while retaining full control of their funds.

New users who complete their first trade through the agent and share their experiences could receive Anthropic stock tokens worth up to 105 USDT.

The new round follows a limited early-access round that closed on November 6.

It incentivized early adopters who reached 10,000+ USDT in trading volume on their Agentic Account for Anthropic stock tokens worth 150 USDT each.

The new round extends the opportunity to traders who have yet to place their first agent trade, and Bitget intends to keep recognizing users who adopt agent-based trading early.

The campaign arrives as AI-related stocks continue to move sharply and interest in Anthropic keeps growing.

That leaves individual traders with a practical question about how to distinguish signal from noise and act on it when their time and attention are limited.

Launched in April and upgraded in September 2026, Bitget's Agentic Account addresses that gap by letting an agent monitor markets, support research, and carry out trades under rules the user sets.

"Traders want to act on what they see in the market, but few have the time to watch it around the clock," said Gracy Chen, CEO of Bitget.

"With the Agentic Account, users can connect the AI agent they already use, let it research and execute trades for them, and keep control of their funds in a separate subaccount. This campaign gives traders a simple reason to take that first step."

The Agentic Account is built on Bitget Agent Hub, which offers 164 API capabilities spanning trading, account management, and market research data across crypto and US equity use cases.

It works with most mainstream agents, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Grok Bot.

Each Agentic Account is separate from the user's main account, making sure that the agent can only use the funds allocated to it, and users keep control over withdrawals, transfers from the main account and disconnecting the agent.

As of mid-November 2026, the average cumulative trading volume per AI trading user has exceeded 300,000 USDT, while cumulative Agent Hub API calls have surpassed 100 million.

The Agentic Account is a core part of Bitget's AI strategy and its move toward an agent-native exchange, where users and their agents can operate side by side.

Within the UEX model, an agent can trade crypto and tokenized stocks in a single venue, with research and execution connected in a single workflow.

headline: Solana surges 3% as ETFs attract $11.68 million
html_content:
Solana (SOL) extended its recovery on Wednesday, trading near $75 after gaining more than 3% in the last 24 hours as institutional demand showed tentative signs of improvement.

The rebound followed the first positive daily inflow into Solana exchange-traded funds (ETFs) in nearly four weeks, alongside stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings from Nvidia.

However, the recovery comes against a challenging market backdrop. Solana has recorded six consecutive weekly losses, while futures Open Interest has declined significantly as traders reduce their exposure.

Technical indicators also present a mixed picture. Although oversold conditions suggest that selling pressure may be easing, SOL remains below its major moving averages, leaving the broader downtrend intact.

Solana ETFs record first inflows since October 21

Institutional demand for Solana showed signs of improvement this week after several weeks of persistent withdrawals.

According to SoSoValue, US spot Solana ETFs recorded approximately $11.68 million in net inflows on Monday, marking their first positive daily flow since October 21.

The inflows coincided with SOL's recovery, suggesting that some investors may be returning after the cryptocurrency's prolonged decline.

However, the improvement remains tentative. Solana ETFs recorded no net inflows on Tuesday, indicating that institutional buying has yet to establish a consistent trend.

If positive ETF flows continue, they could provide additional support for SOL and help stabilize sentiment.

Solana's rebound also coincided with stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings from Nvidia. The semiconductor company reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, representing a 103% increase from the previous year and a 20% rise from the preceding quarter. 

The results helped improve sentiment toward technology-related investments and other risk-sensitive assets.

Despite the recent price recovery, Solana's derivatives market continues to show signs of weakening activity.

According to CoinGlass, SOL futures Open Interest declined to approximately 54.33 million SOL from 62.79 million SOL last week.

A decline generally indicates that traders are closing positions or that contracts are being liquidated faster than new positions are opened.

Solana recovers from $67.50 after six consecutive weekly losses

Solana's recent rebound follows an extended period of weakness. SOL trades around $74.82 on Wednesday after recovering from the $67.50 support level tested on Sunday.

The cryptocurrency declined approximately 16% last week, recording its sixth consecutive bearish weekly close.

The prolonged downturn has pushed Solana significantly below its major daily Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs). The 50-day EMA stands near $93.11, while the 200-day EMA is positioned around $96.46.

Both indicators remain well above the current market price, reinforcing the broader bearish structure.

Solana's momentum indicators suggest that the recent decline may be becoming overstretched. The daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands near 25, placing SOL in oversold territory.

An RSI reading below 30 generally indicates that selling pressure has been unusually strong relative to recent buying activity.

Meanwhile, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator remains negative, suggesting that bearish momentum continues to dominate.

The combination of an oversold RSI and moderating MACD weakness supports the possibility of a short-term rebound.

Solana faces several important technical barriers as buyers attempt to extend the current recovery.

The first significant resistance stands near $77.60. A sustained breakout above this level could encourage buyers to target the next horizontal resistance around $87.46.

Beyond $87.46, Solana faces a concentrated resistance region formed by its major daily moving averages and nearby horizontal levels.

The 50-day EMA at $93.11 represents an important technical hurdle, followed by horizontal resistance near $95.82 and the 200-day EMA around $96.46.

Reclaiming this resistance cluster would provide stronger evidence that bearish momentum is weakening.

On the downside, $67.50 remains the most important immediate support. A breakdown below this level would weaken the current rebound and expose Solana to further selling pressure.

The next significant downside target stands near $60.13. Buyers may attempt to defend this region, although a sustained break below it would increase concerns about a deeper correction.

For now, Solana's near-term outlook remains mixed, with oversold conditions supporting a possible rebound while the broader trend continues to favor sellers.

headline: Lenovo stock has fallen ahead of earnings: will AI growth offset plunging PC sales?
html_content:
Lenovo Group stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has dropped from a high of $37.78 in September to the current $17.20. Focus now shifts to the upcoming earnings report, which will provide more hints on its revenue and profitability growth. 

Lenovo Group to publish strong earnings report

Lenovo Group is a top technology company that offers products and services to consumers and businesses. It operates two businesses, including the Intelligence Devices Group (IDG) and Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG). 

The company’s business has done well this year, driven by its ISG segment, which has benefited from the ongoing data center demand. This business includes products like servers and other networking equipment. 

The most recent earnings report showed that the company’s business continued growing. IDG’s segment grew by 27% to $17.1 billion, driven by PCs. On the other hand, its ISG business grew by 98% to $8.5 billion. 

Lenovo Group will publish its financial results on Thursday. A key aspect to watch will be its ISG business, which is expected to show some weakness. In a recent report, Gartner said that global PC sales stood at 55.4 million in the third quarter. It dropped by 22.4% from a year earlier.

The PC business is being affected by the rising cost of doing business, including in the memory and servers. Lenovo maintained the biggest market share with over 14.9 million shipments, which dropped by 22% from a year earlier. The other top companies in the PC industry were HP, Dell, Apple, and ASUS.

On the positive side, the company’s infrastructure business is expected to show strength because of the ongoing AI infrastructure. Gartner predicts that AI infrastructure spending will continue rising in the near term. 

The report showed that AI spending will jump to $4 trillion next year, with AI infrastructure accounting for $2.4 trillion, a 53% jump from this year. This surge will benefit companies like Lenovo Group that provide the items necessary for the rollout.

Lenovo faces some potential risks

Lenovo Group faces some major risks ahead. One of them is that the rising memory costs is affecting its PC and tablet businesses. As such, there is a risk that margins in this business will be subdued. 

The other risk is that the company is still highly overvalued, with the forward price-to-earnings ratio is 32.75. This multiple is much higher than Dell’s 12.41 and HP Enterprise’s 12. 

There is also a risk that the AI bubble will burst, a move that will affect demand for servers and networking devices. Further, the company faces the risk of falling prices of servers, storage, and networking products as supply growth continues. 

Additionally, the company faces substantial competition from the likes of Dell, HP Enterprise, and Super Micro Computer.

Lenovo Group stock technical analysis

Lenovo Group stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Lenovo Group shares have been under pressure in the past few months. It has already plunged below the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA).

Most importantly, the stock has been forming a series of lower lows and lower highs. It has also dropped below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level. It has also fallen below the Strong, Pivot, Reverse level of the Murrey Math Lines tool. 

Therefore, there is a risk that the stock will drop further, potentially to the Ultimate Support level of $12.50. A move below that level will point to more downside in the near term. However, in the long term, there is a possibility that the stock will rebound, potentially to the Major S/R pivot point at $25.

headline: What to expect from Trump's historic trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Putin
html_content:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday and received an unusually warm welcome from Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of a historic trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, scheduled for Thursday.

Xi greeted Trump with a hug at the airport, an uncommon gesture by the Chinese leader and a signal of the importance Beijing has attached to the visit.

The meeting will bring together the leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers for the first time in a trilateral format, with discussions expected to cover nuclear arms reductions, trade and global security.

The encounter will mark the last leg of Trump's visit to Asia, which has been overshadowed by trade tensions, the Nvidia espionage controversy and concerns over critical infrastructure failures in the US.

North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un could also potentially attend the wider gathering, which is being held alongside the 21-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' summit.

Xi welcomes Trump with rare airport reception

Xi's decision to personally receive Trump at the airport was notable.

The Chinese president did not extend a similar welcome when Trump visited Beijing in May.

However, Trump had made an unusual gesture of his own in September, travelling to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Xi during the Chinese leader's visit to the US.

It was the first time Trump had personally welcomed a foreign visitor at the military base.

China's state news agency Xinhua said Xi referred to that reception during his meeting with Trump, describing Beijing's welcome as an expression of its tradition of reciprocity.

"When I visited the United States in September this year, president Trump and his wife made a special trip to the airport to welcome me, and a grand welcoming ceremony was held.

"China is a nation of courtesy, with a tradition of reciprocity. I welcome you back to China and look forward to exchanging in-depth views with you on major issues concerning China–US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape, so as to advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship between China and the US based on respect, fairness and reciprocity."

Xi said he hoped the discussions would help build a "constructive, strategic and stable relationship" between the two countries, guided by "respect, fairness and reciprocity".

The meeting marks Trump's third encounter with Xi this year.

After visiting Beijing in May, the US president hosted the Chinese leader for a state dinner at the White House in September.

Trump, who previously criticised Beijing over its trade practices, has increasingly sought to improve relations between the world's two largest economies.

Trump, Xi and Putin to discuss nuclear weapons

The most significant item on Thursday's agenda is expected to be nuclear nonproliferation.

The White House confirmed last Friday that Trump would meet Xi and Putin to discuss possible reductions in the three countries' nuclear arsenals, Politico reported.

It would be the first time the leaders of the world's largest nuclear-armed nations have met in a trilateral format specifically to discuss the issue.

A senior US administration official, briefing reporters on the planned meeting, said Washington hoped the discussions would open the door to further engagement but did not expect an immediate agreement on reducing nuclear stockpiles, the report by Politico said.

"This is hopefully the beginning of a conversation that can be productive going forward," the official said, according to Politico.

The official also sought to rule out discussions on the war in Ukraine, saying: "The president has said that he does not intend to talk about Ukraine in that meeting."

The administration's position reflects its view that negotiations on Ukraine are being handled through a separate diplomatic track that does not involve China.

Nvidia controversy unlikely to dominate talks

The meeting is taking place against the backdrop of a major controversy involving Nvidia and allegations of Chinese espionage.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was forced to resign last week following revelations about an extramarital affair with a businesswoman whom US intelligence agencies had determined was spying for China.

However, both Trump and Xi have sought to play down the issue ahead of their meeting.

Trump has said he does not intend to raise the allegations with the Chinese president, despite the potential implications for US-China technology relations.

The issue is particularly sensitive given the strategic importance of advanced semiconductors and artificial intelligence to both countries.

Trump has also indicated that he does not intend to raise allegations of Chinese interference in American affairs during his discussions with Xi.

Trade and artificial intelligence feature prominently

Beyond the trilateral meeting, trade and technology are expected to dominate the broader APEC discussions.

Xi opened the summit by calling for greater cooperation in international trade, scientific innovation and artificial intelligence, positioning China as a supporter of multilateral engagement at a time of growing geopolitical tensions.

"We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," Xi said.

Russian President Putin also addressed the gathering, arguing that Western sanctions had failed to weaken Russia and had instead strengthened the country.

The choice of Shenzhen as the host city adds a technological dimension to the discussions.

Often described as one of China's "Silicon Valleys", the city is a major centre for the country's internet, technology and artificial intelligence industries.

Beijing is expected to use the summit to present itself as a champion of multilateralism in contrast with what it describes as unilateralism and protectionism.

Trade, artificial intelligence and the conflict in the Middle East are also expected to feature on the agenda.

Xi held several bilateral meetings with visiting leaders on Wednesday, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung.

Their discussions covered trade and commerce, while Seoul's account also said the two leaders discussed peace on the Korean Peninsula.

That subject was absent from Beijing's official readout of the meeting.

While expectations of a concrete breakthrough from Thursday's trilateral talks remain limited, the gathering will offer an important opportunity for Washington, Beijing and Moscow to signal whether cooperation on nuclear security and other global issues remains possible amid deep strategic divisions.

I welcome you back to China and look forward to exchanging in-depth views with you on major issues concerning China–US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape, so as to advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship between China and the US based on respect, fairness and reciprocity." Xi said he hoped the discussions would help build a "constructive, strategic and stable relationship" between the two countries, guided by "respect, fairness and reciprocity". The meeting marks Trump's third encounter with Xi this year. After visiting Beijing in May, the US president hosted the Chinese leader for a state dinner at the White House in September. Trump, who previously criticised Beijing over its trade practices, has increasingly sought to improve relations between the world's two largest economies. Trump, Xi and Putin to discuss nuclear weapons The most significant item on Thursday's agenda is expected to be nuclear nonproliferation. The White House confirmed last Friday that Trump would meet Xi and Putin to discuss possible reductions in the three countries' nuclear arsenals, Politico reported. It would be the first time the leaders of the world's largest nuclear-armed nations have met in a trilateral format specifically to discuss the issue. A senior US administration official, briefing reporters on the planned meeting, said Washington hoped the discussions would open the door to further engagement but did not expect an immediate agreement on reducing nuclear stockpiles, the report by Politico said. "This is hopefully the beginning of a conversation that can be productive going forward," the official said, according to Politico. The official also sought to rule out discussions on the war in Ukraine, saying: "The president has said that he does not intend to talk about Ukraine in that meeting." The administration's position reflects its view that negotiations on Ukraine are being handled through a separate diplomatic track that does not involve China. Nvidia controversy unlikely to dominate talks The meeting is taking place against the backdrop of a major controversy involving Nvidia and allegations of Chinese espionage. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was forced to resign last week following revelations about an extramarital affair with a businesswoman whom US intelligence agencies had determined was spying for China. However, both Trump and Xi have sought to play down the issue ahead of their meeting. Trump has said he does not intend to raise the allegations with the Chinese president, despite the potential implications for US-China technology relations. The issue is particularly sensitive given the strategic importance of advanced semiconductors and artificial intelligence to both countries. Trump has also indicated that he does not intend to raise allegations of Chinese interference in American affairs during his discussions with Xi. Trade and artificial intelligence feature prominently Beyond the trilateral meeting, trade and technology are expected to dominate the broader APEC discussions. Xi opened the summit by calling for greater cooperation in international trade, scientific innovation and artificial intelligence, positioning China as a supporter of multilateral engagement at a time of growing geopolitical tensions. "We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," Xi said. Russian President Putin also addressed the gathering, arguing that Western sanctions had failed to weaken Russia and had instead strengthened the country. The choice of Shenzhen as the host city adds a technological dimension to the discussions. Often described as one of China's "Silicon Valleys", the city is a major centre for the country's internet, technology and artificial intelligence industries. Beijing is expected to use the summit to present itself as a champion of multilateralism in contrast with what it describes as unilateralism and protectionism. Trade, artificial intelligence and the conflict in the Middle East are also expected to feature on the agenda. Xi held several bilateral meetings with visiting leaders on Wednesday, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung. Their discussions covered trade and commerce, while Seoul's account also said the two leaders discussed peace on the Korean Peninsula. That subject was absent from Beijing's official readout of the meeting. While expectations of a concrete breakthrough from Thursday's trilateral talks remain limited, the gathering will offer an important opportunity for Washington, Beijing and Moscow to signal whether cooperation on nuclear security and other global issues remains possible amid deep strategic divisions. headline: Nasdaq futures up 250 pts: Five things to know before Wall Street opens
html_content:
Wall Street futures climbed on Wednesday as Nvidia's stronger-than-expected quarterly results and upbeat revenue guidance helped restore confidence in the artificial intelligence trade after a difficult start to the week.

Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.94%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.46% and Dow Jones futures advanced 0.17%.

The recovery follows another difficult session on Tuesday, when all three major US indexes closed lower. The Dow fell 1.6%, the S&P 500 declined 1%, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.7% as investors reduced exposure to technology and AI-related stocks.

Nvidia's earnings have provided some relief, but investors still face several important developments. Here are five things to know before markets open.

Nvidia results revive AI trade

Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double the year-earlier figure and above Wall Street expectations. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.68 per share.

    Its data center division generated $107.6 billion in revenue, up 110% year over year, highlighting continued demand for AI computing infrastructure.

    The company also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, comfortably above the analyst estimate of $125.25 billion.

    The stock was up over 3% in premarket trading.

    The results were particularly significant given the leadership crisis following Jensen Huang's departure.

    Board Chairman Harvey Jones and Interim CEO Colette Kress both ruled out bringing Huang back even as the Nvidia co-founder himself showed willingness to return.

    Jones highlighted that the company would move quickly to find a permanent successor to the controversy-hit Huang.

    AI stocks stage a broad recovery

    Nvidia's strong results lifted semiconductor and AI infrastructure stocks across the board.

      AMD gained around 2% in premarket trading, while Broadcom rose 2.5%, Micron advanced 2.5% and Marvell climbed 2.9%.

      Neocloud providers also rallied, with CoreWeave gaining 4.5% and Nebius rising 6.3%. Other data center-related stocks, including IREN and Applied Digital, also advanced.

      The recovery suggests investors are looking beyond Nvidia's leadership controversy and focusing again on demand for AI computing capacity. However, concerns remain over the durability of the same.

      Chip stocks in South Korea also gained, with Samsung Electronics gaining over 2% and SK Hynix adding more than 4% to take the broader Kospi index higher.

      Anthropic IPO: the next big test

      Investors are now turning their attention to Anthropic's highly anticipated stock market debut.

        According to Bloomberg, the Claude maker is guiding prospective investors toward an IPO price of $78 per share or higher, above its initial $70-$78 range.

        The offering, combined with a $26 billion private placement, could raise approximately $90.4 billion and value Anthropic at around $1.4 trillion.

        The shares are expected to begin trading on Thursday under the Nasdaq ticker ANT.

        Oil prices retreat

        Crude prices declined as rising US inventories outweighed some concerns about Middle Eastern supply disruptions.

          Brent crude fell 0.50% to $92.68 a barrel, while WTI declined 1.14% to $85.09.

          US crude inventories increased by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13, while gasoline stocks rose by 5.12 million barrels.

          Continued tensions involving Iran and threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited the decline.

          Fed minutes due later today

          Investors will also examine the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting, scheduled for release at 2 p.m. ET.

            The minutes could provide insight into policymakers' views on persistent inflation and the possibility of further interest rate increases beyond December.

            Markets are almost fully pricing in a quarter-point rate hike in December after recent inflation and employment figures came in stronger than expected.

            The minutes will be particularly important for Treasury yields and equity sentiment as investors assess how much further monetary tightening the economy can absorb.

headline: WhiteBIT expands institutional offering with relaunched OTC Desk
html_content:
WhiteBIT has updated its over-the-counter (OTC) platform and expanded its institutional offering with a large-volume trading section for digital assets and fiat currencies.

Designed for institutional and corporate customers, investment funds, family offices, and other market participants who are looking for a new solution when dealing with high-value transactions.

Large trades without the price slippage

When trading over-the-counter, orders placed are not traded on the public order book, and therefore do not have the same effect on the market price or execution costs as the normal exchange trading order.

This can minimize the market impact, allow more flexibility on the period of execution and allow more customizations in institutional trading.

The institutional engagement with cryptocurrencies is growing at the level of more than just access to cryptocurrencies. Equipped with a reliable compliance framework, a dedicated team of support and processes that are predictable in their operations, funds, corporate treasuries and professional investors require execution models that allow them to operate in the same way they do in traditional financial markets. By relaunching our OTC desk, we're strengthening the infrastructure that enables these participants to execute large transactions more efficiently and with greater flexibility.

Founder and President of W Group, of which WhiteBIT is a part.
Volodymyr Nosov

Currencies supported and deal sizes

The newly relaunched desk now offers crypto-to-fiat and fiat-to-crypto trading of the major fiat currencies such as USD, EUR, GBP, CHF, and stablecoins USDT and USDC. 

The top 10 crypto assets by market capitalization are also being offered on the OTC desk, where they can be traded with USDT and USDC. Other crypto assets not in the top 10 and other fiat currencies can be obtained on request.

There is no limit on the maximum size of the OTC transaction in WhiteBIT.

Rather, the maximum depends on the source of the funds and the outcomes of the necessary compliance evaluations, and capacity is determined based on each client's actual activity.

Every client has their own OTC manager that will assist them in negotiating the parameters of the transaction, agreeing terms of execution, and support during the transaction.

It ensures the security of data and transactional information for the clients and adheres to Know Your Customer (KYC), Know Your Business (KYB), and all relevant compliance regulations.

Zero fee campaign for new OTC clients

WhiteBIT is introducing a zero fee offer for new OTC clients, covering their first transaction of up to $2 million.

It is a one-time offer, valid for three months from release after which it can be extended; transactions with the top 10 crypto assets are not covered by the offer. 

Deals with a value of more than 2 million are processed as a single tranche with an indicative price derived from the OTC pricing strategy established in advance with the client's dedicated OTC manager, allowing institutional and corporate clients to plan bigger deals from the beginning.

Strategic context

The relaunch is a part of WhiteBIT's institutional and professional market business growth strategy.

With the addition of a dedicated OTC execution channel, WhiteBIT will aim to provide crypto liquidity and allow more flexibility in handling large-scale digital asset transactions for businesses and investors.

About WhiteBIT

WhiteBIT is a leading global crypto exchange by user traffic, offering over 1020 trading pairs, 370+ assets, and supporting 8 fiat currencies. With a strong focus on regulatory compliance, WhiteBIT serves 10 million users across six continents and more than 150 countries.

Founded in 2018, the platform is part of W Group, which has more than 40 million customers globally. WhiteBIT collaborates with Visa, FACEIT, FC Barcelona, Juventus FC, and the Ukrainian national football team.

The company is dedicated to driving the widespread adoption of blockchain technology worldwide.

headline: Target earnings: retailer's comeback is showing up at checkout
html_content:
Target (TGT) cut prices on nearly 2,000 additional items in its fiscal Q3; it also persuaded shoppers to check out more often.

The retailer posted a 7.1% year-on-year increase in revenue to $27.1 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.56 per share, including 50 cents from tariff refunds.

The refunds made for a bigger earnings beat, but the sales figures tell investors more about whether the turnaround can last.

Target is ringing up more purchases in stores and online, and it kept more of each sales dollar even before counting the refunds.

At the time of writing, Target stock is up nearly 60% versus the start of this year.

What drove strength in Target’s fiscal Q3?

Target’s comparable sales rose 5.6%, with transactions up 5% and the average purchase up just 0.6%.

That mix matters for a retailer trying to win back shopping trips.

Target’s Fun 101 assortment, which includes toys, gaming gear and trading cards, posted nearly 27% sales growth.

Beauty rose more than 9%, while food and beverage sales climbed nearly 7%.

A collectible can give someone a reason to visit today. Groceries and beauty staples can give them a reason to return next week.

Apparel sales, meanwhile, fell 3.8%, a reminder that Target still has work to do in a category that can help turn an errand into a bigger purchase.

Note that TGT shares also currently pay a solid dividend yield of 2.91%.

Profitability wasn’t tariff-refund dependent

Taking out the refund leaves Q3 earnings of $2.15 a share, about 21% above last year’s adjusted $1.78.

Gross margin would still have risen roughly 1.2 percentage points.

Target pointed to a comparison with heavier markdowns and higher tariff rates a year earlier, as well as productivity gains at its supply chain facilities.

Non-merchandise sales also rose 19.3%, helped by advertising, paid memberships and the Target Plus marketplace.

That gives Target more ways to earn money from the shoppers it’s bringing back.

The holiday test is whether those gains can keep offsetting pressure from freight costs and price cuts, especially when the retailer has to clear seasonal inventory.

How to play Target stock after Q3 earnings?

Target raised its full-year sales growth forecast from about 5% to 6% and lifted its earnings outlook to $10.65–$11.40 a share.

That range includes roughly $2.14 in tariff refunds recognized so far.

Subtract those and the midpoint comes to about $8.89.

At Tuesday’s close, Target shares traded at roughly 18x that figure after gaining about 63% this year.

Investors now have a higher bar for the holiday quarter.

Target says November sales through the report date had accelerated from October.

The more telling result will be whether shoppers keep coming after the holiday deals end, with fewer markdowns and more of them putting clothes and home goods in their carts.

headline: Kalshi buys New York broker FB Securities to launch stock and ETF trading
html_content:
Kalshi, the US prediction market operator, has bought a small New York broker-dealer and plans to let customers trade stocks and exchange-traded funds, according to a Wall Street Journal report on Monday.

The Journal said Kalshi acquired FB Securities in July and intends to launch equity trading within the next two months, citing people familiar with the matter. Some FB Securities staff are staying on, the paper said.

CBS News separately reported that a person familiar with the matter had confirmed the plan, and that Kalshi expects to roll out the service later this year, with FB Securities facilitating the trading. Kalshi has not made a public announcement, and LeapRate said neither Kalshi nor the broker had responded to requests for comment.

What the register shows

FB Securities is a young firm. FINRA's BrokerCheck register lists FB Securities, LLC, also known as Fundbank Securities, LLC, as an SEC-registered broker-dealer formed in Delaware in September 2024. Its FINRA registration was approved on 16 December 2025.

The register describes it as a small firm based in New York, registered in 51 US states and territories, with no disclosures. John Damion Rosanelli is listed as chief executive, and the sole member is an entity called FB Securities Member, LLC.

BrokerCheck does not name Kalshi as a direct or indirect owner, so the reported change of control is not yet reflected on the public record.

From event contracts to equities

Buying an existing broker-dealer is the quicker route into US securities. A Kalshi-owned broker would sit alongside its exchange, which is regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and allow it to offer shares and ETFs that fall under SEC and FINRA oversight.

The Journal said the aim is to build a multi-asset exchange. Kalshi has moved quickly beyond its core event contracts this year. It began offering perpetual futures on cryptocurrencies in May and on precious metals in September, according to CBS News.

In October, after CFTC approval, it launched a perpetual contract tracking the MerQube US Large Cap Index, Finance Magnates reported. Earlier this month it added perpetuals tied to more than 50 individual stocks. Kalshi has said its crypto perpetuals generated more than $5.5 billion of trading volume in their first two weeks.

The company also plans to launch compute futures, which would let investors and companies hedge the rental price of AI computing power, and is in talks to raise money at a $65 billion valuation, the Journal reported.

Pressure on incumbents

The report weighed on listed brokers. Shares in Robinhood and Charles Schwab edged lower on Monday after the news, Investing.com reported, although Robinhood was already under pressure from weakness in crypto markets.

An equity account would let Kalshi hold a customer's event contracts, perpetuals and shares on one platform, putting it in competition for the same active retail traders that Robinhood and Charles Schwab serve. Robinhood already offers prediction markets to its own customers, so the overlap runs both ways.

Regulatory backdrop

The expansion comes as Kalshi's core business faces legal challenges. Several US states argue that its sports contracts amount to illegal gambling and should be regulated at state level, while the CFTC maintains that it has exclusive jurisdiction. Last week the CFTC and the Department of Justice sued Louisiana after a state court order barred Kalshi and others from offering event contracts there.

Political pressure is also building. Nine Democratic senators wrote to the CFTC on Monday asking it to halt efforts to assert its authority over prediction markets, according to the Journal.

Kalshi has not given a launch date, pricing or a list of the products it will offer. Until it does, traders comparing stock and ETF providers can review the field in our guide to the best trading platforms.

headline: IG to close Paris, Madrid and Milan offices as Jersey move completes
html_content:
IG Group is shutting its offices in Paris, Madrid and Milan, according to a Bloomberg report, as the London-listed broker presses on with a restructuring that has reshaped the business this year.

Bloomberg reported on Friday that staff in the three offices had been told of the plans, citing people familiar with the matter. Dozens of jobs are affected, with one source putting the figure at roughly 50, the news agency said.

"We have refreshed our organisational model to ensure IG is best placed to serve customers," an IG spokesperson told Bloomberg. "This includes consolidating our European presence into a smaller number of larger hubs."

IG has not issued a stock exchange announcement on the closures. Finance Magnates said the company had not responded to its request for comment, and IG has not said which hubs will serve clients in France, Spain and Italy, or whether licensing arrangements for those customers will change. Finimize reported that IG told MT Newswires that service for European customers would not change and that clients did not need to take any action.

IG opened its Spanish and French offices in 2007 and its Italian office in 2008, according to Finance Magnates.

A smaller piece of the group

Europe is one of IG's smaller regions. Its Europe division generated £74.5 million of net trading revenue in the first half of 2026, up 10% from £67.7 million a year earlier, according to the company's half-year results. That compares with group net trading revenue of £588.8 million for the period.

The closures follow a strategic review announced in March. In its half-year results, IG said it would bring its UK and Ireland, Europe, and APAC and Middle East businesses together in a single commercial unit, IG Consumer, with the change taking effect in the second half of 2026. At a capital markets event on 22 October, the group said it had reorganised around three divisions: IG Consumer, IG Securities and tastytrade, its US business.

Pressure on revenue

The cost cuts come after a weaker third quarter. In a trading update on 2 October, IG said it expected total revenue of about £240 million for the three months to September, down about 14% from £280.1 million a year earlier.

The company blamed lower revenue retention in its over-the-counter derivatives business, the part of the group that offers CFDs and spread bets. Retention was about 70% in the quarter, below the roughly 80% averaged since IG introduced market-making optimisation measures in the second half of 2025. IG cut its 2026 guidance to total revenue growth in a mid-single-digit percentage range.

The group has said it expects about £30 million of non-recurring redomicile and restructuring costs this year.

Jersey move completed

The reported closures coincide with the final step of IG's move to Jersey. The scheme of arrangement took effect at 8pm on Friday, 13 November, and shares in the new Jersey-incorporated IG Group Holdings plc were admitted to the London Stock Exchange's main market on Monday, keeping the IGG ticker.

In a separate regulatory notice on Monday, IG said the Jersey company had replaced the previous parent as issuer of its £250 million senior notes due October 2030 and £300 million senior notes due November 2028, with effect from 13 November.

For clients in France, Spain and Italy, the practical question is where their accounts will be served from once the local offices close. Until IG sets that out, those weighing up alternatives can compare providers in our guides to the best CFD brokers and best forex brokers.

headline: Dell stock rises as Nvidia rally lifts chipmakers, Citi backs shares
html_content:
Dell Technologies shares DELL gained more than 3% in premarket trading on Wednesday, supported by a broader rally in semiconductor and AI infrastructure stocks following Nvidia's stronger-than-expected quarterly results and revenue forecast.

Nvidia forecast January-quarter revenue of $130 billion, ahead of Wall Street expectations of $125.3 billion, reassuring investors about continued demand for AI computing infrastructure.

Dell also received support from Citi, which named the company among its preferred IT hardware stocks alongside Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Everpure, formerly Pure Storage.

However, the outlook remains mixed ahead of Dell's fiscal third-quarter results on November 24, with GF Securities warning of weakening demand in its traditional server and PC businesses.

Nvidia earnings lift Dell and semiconductor stocks

Nvidia's latest results helped ease concerns about a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure spending.

The chipmaker reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-over-year.

The results lifted semiconductor stocks in premarket trading, providing support to Dell and other companies exposed to AI infrastructure demand.

Citi identified Dell as one of its preferred IT hardware names, citing a strengthening enterprise infrastructure refresh cycle and resilient demand for AI infrastructure.

The endorsement comes as Dell prepares to report its fiscal third-quarter earnings on November 24.

Options markets are pricing in an approximately 10% move in the stock following the results.

Dell has exceeded the moves implied by options markets in five of its last eight earnings announcements.

The company's record $95 billion AI server backlog and raised full-year revenue guidance also support the bullish case, giving investors reasons to look beyond the stock's steep November selloff.

GF Securities cuts Dell price target to $341

Despite the positive sentiment surrounding AI infrastructure, GF Securities has taken a more cautious view of Dell's longer-term business outlook.

The firm cut its price target to $341 from $497, citing growing headwinds in traditional enterprise servers, PCs, and competition for AI server orders.

GF Securities expects enterprise server shipments to decline 9% year-over-year in fiscal 2027, with another decrease in the following year.

It also forecasts a high-single-digit decline in PC shipments in fiscal 2028.

The analysts pointed to Dell losing a portion of SpaceX's VR200 order to Hon Hai as another potential challenge.

However, GF Securities expects Dell's upcoming fiscal third-quarter results to remain solid, supported by strong AI server shipments.

The firm estimates quarterly revenue of $54 billion, with gross margins of 18.4% and earnings per share of $7.18.

These figures compare with consensus estimates of 19.2% for gross margins and $6.50 for earnings per share.

GF Securities also revised its earnings estimates, raising its fiscal 2027 EPS forecast by 2% while cutting its fiscal 2028 estimate by 3%.

AI server demand supports near-term outlook

GF Securities expects Dell to raise its fiscal 2027 guidance again, supported by AI server revenue that could reach $85 billion.

The analysts believe this could push full-year revenue above $200 billion, alongside a modest upward revision to earnings per share.

However, the firm warned that traditional server demand could weaken more significantly because of pricing pressures and sales brought forward into 2026.

It now expects traditional server shipments to decline by double digits in the second half of 2027, with subdued demand continuing into fiscal 2028.

headline: Why AMD stock is rallying in premarket trading on Wednesday?
html_content:
AMD shares jumped 1.15% in premarket trading on Wednesday as artificial intelligence-linked stocks rallied following Nvidia's stronger-than-expected third-quarter results and upbeat revenue forecast.

The gains came after a mixed session on Tuesday, when AMD opened higher but eventually closed 0.17% lower as broader market concerns weighed on technology stocks.

AMD, like other semiconductor companies, had faced pressure amid uncertainty surrounding Nvidia following Jensen Huang's departure as CEO.

The controversy had added to concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade and the leadership of one of its most important companies.

However, Nvidia's latest results offered some relief, with the chipmaker reporting another record quarter and issuing guidance that exceeded Wall Street expectations.

AMD's semiconductor peers were also trading higher in premarket dealings.

Nvidia revives confidence in AI demand

Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, an increase of 103% year over year and above analyst expectations of approximately $109 billion.

Net income reached $65.3 billion, while earnings per share came in at $2.68, beating the FactSet consensus estimate of $2.48.

Demand for Nvidia's AI hardware remained strong during the quarter, with the company also beginning shipments of its latest Vera Rubin systems.

The bigger boost for investors came from its forward guidance.

Nvidia expects revenue of approximately $130 billion in the quarter ending in January, exceeding analyst estimates. The forecast does not include any data-center revenue from China.

The company also expects a gross margin of around 71.5% in the coming quarter.

The outlook reinforced expectations that demand for AI chips and computing infrastructure remains robust, despite concerns about elevated valuations and the sustainability of spending across the sector.

"For Nvidia, strong earnings have bought management time. For the broader AI trade, they reinforce confidence in infrastructure demand, but the next leg of the rally may depend increasingly on which companies can turn that demand into sustainable profits," Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo told Reuters.

The guidance was particularly significant given speculation over whether Nvidia would provide a quarterly forecast amid uncertainty surrounding its leadership.

However, the leadership situation remains unresolved.

Huang has said he would be willing to return as CEO if the board considers it to be in the company's best interest, while interim CEO Colette Kress has clearly said that the company is not bringing back its co-founder in the role.

AMD continues to expand its AI business

Beyond the broader boost from Nvidia's results, AMD has been advancing its own AI strategy through acquisitions and partnerships.

The company recently closed its roughly $8.2 billion all-stock acquisition of World Labs, the AI research firm founded by Fei-Fei Li.

The deal adds expertise in spatial intelligence, computer vision and 3D world models. Li will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist.

AMD also completed its acquisition of Taalas, a specialist in AI inference silicon.

The technology is expected to be incorporated into the company's accelerator roadmap and system-level offerings alongside Instinct GPUs, EPYC processors, ROCm software and the Helios rack-scale platform.

The company's AI infrastructure ambitions also received support from a six-year agreement signed by TensorWave, an AMD-backed AI cloud provider, to supply OpenAI with 457 megawatts of dedicated computing capacity.

The infrastructure will run on AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs housed in Helios racks, with capacity expected to begin coming online in the first half of 2027.

Analyst upgrades add to AMD optimism

Wall Street analysts have also turned more positive on AMD's prospects, pointing to its competitive position in server CPUs and AI accelerators.

William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform last Thursday, although it did not assign a price target. The firm said the risk-reward profile had shifted in the company's favor.

Oppenheimer also raised its rating on Advanced Micro Devices to Outperform from Perform and assigned the stock a price target of $600.

headline: Nvidia earnings lift CoreWeave, Nebius, Iren stocks, but Kress adds word of caution
html_content:
Shares of neocloud companies CoreWeave, Nebius Group and Iren surged in premarket trading on Wednesday after Nvidia reported stronger-than-expected earnings and issued an upbeat revenue forecast, easing concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

CoreWeave shares CRWV rose more than 4%, while Nebius gained over 6% and Iren climbed more than 5%.

Nvidia's results reinforced expectations that spending on AI chips and data centre infrastructure will remain strong despite recent turmoil surrounding the company and the departure of its longtime CEO Jensen Huang.

The stronger outlook is particularly important for neocloud providers, which have invested heavily in Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) to build AI infrastructure and rent computing capacity to customers such as Microsoft and OpenAI.

CoreWeave and Nebius are also backed by Nvidia which holds equity stakes in both companies.

Nvidia itself surged about 3% in premarket trade.

Nvidia outlook revives confidence in AI demand

Nvidia's results helped reassure investors that its business remains resilient following Huang's exit and the appointment of interim CEO Colette Kress.

“Nvidia has answered the question everyone was asking: the business is bigger than one man. In its first report without Jensen Huang, revenue more than doubled, while data centre sales surged. Interim CEO Colette Kress called it ‘business as usual’ – and the numbers back her up," Kate Leaman, chief market analyst at AvaTrade, said.

“The real headline is the outlook. Guidance of about $130 billion for this quarter, well ahead of forecasts, and a higher growth target for next year suggest demand for AI chips is nowhere near peaking. For a market that was starting to doubt the AI trade, that’s a significant vote of confidence," she said.

Debt and profitability concerns continue to weigh

The latest rally comes after a difficult period for neocloud stocks, which have faced growing concerns lately over their debt-funded expansion and ability to generate sufficient returns on their investments.

Gartner warned that more than 80% of neocloud providers could cease independent operations by 2030.

The research firm pointed to mounting cost pressures and a lack of differentiated business models, arguing that providers must generate returns from AI-optimised infrastructure and associated platforms to remain viable.

CoreWeave's earnings earlier this month had briefly lifted the sector and revived optimism across AI-related stocks.

However, the recovery lost momentum after the controversy surrounding Huang's alleged relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US agencies of spying for Beijing.

The uncertainty over his position at Nvidia weighed on investor sentiment before his eventual resignation.

CoreWeave stock remains down over 18% over the last month, while Nebius has lost over 37% during the same time, and Iren has lost 43%.

Nvidia signals selective support for neoclouds

Nvidia's latest commentary on financing arrangements for AI infrastructure providers has also offered some reassurance to investors, although the company stressed that it would remain cautious.

"Neoclouds and frontier labs are seeing extraordinary demand for AI infrastructure, yet many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support," Kress said in prepared remarks posted on Nvidia's website.

"In response, we have entered into arrangements that help select customers secure the land, power and data-center capacity needed to support their growth."

The comments suggest Nvidia recognises the financing pressures facing companies seeking to expand their data centre capacity, while remaining willing to support selected players.

"We view efforts to unlock land, power and financing as constructive for the broader neocloud ecosystem," Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani said in a note to clients.

On the earnings call, Kress described neoclouds as "an increasingly important part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem, providing additional customers with access to Nvidia compute and expanding the reach of our platform."

However, she emphasised that Nvidia would "continue to be disciplined and selective in our support" of the sector.

Kress said the company would take "a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing", adding that "a lot of things have changed over this last quarter."

While Nvidia's emphasis on disciplined financing indicates that not every neocloud provider can expect support, its comments appeared more reassuring than investors had feared.

The latest earnings and outlook have strengthened confidence in AI infrastructure demand, but questions over debt, cash flows and the long-term viability of individual providers remain.

The comments suggest Nvidia recognises the financing pressures facing companies seeking to expand their data centre capacity, while remaining willing to support selected players. "We view efforts to unlock land, power and financing as constructive for the broader neocloud ecosystem," Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani said in a note to clients. headline: Take Two stock jumps ahead of GTA VI launch: why this analyst sees a 63% upside
html_content:
Shares of Take-Two Interactive Software TTWO rose about 5% in premarket trading on Wednesday ahead of the highly anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), which ends a 13-year wait since the release of its predecessor.

The game is scheduled to become available at midnight Eastern time on Wednesday, with the launch rolling out across time zones.

It had already gone live in New Zealand as Thursday began.

Millions of players have downloaded the game in anticipation of its release.

Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA 6 is widely regarded as one of the most anticipated video game launches in history.

Its production costs are estimated at $1 billion or more, making the commercial stakes particularly high for Take-Two.

GTA 6 preorders point to strong launch demand

The game has generated an estimated 15.88 million digital preorders globally, translating into approximately $1.54 billion in pre-release sales, according to Sensor Tower.

PlayStation accounted for an estimated 75% of preorders, while Xbox represented the remaining 25%.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said last week that preorders were far above the company's initial expectations.

Chief Financial Officer Lainie Goldstein described demand as “extraordinary.”

Early reviews have also been strong.

IGN called the game "unprecedented, unbelievable, and unmissable," while Vice described it as Rockstar Games' "Magnus Opus."

Its Metacritic score currently stands at 99 out of 100, matching the highest score recorded on the platform.

At launch, GTA 6 will be available exclusively on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S.

Players using older Xbox One consoles will be able to stream it through Xbox Cloud Gaming. PC and Nintendo Switch 2 users will have to wait for a later release.

Bank of America sees 63% upside to stock driven by the launch

Bank of America has said the game's release could be a growth-driving catalyst for Take-Two Interactive.

It estimates that GTA 6 needs to generate at least $1.9 billion in sales to meet investor expectations for fiscal 2027.

The brokerage has maintained a Buy rating on Take-Two, with a price target of $330, implying approximately 63% upside from current levels.

Analysts estimate that the initial launch window alone could generate around $600 million in profit for the company.

Longer-term projections also factor in the potential of GTA 6's online component, which some models expect could eventually attract around 60 million monthly active users.

"We recommend being long TTWO through the GTA 6 launch," BofA wrote in a note to investors last month.

"It remains cheap on the LT growth we believe will soon become apparent."

BofA believes Take-Two's weak stock performance in 2026 could present a buying opportunity, given the growth potential of the GTA franchise, particularly the monetization opportunities offered by its hugely popular online mode.

The stock is down about 19% this year.

The bank views monetization of GTA Online as the franchise's most important long-term earnings driver.

"Our LT EPS growth forecast is materially stronger than what we've heard, and a GTA Online launch in 1CQ27 should begin providing tangible evidence of that monetization upside," BofA noted.

"As that strength becomes apparent, we believe the market will need to revise its long-term EPS growth forecasts higher."

Bank of America analyst Omar Dessouky expects the company to release initial sales figures by November 23.

An announcement as early as November 20 could indicate particularly strong first-day demand, he said.

Conversely, the absence of a sales update by November 23 could suggest that launch demand has fallen short of expectations.

Take-Two maintains $8 billion bookings forecast

The launch comes as Take-Two seeks to deliver on its ambitious financial outlook for fiscal 2027.

The company reported second-quarter revenue of $1.50 billion, down from $1.77 billion a year earlier.

Its loss narrowed to $0.29 per share from $0.73 per share in the corresponding period last year.

Take-Two maintained its fiscal 2027 net bookings forecast of $8 billion to $8.2 billion, representing an expected increase of approximately 20.5% from the previous year.

The success of GTA 6 will be central to meeting those expectations.

Bank of America has said it expects Take-Two to issue a press release within the first few days of launch if the initial sales figures are strong.

With substantial preorder demand and favourable early reviews, the launch has set high expectations.

The first few days of sales could provide investors with a clearer indication of whether the game can deliver the commercial performance that the market has been anticipating.

headline: Palo Alto Networks tests 200 EMA as a head and shoulders forms ahead of earnings
html_content:
Palo Alto Networks stock has slumped in the past few weeks, moving from a high of $432 in September to the current $309, which coincides with the 200-day moving average. It has slumped by nearly 30%, mirroring the performance of top software companies, including CrowdStrike and Zscaler. 

Palo Alto Networks earnings are coming up

PANW stock has slumped in the past few months as investors booked profits despite the ongoing revenue and profit growth. The most recent earnings showed that its revenue rose by 34% to $3.4 billion in the fourth quarter. Most notably, the ARR jumped by 63% to $9.1 billion, while its remaining performance obligations rose to over $21.2 billion.

Palo Alto Networks’ business has done well because of the organic demand of its products. At the same time, the company’s growth is also due to its $25 billion acquisition of CyberArk. Its business will likely continue growing demand for cybersecurity amid the ongoing artificial intelligence trends.

According to Gartner, the cost of securing AI is expected to jump to $4.8 billion in 2027, up by over 68% from a year earlier. The report said: 

"This is compounded by growing vulnerabilities and supply chain attacks involving third-party and open-source software in AI projects. Without adequate security and visibility controls, enterprise AI initiatives face a high risk of failure."

The next key catalyst for Palo Alto Networks stock will be its earnings report that comes out on Wednesday. Analysts expect the upcoming report will show that its revenue growth continued in the first fiscal quarter. The average estimate is that its revenue jumped by 33% to over $3.31 billion. Its earnings-per-share is expected to come in at 97 cents, up modestly from 93 cents in the same period last year. 

Valuation concerns remain

One of the main risks that Palo Alto Networks faces is that it is a highly overvalued company. The forward price-to-earnings ratio stands at 74, much higher than the S&P 500 Index’s 18. The multiple is also much higher than the sector median of 18, and the five-year average of 59. 

Palo Alto Networks’ forward price-to-earnings-to-growth ratio of 4.23 is also higher than the sector median of 1.05. The company’s Rule-of-40 multiple is also below 40. Its forward revenue growth is about 33, while the profit margin is 2.67%. 

Analysts have maintained a bullish outlook for PANW stock. Citigroup analysts hiked the target from $410 to $440, while Wells Fargo boosted it from $475 to $525. Other analysts who have a bullish outlook for the company are Yorkville Ives, KeyCorp, and Cantor Fitzgerald. 

Palo Alto Networks stock technical analysis

PANW stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the PANW stock has jumped from $138 in February to a high of $431 in October. Since then, the stock has pulled back to the current $309. 

It has dropped below the 38.2% Fibonacci Retracement level at $320. It also plunged below the 50-day moving average and the Supertrend indicator. At the same time, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and the MACD have continued falling.

The stock has also formed a head-and-shoulders pattern, a common bearish reversal sign. It has already formed the left shoulder and the head. As such, since it has settled along the 200-day Exponential Moving Average, there is a likelihood that it will bounce back to form the right shoulder. If this happens, the stock may bounce back to $350.

On the other hand, there is a risk that the stock may drop further, potentially to the 50% Fibonacci Retracement level of $285. This target is about 10% below the current level.

headline: UBS predicts S&P 500 moving up 12% in 2027 but flags major risks around AI
html_content:
UBS expects US stocks to deliver another year of gains in 2027, forecasting that the benchmark S&P 500 will climb to 8,200 by the end of the year as resilient economic growth and stronger corporate earnings support equities.

However, the investment bank has also warned that the artificial intelligence boom could face a difficult phase as infrastructure investments accelerate faster than the revenue they generate.

Financing constraints, power shortages and questions over profitability are among the risks that could interrupt the current investment cycle.

UBS expects another good year

In its newly released Year Ahead 2027 report on Wednesday, UBS estimated that its S&P 500 target implies approximately 12% upside from current levels.

The bank also moved to a neutral stance on US equities, saying that elevated expectations and market concentration warrant greater caution even as the broader outlook remains constructive.

UBS expects corporate earnings to remain the primary driver of US stock market performance.

The bank forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 29% in 2026, followed by another 15% expansion in 2027.

It believes resilient economic activity and continued AI investment will support corporate profits, although the pace of earnings growth is likely to moderate.

The bank expects inflation to gradually move closer to central bank targets during 2027, although the path could remain uneven.

Geopolitical tensions are also expected to remain elevated, but UBS believes underlying economic fundamentals will continue to determine market performance.

AI spending could face a turning point

AI may experience excess supply and doubts about profitability. Risks include higher financing and execution risks, surging neocloud borrowing costs, permitting constraints, and persistent power shortages.

UBS

Its latest forecast also comes with a more cautious assessment of the AI investment cycle.

UBS expects global AI-related investment to increase from $1 trillion in 2026 to $1.4 trillion in 2027 and $1.5 trillion in 2028.

UBS warned that the enormous investments flowing into AI could eventually create excess computing capacity and put pressure on prices and profitability.

The bank highlighted several risks, including higher borrowing costs for neocloud providers, execution challenges, power shortages and delays in obtaining permits for data center construction.

It also identified specific warning signs that could indicate a turning point in the AI investment cycle.

"We would be concerned about a turning point for AI investment if capacity expansion began to outstrip demand growth, AI lab revenue growth slowed meaningfully, cloud utilization weakened, or falling
AI costs failed to stimulate sufficient new usage to absorb expanding capacity," the bank said.

UBS said investors should remain exposed to AI but favor financially strong hyperscalers with visible monetization opportunities and internally funded investments.

It also favors select semiconductor, computing and chip-equipment companies with established competitive advantages.

How other Wall Street firms see 2027

Other major investment banks are more optimistic about the S&P 500's potential gains.

Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs have both set their 2027 S&P 500 targets at 8,700.

Morgan Stanley expects corporate earnings per share to increase to $420 in 2027 from an estimated $369 in 2026, while Goldman believes improving valuations and lower borrowing costs will support stocks despite slower earnings growth.

The forecasts suggest Wall Street broadly expects further gains, even as concerns about AI investment returns and elevated valuations remain.

UBS, however, is urging investors to be more selective, warning that the next phase of the AI boom may not reward every company participating in the infrastructure buildout.

headline: Lowe’s stock falls 4% despite earnings beat as tariff refunds lift profit
html_content:
Lowe’s shares fell more than 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday despite the home-improvement retailer reporting better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and stronger comparable sales.

The company posted adjusted earnings of $3.10 per share on revenue of $22.8 billion for the quarter ended October 30.

Analysts had expected earnings of $2.88 per share on sales of $22.4 billion, according to FactSet.

Revenue increased 9% from a year earlier, while comparable sales rose 1.8%.

However, the earnings beat included a contribution from tariff refunds, raising questions about the underlying strength of the results.

Tariff refunds contribute to earnings beat

Lowe’s said refunds related to tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act added 34 cents to adjusted earnings per share during the quarter.

That contribution may have tempered investors’ reaction to the results, as the company’s underlying earnings performance was less strong than the headline figure suggested.

The retailer’s gross margin fell 140 basis points to 33% of sales.

Cost of sales increased to 67.1% of revenue, compared with 65.8% in the same period last year.

Operating income also declined as a share of sales, falling to 11.3% from 11.9%.

Lowe’s paid $701 million in dividends during the quarter.

At the end of October, it operated 1,762 stores, covering 197 million square feet of retail selling space.

The shares had already declined 8.6% through Tuesday’s close, adding to the pressure following Wednesday’s results.

Comparable sales outperform expectations

Comparable sales, a closely watched measure of underlying retail performance, increased 1.8% year over year.

The result exceeded the FactSet consensus estimate of 0.4% growth, although it was below the 2.2% increase reported by rival Home Depot for a roughly overlapping period.

Online sales rose 17.4%, while the company also cited solid performance in its professional customer and home services businesses.

“These results reflect the resiliency of our total home strategy,” CEO Marvin Ellison said.

He added that Lowe’s remained confident in its business model and looked forward to discussing its growth opportunities at its Analyst and Investor Conference in December.

The results come amid a difficult housing market, although the latest figures suggest that demand across parts of the home-improvement sector has shown some resilience.

Lowe’s maintains earnings guidance

Lowe’s raised its full-year revenue outlook but maintained its adjusted earnings forecast, a combination that may have disappointed investors expecting stronger guidance following the quarterly beat.

The company now expects full-year sales of approximately $92.5 billion, compared with its previous forecast of $92 billion.

The updated outlook is also above the Wall Street consensus of about $92.1 billion.

However, Lowe’s kept its adjusted earnings guidance at $12.25 per share.

That compares with the analyst consensus of $12.27, suggesting the company does not expect the third-quarter outperformance to translate into a stronger full-year earnings result.

The retailer expects comparable sales to range from flat to an increase of 0.5% for the full year.

Lowe’s reported its results a day after Home Depot also beat Wall Street’s third-quarter earnings expectations.

However, a change in leadership and relatively modest guidance overshadowed Home Depot’s performance.
