headline: Anthropic set to price its IPO tonight, with reports pointing above $80
html_content:
Anthropic is due to price its initial public offering on the evening of Wednesday, 18 November, with shares in the Claude developer scheduled to begin trading the next day on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT.

The offering is still officially marketed at $70–$78 a share.

That is the range in Amendment No. 3 to Anthropic's Form S-1, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 17 November, which kept the terms set a week earlier: 825 million Class A shares, of which 801,351,354 are being sold by the company and 23,648,646 by existing holders.

At $78, the IPO would raise $64.35 billion before underwriting discounts, an Invezz calculation from the filed share count and price. A separate $26 billion private placement of Class N shares is due to close at the same price.

Those reports are not a new filing, and the official range has not changed.

Has Anthropic changed its official IPO price range?

No. The 17 November amendment still estimates an offering price of $70.00 to $78.00 a share and keeps the 825 million share count.

If the underwriters exercise their option to buy a further 123.75 million new shares, gross IPO proceeds could reach $74.00 billion at $78, again an Invezz calculation, as set out in our note on Anthropic's $70–$78 IPO price range.

Nasdaq has already published the listing mechanics. In Data Technical News #2026-28, issued on 11 November, it said Anthropic's Class A common stock, CUSIP 03703U107, is expected to begin trading on Thursday, 19 November.

Why are reports pointing to a price above $80?

The Wall Street Journal reported on 17 November that Anthropic expects to price the shares above $80, citing people familiar with the matter.

On those figures, the Journal said the company would be valued at roughly $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion, up from about $1.33 trillion at the top of the filed range. Those valuation figures are the Journal's, not a number in the prospectus.

Earlier on Tuesday, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber that the IPO was likely to price above the $70–$78 range, and that the company planned to close the order books at 4pm ET that afternoon.

Demand has been strong, if the bank briefing figures are right. Bloomberg News said on 18 November that the offering is close to seven times oversubscribed, after an earlier snapshot of about six times mid-roadshow. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner has said his firm requested a $5 billion allocation and has been quoted as putting demand at 10 to 20 times the shares on offer.

That multiple is a single investor's claim, not a bank-reported order-book figure. The Journal also said long-time backers including Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures and Accel plan to add to their stakes rather than sell. Anthropic has said it expects to allocate up to 20% of the offering to individual investors.

At $80 a share, the 825 million Class A shares would raise $66.00 billion before discounts, an Invezz calculation for illustration only. That is not a filed price.

How did Nvidia's results affect the backdrop?

Nvidia, one of the investors in Anthropic's private placement, reported its first results since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive.

In a statement on 17 November, it said third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue was $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, guided to fourth-quarter revenue of $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, and raised its forecast for fiscal 2028 revenue growth to about 75% from 70%.

CNBC, citing LSEG, said those figures beat estimates of $109.10 billion and $125.1 billion respectively, and that the shares rose more than 3% in extended trading. The Journal had said Anthropic's final price would depend in part on how markets reacted to that report.

What happens after tonight's pricing?

IPO prices are typically set after the US market close on the evening before trading starts. A prospectus supplement, usually a Form 424B4, would then lock in the terms on EDGAR. As of early afternoon in London on 18 November, no such pricing filing had appeared.

Trading is scheduled to begin on Thursday under the ANT ticker.

Hargreaves Lansdown tells UK applicants that the final price and allocations are due to be confirmed on 19 November, with trading expected from 2:30pm London time (9:30am ET). Investors who receive an allocation pay the IPO price; anyone buying once the shares are listed pays the market price. Retail windows are closing as the price is set. Hargreaves Lansdown says UK applications close at 3pm London time on 18 November and may close early. The European offer lists 16:00 CET (15:00 London time) the same day as an indicative deadline; brokers can cut off earlier. The Australian retail offer has already closed.

📘 If you are preparing a brokerage account for Thursday's debut, our guide on how to buy Anthropic stock walks through the steps for buying US-listed shares.

📅 We are tracking the price, valuation and timetable on our Anthropic IPO date, valuation and ticker hub.

The first number that matters is tonight's price: whether it lands inside the official $70–$78 range or comes in above $80, as reported. A new SEC filing would be the official confirmation. Then comes Thursday's first trade, and whether demand that was built in a private order book holds up in public.

headline: Anthropic stock price targets: what analysts say before the ANT debut
html_content:
Wall Street's largest banks will not be publishing Anthropic price targets tonight, because the firms underwriting the IPO are in a research quiet period. That has left a small group of independent houses to put numbers on the stock before Class A shares in the Claude developer are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, 19 November, under the ticker ANT.

The figures sit well above the official $70–$78 range in Amendment No. 3 to Anthropic's Form S-1, filed on 17 November, and above $80, the level at which the Wall Street Journal has reported Anthropic expects to price, citing people familiar with the matter.

That report is not a new filing, and the official range has not changed. Two of the targets reached the public via secondary reports and should be treated as individual views, not a settled Street forecast.

What are the Anthropic stock price targets so far?

The highest 12-month target in circulation is $105, from New Street Research. Analyst Pierre Ferragu initiated coverage with a Buy rating, CNBC reported on 17 November, calling Anthropic a "generational IPO".

He argued that AI would take a growing share of spending on knowledge work, spreading twice as fast as cloud computing did after 2010, across an addressable market 10 times larger, and that the IPO was being priced "on the cautious side". Reuters, citing the same note, said New Street expects revenue of $505 billion by 2030, from $53 billion in 2026 — New Street's projections, not company guidance. We looked at the initiation in more detail when the Buy rating was published.

Freedom Finance, part of Freedom Broker, has a Buy rating and a $101.90 target, according to a note seen by Oninvest on 13 November.

Analyst Alem Bektemirov tied the valuation to further growth in large enterprise customers. Oninvest is a secondary source.

KGI Securities initiated coverage with an Outperform rating on 16 November, StreetInsider reported, naming analyst Zheng Jiemao.

Investing.com reported the accompanying target as $100 a share. That figure also comes via a secondary report.

Morningstar is working from a different kind of number. In an 11 November note, analyst Malik Ahmed Khan, CFA, set a base-case fair-value estimate of $92.00 a share, equal to $1.7 trillion in equity value on his figures.

He described Anthropic as a narrow-moat company and said the $70–$78 IPO range, which he put at up to $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted share count, reflected souring sentiment towards AI rather than the firm's fundamentals.

He saw about 24% upside from the midpoint and viewed the stock as undervalued in that range, with a bull case of $188 and a bear case of $25. The $92 figure is a fair-value estimate, not a 12-month Street target.

Seaport Research Partners has not put a target on the stock. It initiated coverage on 7 November, before the price range was filed, but deferred a rating and a target until after the IPO, according to Investing.com. That report also cited a Seaport discounted-cash-flow valuation of about $1.64 trillion, which is not a published price target and predates the filed range.

How much upside do those numbers imply?

From the $78 top of the official range, New Street's $105 target implies about 35% upside, Freedom's $101.90 about 31%, KGI's $100 about 28%, and Morningstar's $92 fair value about 18%. From the $74 midpoint, those figures are about 42%, 38%, 35% and 24%.

From $70, New Street's target implies 50% upside. If the deal prices above $80, as the Journal has reported, the same four figures would imply about 31%, 27%, 25% and 15%. A sharp jump on Thursday would narrow the gap further for anyone buying in the open market rather than in the IPO.

Why have the underwriting banks not published targets?

Because they are in a research quiet period. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the representatives of the underwriters, according to the prospectus.

Under FINRA Rule 2241, firms that participated in an IPO of a company that is not an emerging growth company are generally barred from publishing research about the issuer for 10 calendar days after the offering date. The older 25-day research blackout no longer applies. A broader set of bulge-bracket targets is therefore unlikely in the first days of trading. Seaport has said it will return with a rating and a target after the IPO.

The views already out are clustered, and they are all constructive at the $70–$78 range. They do not remove the risks in the prospectus, including large compute commitments and a history of GAAP losses.

Anthropic reported a net loss of $104.0 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, including $94.3 billion of fair-value changes on convertible notes and related instruments.

headline: Google stock analysis: may benefit from Anthropic IPO but major risks remain
html_content:
Google stock has plunged and moved into a bear market after falling by over 30% from the year-to-date high. GOOG was trading at $277, down sharply from a high of $403. This retreat may continue as the company continues to face major headwinds. 

Google to benefit from Anthropic IPO, but gains may be short-lived

Alphabet is set to be one of the biggest beneficiaries of Anthropic’s IPO, which is scheduled for today. Google has emerged as one of the company’s largest investors, holding a 14% stake. 

If Anthropic debuts at a $1.5 trillion valuation, that stake would be worth $210 billion, a substantial return on an investment of less than $10 billion. The value would climb even higher if the stock jumps after the listing.

Alphabet was also one of the biggest beneficiaries of SpaceX’s IPO since it is now its biggest investor. The company owns 555 million shares, currently valued at $78 billion. At its peak after the IPO, this stake was worth over $124 billion. 

The risk, however, Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic will start falling if the stock trades as other newly listed companies. For example, SpaceX stock initially surged after the IPO and then dropped by over 50% within a few days. Other recent IPOs like Circle Internet Group, Medline, Figma, and Klarna have all plunged after the IPO. 

Alphabet’s business is facing headwinds and tailwinds

The most recent results showed that Alphabet’s business is facing headwinds and tailwinds. On the positive side, the company’s cloud revenue is soaring as demand from AI companies surge. Its revenue soared by 103% in the third quarter, driven by AI infrastructure. 

The company’s Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon have seen substantial growth, with the Gemini app having over 1 billion downloads. Its models are processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, app by 40% from the second quarter. 

On the other hand, however, there are signs that its AI investments are cannibalizing its core business. Google Search made over $63 billion in the third quarter, while YouTube Ads, Google Network, and subscriptions, platforms and devices grew by 9%, 1%, and 11%, respectively. TPU, its chips are also doing well.

The challenge, however, is that the company is spending aggressively in its business. Its capex jumped to over $51.35 billion last quarter, up from $44 billion in the second quarter. As a result, the company has started burning cash. Its free cash flow stood at negative $9 billion, a big reversal after making over $24 billion in the same period last year. It has burned over $14 billion in the last two quarters. 

The company has also continued raising cash. It recently raised $80 billion to raise cash, including from Berkshire Hathaway. It also recently raised $3.8 billion in Hong Kong. 

These fears explain why analysts have slashed their targets for the stock. UBS Group slashed its target from $380 to $320, while Wells Fargo reduced the target to $365. Other analysts who slashed their targets after earnings are from BMO, Cantor Fitzgerald, Piper Sandler, and Scotiabank.

Google stock technical analysis

GOOG stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the GOOG stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has dropped from $403 to the current $277. It gapped lower after the recent earnings report.

The current price is along the 50% Fibonacci Retracement level. It has also slumped below the 50-day moving average and the Supertrend indicator. 

Therefore, there are signs that the stock is in an overall bear market, which may continue in the coming months. In the long term, however, the stock will likely bounce back.

headline: Nasdaq rises as Nvidia forecast lifts stocks; Anthropic IPO in focus
html_content:
US stocks opened higher on Wednesday as Nvidia’s stronger-than-expected revenue forecast eased concerns about the chipmaker and lifted sentiment across stocks.

Investors were also looking ahead to the pricing of Anthropic’s initial public offering, which could provide an important test of demand for companies linked to the AI boom.

Nvidia shares rose 1.6% in trading after the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

That was above the average analyst estimate of $125.25 billion, according to LSEG data.

The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.35% while the S&P 500 rose 0.13%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 210 points.

Nvidia forecast boosts chipmakers and AI stocks

Nvidia’s outlook helped ease investor concerns following the sudden departure of former CEO Jensen Huang last week.

Uncertainty surrounding the company's leadership and future prospects had weighed on confidence in the AI trade.

The company's board dismissed the possibility of rehiring Huang on Tuesday, despite a campaign calling for his return.

Its latest revenue forecast nevertheless provided reassurance about its near-term business outlook.

Companies involved in AI infrastructure reversed premarket gains after the market opened.

Neocloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius fell 5.4% and 0.79%, respectively.

Data centre-related firms IREN and Applied Digital fell between 0.25% and 2.4%.

Nvidia's shares could remain under scrutiny as investors assess developments following Huang's exit.

The company's latest forecast has helped restore some confidence, but uncertainty around its leadership remains a factor for the stock.

Anthropic IPO pricing in focus

With Nvidia's results out of the way, attention is shifting to Anthropic's IPO pricing later on Wednesday.

The creator of the Claude chatbot is targeting a valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion.

The offering would mark the first-ever IPO by a frontier AI model developer and provide an indication of Wall Street's appetite for businesses at the centre of the artificial intelligence boom.

The timing makes the listing particularly significant for technology investors.

Nvidia's forecast has reinforced expectations for continued demand in the AI sector, while Anthropic's proposed valuation will test how much investors are willing to pay for a leading AI model developer.

Fed policy and other stocks in focus

Monetary policy was another major focus for markets.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Wednesday that the central bank should either raise interest rates by 50 basis points at its December meeting or signal a more aggressive response to inflation.

Investors were also awaiting the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting, due later on Wednesday, for further clues about the policy outlook.

Traders were almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate increase next month, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Several Federal Reserve officials had called for more aggressive rate increases following a hotter-than-expected October inflation report.

Among individual stocks, Lowe's fell 1% in trading after forecasting annual profit below Wall Street expectations, despite raising its sales outlook.

Target gained 4% following its quarterly results.

Take-Two Interactive moved in the opposite direction, gaining 6.1% as the global rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game began.

headline: Why is gold price down today? Gold futures slip 2.5% to September 2025 low
html_content:
US gold futures slipped on Wednesday to their lowest level since September 2025, as hawkish Federal Reserve comments and a stronger dollar hit the non-yielding metal.

COMEX gold futures for December delivery were down $96.00, or 2.48%, at $3,768.20 an ounce at 13:21 UK time.

The contract hit a session low of $3,744.60, down 3.1% from Tuesday's price.

Spot gold was down 2.04% at $3,770.65 at 13:21 UK time after touching $3,742.71.

What happened to gold price today?

December futures traded near $3,857 when trading reopened at 23:00 UK time on Tuesday, fell below $3,800 before 03:00 UK time and slid again shortly before 13:00 UK time, COMEX data via TradingView showed.

The low took the contract below Monday's previous 52-week low of $3,835.20 and left front-month gold futures about a third below their 52-week high of $5,626.80, set on January 29.

The selling spread across precious metals.

COMEX silver futures for December delivery were down 3.43% at $45.735 an ounce, according to COMEX data.

Why is gold price falling?

The main driver is the Fed. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday that the US likely needs several more rate hikes, in remarks at the Central Bank of Argentina.

“The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve price stability in a timely manner,” Musalem said.

New York Fed President John Williams told Axios that the AI boom could argue for further rate increases, though he did not see a need for “dramatic action”.

Higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding gold, which pays no interest.

The US 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.115%. The Fed's target range is 3.75% to 4%.

The dollar added to the pressure.

The US dollar index rose 0.16% to 103.77 after touching 103.91, a 52-week high, according to TradingView.

A firmer dollar makes bullion expensive for buyers using other currencies. The dollar also hit a 19-month high last week.

What happens next?

Minutes from the Fed's October 27-28 meeting are due at 19:00 UK time on Wednesday.

A hawkish tone could keep the dollar and yields elevated. For gold, the next test is whether futures can hold above Wednesday's $3,744.60 low.

Should you buy gold now?

Gold is falling as markets price in higher US rates, and the downtrend has not yet turned.

Despite the near-term concern, Goldman Sachs sees the precious metal reaching $4650 by the end of 2027.

If investors are confused between buying bullion, a gold ETF or mining stocks, you can read this guide on how to invest in gold to learn about the ways you can invest and the opportunities and risks that prospective investors should know.

Tonight's Fed minutes will show whether the hawkish shift behind gold's slide has further to run.

headline: Why Micron stock is falling despite strong Nvidia results?
html_content:
Micron Technology MU shares fell in early trading on Wednesday as investors remained cautious about the broader fallout from Nvidia's leadership crisis, even after the chip giant delivered strong quarterly results.

Micron was down around 0.88% at 10:06 AM ET, trading near $707. The decline came after the stock had gained in after-hours trading following Nvidia's earnings report on Tuesday.

The weakness reflected lingering concerns across the artificial intelligence trade, with peer Sandisk also falling in early trading.

Nvidia shares also traded lower during Wednesday's session despite forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion and reporting third-quarter sales of $115.8 billion, comfortably above analyst expectations.

Nvidia results could help Micron

Nvidia's latest results included a significant increase in its supply commitments, which rose to $390 billion from $279 billion in the previous quarter.

The company said the commitments were primarily related to multi-year procurement of memory supply, potentially providing a boost to manufacturers such as Micron that are expanding production of high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

HBM chips are a critical component of AI infrastructure, enabling processors to access large volumes of data at high speeds.

Micron is one of the key suppliers seeking to benefit from rising demand for these specialized memory products.

However, the market response suggested that strong demand forecasts alone were not enough to ease concerns about the risks surrounding the AI infrastructure buildout.

Nvidia leadership uncertainty continues to weigh on sentiment

The controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure has added another layer of uncertainty to the AI trade.

Huang had offered to return to the role if the board determined that his reinstatement would be in the company's best interest.

However, Nvidia's board rejected the proposal and said it would proceed with a search for a permanent successor.

Investors are now watching whether the leadership transition could affect Nvidia's strategy, particularly its aggressive investment and financing arrangements supporting AI infrastructure customers.

The broader market backdrop has also remained challenging for semiconductor stocks, with investors questioning whether AI-related capital spending can maintain its pace amid regulatory, political and financing concerns.

RBC reiterates Buy rating on Micron with $1,500 target

Despite the pressure on the stock, RBC Capital Markets maintained a bullish stance on Micron.

Analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated a Buy rating and a $1,500 price target on Tuesday. The target stands well above Micron's recent trading range of around $700.

Pajjuri has highlighted Micron's positioning in high-bandwidth memory, the prospect of firmer pricing and tighter industry supply-demand conditions as factors that could support earnings growth.

Broader Wall Street sentiment also remains positive.

Data from Google Finance showed 28 Buy ratings and one Hold among 29 analysts covering Micron, with an average price target of approximately $1,624.

Micron's next earnings report, expected in December, should provide investors with a clearer picture of demand for its memory products, pricing trends and the company's ability to capitalize on AI infrastructure spending.

Until then, the stock could remain sensitive to developments surrounding Nvidia and broader sentiment toward AI-related investment.

headline: AI reputation management after a hack: why engines skip your incident report
html_content:
AI engines quote the page that holds the claim they are writing, and after a hack, that is rarely your own post-mortem.

Ledger published its response to the CryptoBilis implant attack on 15 October.

By the next morning, ChatGPT was quoting it, while Google still did not show it.

That morning, we asked four AI engines 10 questions about the incident, and Ledger's post appeared as a source in 5 of the 40 answers. The other 35 did not cite it.

An engine treats your incident report as one source among many and cites it only when it holds the exact claim the answer needs.

AI reputation management after a hack starts with writing those claims into the page.

A hack ends in a week. AI keeps telling the story for months.

This column is part of Crisis Memory, ICODA's November series on what ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini say about crypto brands after a crisis, with insights from Vlad Pivnev, Anastasia Marmuzevich, Anastasia Shalepina and Artyom Abbasov.

Did AI quote Ledger's post-mortem?

Only partly: ChatGPT cited the 15 October post in 4 of its 10 answers, Perplexity in 1 of 10, and Claude and Gemini never did.

ChatGPT sent 24 of its 34 citations to Ledger's own sites, including the 2020 breach notice and the 2023 Connect Kit report.

Claude sent 1 of its 52 there and built its answers from BleepingComputer, Help Net Security, The Hacker News and Bitquery.

Perplexity cited 232 sources across its 10 answers, and Ledger's post appeared in one of them.

Gemini skipped web search in 6 of its 10 answers, and none of those answers mentioned the incident.

How do AI engines pick a source after a hack?

An engine cites the page that contains the claim it is writing, so every claim your post-mortem leaves out gets sourced from someone else.

Ledger's answers show that rule in three claims.

In the second row, Claude gave Bitquery's $102.0M across 324 wallets and Specter's $86M+, then added: "Ledger itself said it has not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost."

In the third row, the post is dated 15 October and mentions no earlier statement, although Ledger had spoken on 9 October and confirmed the implant on 10 October.

Does a Google ranking mean AI search visibility?

No: on 16 October, ChatGPT quoted Ledger's post while Google did not show it, so rank and AI search visibility need separate tracking.

For the query "ledger hack", an old phishing-campaigns page still held #2, and the 15 October response was missing. Engines run their own retrieval, so a page can be quoted before it ranks.

Google's AI Overviews diverged by market too: after the news broke, they vanished from brand queries such as "ledger" in the US, UK, France and Germany, and stayed in Malaysia and Indonesia, where they cited crisis coverage within one to three days.

"First hours, nobody recalls statement quality; they remember search results," said Anastasia Marmuzevich, Head of PR at ICODA.

Old pages compete with the new one. ChatGPT cited Ledger's 2020 breach notice and 2023 incident report next to the new post.

In the Crisis Memory prompts about Ledger, the 2020 leak appeared in 25 of 48 answers and the 2026 implant in 15.

What should an incident page contain so AI quotes it?

Write the page as a set of claims an engine can lift: dated milestones, confirmed numbers, who is affected and what users got back.

  • Date every milestone: the first statement, the confirmation, and each update. A page that shows one date hands the engine that date.
  • State what is confirmed and what is not, with numbers where you have them. Without them, engines fill the gap with Specter's $86M and Bitquery's $102M.
  • Put the recovery in the same paragraph as the hack. In our Crisis Memory data, recovery came up in 33 of 34 Bitget answers that mention the hack, 30 of 38 for Bybit, and 11 of 45 for Kelp DAO.
  • Turn the questions people ask into headings, such as "Were users compensated?" and "Is the device safe to use?", and answer each in the first sentence.
  • Get one independent outlet to repeat your facts: 51 of Claude's 52 citations went to third-party sites.
  • Check all four engines in the first week, because answers barely move afterwards. When we repeated the audit 24 days later, only 2 of 40 carried news from after 16 October.

"Treat the incident page as an answer sheet: every question an engine might get about the hack should have a dated, quotable answer on it," Anastasia Shalepina, AI SEO Expert, ICODA.

Method: API versions of ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini with web search, US location, one run per prompt, 16 October 2026. Crisis Memory covers 296 answers across five crypto brands.

headline: DJT stock is at a record low: Why Trump Media could fall to $2 or lower
html_content:
Trump Media stock has remained under pressure this week and is hovering near its all-time low. DJT traded at $4 on Wednesday, down more than 70% so far this year. The sell-off may continue through the rest of the year, and there is a risk that the stock could fall below $2 over the longer term.

Trump Media faces a $1 billion debt wall

Trump Media, the parent company of Truth Social, is facing some major risks. One of them is that the company needs to repay about $1 billion by November 30. 

The debt emerged from the company’s decision to invest in Bitcoin, mirroring the strategy that Michael Saylor perfected at Strategy. 

It issued that debt in May last year. According to its prospectus, the debt matures on May 29 2028, but its holders can demand cash repayment on November 30th. The stock remains much lower than its conversion price, meaning that cash repayment is more attractive than converting. 

The company is now in a bind as it does not have that money in its balance sheet. As a result, the options include selling its Bitcoin holdings, which are now valued at about $1 billion. It can also decide to raise cash by selling shares, a move that will dilute its shareholders. Also, it can use some of its cash to repay the debt.

These challenges are compounded by the ongoing deterioration of Bitcoin and other coins. Bitcoin dropped to $63,857, down by 27% from its highest point in October. It has also dropped by nearly 50% from its highest point in October last year. At its all-time high, its Bitcoin holdings were worth about $2 billion. 

Trump Media is facing other challenges

The company is facing other risks. For example, Democrats recently won the Senate and the House of Representatives, and will most likely investigate the company for its Truth+ product. This is a service that lets people and companies pay about $100,000 a month to get access to Truth posts from the most active users on its platform. This service is widely seen as a way for Trump to monetize the presidency. 

Further, Trump’s approval rating has continued falling after the midterm elections. This rating stands at 31%, the lowest point of both of his terms, and the trend may continue since he is not working to end the Iran war. As a result, with the president’s popularity fading, there is a likelihood that traffic to the website will also drop. Indeed, SimilarWeb data shows that the traffic dropped by over 22% in October.

Trump Media has a narrow path for making real profits. Its last earnings report showed that its net profit rose to over $409 million from a loss of $238 million in the previous quarter. However, most of these profits came from its Bitcoin gains, which have now reversed.

Further, in the long term, it is hard to imagine how the company survives, especially when Trump leaves office.

DJT stock price technical analysis

Trump Media stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the DJT stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months and is now at its all-time low. It has already dropped below the important support level of $6.96, its lowest level on June 25. 

The stock remains below all moving averages and the Ichimoku cloud, a sign that bears remain in control. Also, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and the MACD have continued moving downwards. 

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling as its fundamentals deteriorate. In the long term, this decline may hit $2 and below.

headline: Bitcoin price today: BTC below $64,000 as Citi cuts target to $99,532
html_content:
Key takeaways

  • Bitcoin traded below $64,000 as Citi cut its 12-month target to $99,532.
  • US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $239.9 million on Tuesday, led by BlackRock's IBIT.
  • Minutes from the Fed's October meeting are due at 19:00 UK time.

Bitcoin price today slipped further below $64,000 on Wednesday, November 18, after Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin target to $99,532 and as US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung back to outflows ahead of the Federal Reserve's October minutes.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $63,465 on Coinbase at 15:08 UK time, down 2.2% from Tuesday's close of $64,873 at midnight UTC.

Citi cuts its 12-month Bitcoin and Ethereum targets

Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin price target to $99,532 from $113,000 and its Ethereum target to $2,838 from $3,028, according to a research note reported by CNBC on Wednesday.

Citi analyst Alex Saunders said a rangebound crypto market had broken lower and that both assets had fallen since the bank's previous update.

He downgraded Citi's near-term outlook for capital inflows to neutral after Bitcoin dropped below its 200-day moving average.

Saunders pointed to weaker ETF demand, with Bitcoin fund flows in net outflow so far this year and Ethereum funds recording outflows in each of the past seven weeks.

Futures positioning pointed to broader deleveraging, he said, while a stronger US dollar, higher real yields and a rise in equity-market volatility had tightened the backdrop for crypto.

Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 is again running above its correlation with gold, according to the note.

Citi had raised those targets to $113,000 and $3,028 in early October.

Even after the cut, the new Bitcoin target implies about 57% upside from Wednesday's Coinbase price. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, leaving about 60% implied upside to Citi's $2,838 Ethereum target.

What happened to Bitcoin price today?

Bitcoin traded between $63,001 and $64,933 on Coinbase on Wednesday, with sellers capping every move towards $65,000.

The world's largest cryptocurrency is about 16% below its November 9 high of $75,500 on Coinbase.

It hit $61,946 on Coinbase on November 15, its lowest point of the month so far.

The rest of the market was also lower. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, while XRP was at $0.98.

Why is Bitcoin price falling?

ETF demand has faded again, the same pressure Citi cited in its target cut.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $239.9 million on Tuesday, November 17, according to Farside Investors.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $209.5 million of that.

That reversed a small $7.9 million inflow on Monday.

Since October 30, the funds have lost about $3.2 billion in 13 sessions, based on Farside's daily data.

US spot Ether ETFs lost $29.1 million on Tuesday, Farside data show.

Interest rates are the other weight.

The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, but Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike.

On Tuesday, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy "will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027", in remarks in Argentina.

Higher rates make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive.

The US dollar index touched a 52-week high of 103.91 on Wednesday, according to TradingView.

What happens next?

The Fed's minutes from its October 27-28 meeting are due at 19:00 UK time on Wednesday.

Traders will look at how many officials backed a hike and how soon. The Fed's next decision is on December 9.

Bitfinex analysts said in their Bitfinex Alpha report on Monday that they expect Bitcoin to trade between $61,800 and $69,400 this week, with another test of the November 15 low possible.

They named $57,803, Bitcoin's July cycle low, as a key level to watch, and said a recovery above $72,700 with renewed ETF inflows would show selling pressure is fading.

Farside's figures for Wednesday's ETF flows will show whether institutional selling has eased.

Should you buy Bitcoin now?

Bitcoin has held above last week's low, but ETF outflows and a hawkish Fed are still weighing on it.

Citi's reduced 12-month target of $99,532 still sits well above the current price, though that is a forecast, not a recommendation.

A hawkish set of minutes could push Bitcoin back towards $62,000, while a softer tone could bring buyers back.

If you plan to buy Bitcoin, compare fees and security on our list of the best crypto exchanges.

For more coverage, see our latest cryptocurrency news.

headline: When could Anthropic stock join the MSCI, Russell, FTSE and Nasdaq-100?
html_content:
Index funds may be among the larger buyers of Anthropic stock after it lists, but they will not all arrive on the first day, and they will not all arrive at once.

Anthropic is due to price its IPO on 18 November and to start trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on 19 November under the ticker ANT, as set out in Nasdaq Data Technical News #2026-28 and the company's latest S-1 amendment. The official range is still $70–$78 a share for 825 million Class A shares.

The timetable is now clearer than it was at the start of the roadshow, and slower than some early commentary suggested. Thanksgiving has pushed two FTSE Russell additions later into December. The S&P 500 is not in prospect at listing at all.

When could Anthropic join MSCI?

MSCI has published the rule, not the decision. In a 12 November announcement for its Global Standard indexes, it said it would apply its usual methodology for large IPOs.

To qualify for early inclusion, the stock must meet MSCI's eligibility rules, with the exception of the usual length-of-trading and liquidity screens, and must have a company full market capitalisation of at least 1.8 times the Interim Market Size-Segment Cutoff, plus a free-float-adjusted market capitalisation of at least 1.8 times one-half of that cutoff, measured at the close of the first or second trading day.

Any greenshoe publicly announced as exercised before MSCI's decision would be included in those calculations.

The decision would be announced no earlier than the first day of trading and no later than before the opening of the third trading day. If the first trade is on 19 November, that third session would be Monday, 23 November. Early inclusions are usually effective as of the close of the tenth trading day, but if that date falls close to a scheduled review, the addition is aligned with the review instead.

On that basis, if ANT begins trading on 19 November and meets the tests, inclusion would be effective as of the close on 30 November 2026, or 1 December, coinciding with the November 2026 Index Review. That remains a conditional outcome.

Why did FTSE Russell push the dates back?

Because a standard fast-entry calendar would have landed next to Thanksgiving.

In two informative notices dated 13 November, FTSE Russell said it will confirm after the first day of trading whether Anthropic meets the tests, and will issue a further notice after that session if it does.

For the Russell US Equity Indexes, the fast-entry threshold is $17.942 billion of investable market capitalisation. The usual rule would add an eligible IPO after the close of the fifth trading day. If the first trade is on 19 or 20 November, FTSE Russell said the stock would instead be added with the December semi-annual reconstitution, after the close on Friday, 11 December, effective at the open on Monday, 14 December, if it meets the criteria.

For the FTSE Global Equity Index Series, the current fast-entry thresholds for FTSE North America are $43.741 billion of full market capitalisation and $14.580 billion of investable market capitalisation. If ANT qualifies, it would be added with the December review, after the close on Friday, 18 December, effective at the open on Monday, 21 December. Until those notices appear, inclusion is not confirmed.

Could ANT enter the Nasdaq-100 in December?

It might be considered. It has not been added. Nasdaq has not published a notice naming ANT as a Nasdaq-100 constituent.

Under the Nasdaq-100 methodology, a newly listed security can be considered for fast-track inclusion if it meets the index's eligibility and ranking tests.

The next scheduled reconstitution is widely expected to take effect on 21 December 2026, and some secondary reports have already treated that date as a likely entry point for Anthropic. That is a reading of the rulebook, not an official Nasdaq announcement, and should not be confused with the MSCI and FTSE Russell calendars above.

Why is the S&P 500 not in play at listing?

Because it still requires a seasoning period and a profitability test, and S&P Dow Jones Indices has declined to waive either for megacap companies.

In the results of a June 2026 consultation, S&P DJI left the S&P 500 rules unchanged: IPOs should have traded on an eligible exchange for at least 12 months, and companies must have positive GAAP net income from continuing operations in the most recent quarter and in the sum of the most recent four consecutive quarters.

If ANT lists on 19 November 2026, the 12-month clock would run into mid-November 2027. The profitability test is a separate hurdle.

Anthropic's prospectus shows a history of GAAP net losses, including a net loss of $104.0 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, of which $94.3 billion was fair-value changes on convertible notes and related instruments.

Even if much of that loss is non-cash, it is still a GAAP net loss, so the stock would not meet the earnings screen at listing.

The broader S&P Total Market Index has a separate fast-track process for eligible IPOs, which Reuters noted on 12 November. That is not an S&P 500 inclusion.

How much passive demand is expected?

The useful estimate on the table is already a few days old, and the calendar has since moved.

Index-rebalance firm Intropic estimated that passive demand from index-tracking funds would account for about 28% of the shares on offer, or roughly $19 billion.

FTSE Russell's Thanksgiving deferral means part of that buying, if it materialises, now sits in mid-December for the Russell US indexes and in the third week of December for FTSE GEIS. MSCI's potential 1 December effective date is still relatively early.

The $19 billion figure should be read as an estimate prepared against a faster calendar, not as a confirmed order for the first two weeks of trading.

Index funds that do buy will be doing so because the rules require it, which can still matter in early trading, but it does not guarantee a higher price.

Investors who want exposure through an index fund will need to check whether the tracker they hold follows a benchmark that is actually adding the stock, and on which date.

Buying ANT directly once trading begins is a different route.

📘 Our guide on how to buy Anthropic stock covers opening an account for US-listed shares once trading begins.

📅 The listing timetable, the official range and the valuation are collected on our Anthropic IPO date, valuation and ticker hub.

headline: Nvidia earnings: investors still need answers to two key questions
html_content:
Nvidia (NVDA) more than doubled its quarterly revenue to nearly $116 billion in its fiscal Q3 and issued impressive guidance for the future as well.

But buying NVDA shares this morning means betting on growth that still has to be earned. Two questions matter for that bet:

  2. If tighter US rules choke off Chinese demand served through Singapore, can it turn those same chips into just as much profit somewhere else?

Nvidia stock is currently down nearly 35% versus its year-to-date high.

Key man risk remains alive for Nvidia stock

While the media narrative this morning is how Nvidia earnings essentially silence the “key man” risk, it’s worth noting that the company’s quarter ended Oct. 25 – about two weeks before its board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation.

Simply put, Huang ran Nvidia for the entire quarter.

So, the earnings beat, and even the guidance, tells investors that orders Nvidia had already secured translated into strong sales. The real test for interim CEO Colette Kress and NVDA stock actually begins with the “next round of orders.”

Kress told CNBC that key cloud customers were still asking for more computing power.

The harder question is whether those customers will keep committing billions to Nvidia’s next generation of chips.

A delayed launch or a large order that goes elsewhere could dent future earnings, turning investors less willing to pay a premium for each dollar Nvidia earns.

China remains a key overhang on NVDA shares

A chip can sit in a Singapore data centre and still do work for a customer in China – the new US rules target some of that remote access.

Nvidia recorded $11.05 billion, about 9.5% of quarterly sales, from direct customers headquartered in China and Hong Kong.

Its print leaves the amount of Chinese demand served through Singapore unknown.

On CNBC, Jim Cramer asked whether other buyers could absorb chips Nvidia might stop shipping to the region without pushing prices down.

Kress explained how Nvidia checks who will use the chips and whether data centres are ready.

But she gave no indication of how quickly alternative buyers could take delivery or whether they would pay the same price.

That remains a key overhang on Nvidia shares.

Technical setup warrants caution on Nvidia

Even from a technical perspective, NVDA shares have not turned attractive yet.

The AI darling currently sits firmly below major moving averages (MAs), with an RSI in the early 20s indicating intense selling pressure.

That said, Wall Street hasn’t thrown in the towel on Nvidia yet.

The consensus rating on the chip-maker remains at Strong Buy, with the mean price target of about $258 indicating massive upside potential from current levels.

headline: Strategy stock falls as analyst warns MSTR could crash to $23
html_content:
Strategy (formerly known as MicroStrategy) MSTR shares fell 4% on Wednesday as a prominent technical analyst warned that the Bitcoin-holding company's stock could plunge to $23, implying a potential decline of approximately 76% from its previous close.

Aksel Kibar, a widely followed Chartered Market Technician (CMT), based his warning on a bearish head-and-shoulders pattern on Strategy's daily share-price chart.

The stock closed at $96.50 on Tuesday, putting the analyst's price target well below its current trading level.

The warning comes as Strategy shares have already lost more than half their value over the past year.

The company has also faced pressure following MSCI's decision to exclude its shares from certain equity indices, raising concerns about its ability to raise capital for further Bitcoin purchases.

Head-and-shoulders pattern signals further downside

Kibar said the head-and-shoulders formation on Strategy's chart remained intact after the stock broke below its neckline earlier this year.

"The H&S top neckline was breached at 101 levels. Then we have seen a sharp rebound that did not negate the pattern with a breach above the high of the right shoulder. The pattern is intact, with a price target of 23," Kibar said in a post on X.

A head-and-shoulders pattern is a technical chart formation characterised by three peaks.

The middle peak, known as the head, is higher than the two surrounding peaks, or shoulders. The lows between these peaks form a support line called the neckline.

The pattern is generally considered bearish when it appears after a substantial price rally.

A break below the neckline can signal a potential reversal, with the price target calculated by measuring the distance between the head and the neckline and projecting it below the breakdown level.

In Strategy's case, the stock fell below the neckline around $101 during the third quarter before rebounding.

However, according to Kibar, the recovery did not rise above the high of the right shoulder, which would have invalidated the formation.

That leaves the bearish technical signal in place, although the $23 level represents an analyst's chart-based projection rather than a guaranteed outcome.

Bitcoin price remains important for Strategy stock

Kibar also linked Strategy's share-price outlook to Bitcoin, given the company's substantial exposure to the cryptocurrency.

On Bitcoin's price chart, the analyst identified a trading range between $60,000 and $82,800.

The range has a lower boundary, or floor, and an upper boundary, or ceiling.

A move below the $60,000 level could signal a continuation of the cryptocurrency's broader downtrend, according to Kibar.

Strategy's shares tend to track Bitcoin's price movements because of the company's large cryptocurrency holdings.

This makes the digital asset's direction an important factor for investors assessing the stock's prospects.

MSCI exclusion adds to investor concerns

Strategy's technical weakness comes alongside concerns about its access to capital.

MSCI recently announced that it would exclude Strategy from its equity indices.

The decision has raised questions about potential pressure on demand for the stock and the company's ability to raise fresh funds to finance additional Bitcoin purchases.

Strategy held 850,849 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $55 billion at the time of writing.

The company's large holdings make it one of the biggest corporate owners of Bitcoin and leave its stock closely tied to the cryptocurrency market.

headline: Can Anthropic IPO beat SpaceX to become the world's largest?
html_content:
Anthropic could price its shares above its proposed $70 to $78 range on Wednesday, putting the maker of Claude on course for one of the biggest stock market debuts ever.

Jay Ritter, director of the University of Florida’s IPO Initiative, told CNBC he expects the deal to “exceed SpaceX as the world’s largest IPO ever.”

At the $80 price he floated, however, Anthropic would still fall short on public proceeds under its current share count.

And for investors buying Anthropic stock as it goes live on Nasdaq, the bigger question is actually how much future profit that price already assumes.

What would it take to beat SpaceX?

At $80 a share, Anthropic’s planned sale of 825 million shares would generate $66 billion before fees, including proceeds going to existing shareholders.

That would rise to $75.9 billion if underwriters bought all the extra shares available to them.

SpaceX’s June debut brought in $75 billion initially and about $85.7 billion after its underwriters exercised their option.

On that like-for-like comparison, Anthropic would need a price above $90 per share with its extra allotment fully used, or a larger offering.

The separate $26 billion private placement with investors including Google and Nvidia boosts the total raised alongside the listing.

But the IPO record counts money raised only through the public offering itself.

Ritter sees a first-day jump in Anthropic stock

Ritter said the shares were “very likely to jump” from his hypothetical $80 offer price.

But using his estimates of a $1.5 trillion valuation and $35.2 billion in trailing 12-month revenue, investors would be paying roughly 43 times annual sales.

In plain terms, that’s about $43 in company value for every dollar Anthropic generated in revenue over the previous year, before paying for the computing power and other costs needed to serve customers.

Ritter said that multiple could look conservative next to Palantir or SpaceX, but “a lot of things have to go right.”

One is keeping customers willing to pay premium prices as competing AI models improve.

Investors who bought SpaceX shares at the time of the IPO haven't done well, with the stock falling 10% since its debut.

What investors are buying beyond the growth story

Ritter also pointed to Anthropic’s public benefit structure as a sign that it takes AI safety seriously.

Its directors must weigh shareholders’ financial interests alongside the interests of people affected by the company and its stated public mission.

In practice, the board has room to back a safety decision even if it slows a product launch or raises costs.

Anthropic’s prospectus says its public benefit initiatives could reduce profitability per share.

The final offer price will settle how close Anthropic gets to SpaceX’s record. For anyone buying after trading starts, a first-day jump raises the bar.

The higher the entry price, the more profit Anthropic must eventually deliver to justify it.

headline: Cathie Wood was right on the money about these 2 stocks
html_content:
Every new artificial intelligence (AI) data center needs chips.

The AI agents running on those chips need to fetch data, call software tools, and interact with websites.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Investment Management found winners on both sides of that buildout.

AMD and Cloudflare have seen explosive rallies since the famed investor first gained exposure to both.

They are proving a perfect example of how AI demand is spreading from the companies that supply the hardware to those that keep the applications running.

AMD turned a server-chip foothold into an AI business

ARK first bought about 640,000 AMD shares in the third quarter of 2018. At the time, they were going for about $31 only.

The firm later exited its position in Advanced Micro Devices, only to reestablish it in early 2023, at roughly $98 each.

As of writing, those same shares are trading at about $507 – suggesting Cathie Wood has secured a more than 5x gain on AMD.

The business behind that massive rally sells two kinds of chips into the same data center.

EPYC server processors handle general computing, while Instinct accelerators do the heavy lifting for AI models.

Demand for both pushed Q3 data center revenue up 97% to $8.5 billion.

The division’s operating profit climbed to $2.9 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier – showing how much of the sales growth is reaching the bottom line.

CEO Lisa Su expects data center chips to account for about 80% of AMD’s revenue in 2027.

That gives AMD more to gain as cloud companies expand capacity and more exposure if they slow the pace of new deployments.

Cloudflare found a way to turn developer adoption into revenue

Cloudflare first appeared in ARK’s reported holdings in the fourth quarter of 2020, when the stock traded at roughly $76.

In comparison, it’s now going for roughly $285, representing about 3.75x return on Cathie Wood’s initial investment.

The company now gives developers a place to run applications and AI agents through Workers – expanding what it can sell to businesses that already depend on its network for both security and performance.

Cloudflare passed 10 million active developers and added a record 158,000 paying customers in its fiscal Q3.

Revenue soared 39% to $782.5 million, and dollar-based net retention reached 122%.

That means the same group of customers generated 22% more revenue over a year after accounting for customers that cut spending or left.

Management also expects GAAP profitability in the fourth quarter, ahead of its earlier target of reaching that milestone by 2028.

The margin story helps explain why.

Workers carries a lower gross margin than some Cloudflare products, but it costs less to sell.

That gives Cloudflare a path to higher operating margins as developers turn experiments into applications they pay to run.

headline: Why is Nvidia stock falling over 2% on Wednesday?
html_content:
Nvidia shares NVDA fell 2.2% on Wednesday, extending their decline to a fifth consecutive session, as the US House Committee on Energy and Commerce demanded a formal briefing from the chipmaker over alleged export control violations and former CEO Jensen Huang's reported links to a suspected Chinese spy.

Representative Brett Guthrie, chairman of the committee, sent a letter to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress requesting that company officials appear before lawmakers no later than December 2.

The inquiry focuses on whether Nvidia circumvented federal restrictions intended to prevent advanced artificial intelligence technology from reaching China.

Lawmakers are also examining allegations that a senior company official attempted to interfere with a federal investigation.

The developments add to the pressure on Nvidia as it navigates a leadership transition and scrutiny over national security concerns, despite strong quarterly results and an upbeat revenue outlook.

Congressional probe focuses on export control allegations

In his letter, Guthrie said the reported events raised questions about Nvidia's compliance with federal export laws and the effectiveness of its security controls.

The congressional investigation centres on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer suspected of helping Chinese companies circumvent US export restrictions.

On November 16, the Justice Department and Commerce Department publicly confirmed a joint criminal investigation into the company.

Reports have also linked Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is alleged to have a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, to suspected Chinese intelligence activities.

According to Guthrie's letter, investigators are examining claims that she established a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia hardware.

Lawmakers are also looking into allegations that the Commerce Department transferred its initial investigation into Megaspeed to the Justice Department last year after Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce officials seeking information about the inquiry.

These allegations have not been established as findings of wrongdoing by Nvidia.

Leadership transition adds to investor concerns

The controversy has coincided with significant changes at Nvidia's senior leadership level.

On November 8, Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair in an internal email to employees and said the company's board had launched an independent investigation into national security concerns raised by media reports.

Four days later, he announced his departure from company leadership.

Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, took over as interim CEO while the company works with an external firm to find a permanent replacement.

The uncertainty has weighed on investor sentiment, with Nvidia shares declining for five consecutive trading sessions and facing the prospect of a seventh consecutive weekly loss.

However, Wall Street analysts have pointed to the company's latest financial results as evidence that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong.

Nvidia reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share, beating analyst expectations by 21 cents.

Revenue reached $115.84 billion, up 103.2% from a year earlier and $7.13 billion above forecasts.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, compared with analyst estimates of $124.89 billion.

The forecast assumes no data centre computing revenue from China.

Analysts remain positive on Nvidia's outlook

Several Wall Street firms have maintained positive views on Nvidia despite the leadership uncertainty.

RBC reiterated its Outperform rating, citing demand that continues to exceed supply, a product roadmap extending over the next three years and limited near-term competitive risks due to industry supply constraints.

The firm also highlighted rising supply purchase commitments as evidence of strong demand visibility.

Morgan Stanley maintained its Overweight rating, pointing to strong demand for AI computing and Nvidia's competitive position.

Its analysts also viewed the company's willingness to provide forward-looking commentary as a positive.

Wedbush raised its price target to $293 from $275 while retaining an Outperform rating.

The firm said Nvidia's near- and medium-term demand outlook remained unchanged despite Huang's departure.

The company also has $227.3 billion remaining under its share buyback authorisation.

Kress described returning capital to shareholders as a top priority during the earnings call and said Nvidia could fully utilise the remaining authorisation by fiscal 2028.

Jefferies said the buyback programme offered another potential source of support for the stock, while noting that investors still need greater visibility into the company's strategic direction following the leadership transition.

Meanwhile, Kress said Nvidia was raising its fiscal 2028 outlook and expected revenue growth of approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% previously and on a higher fiscal 2027 base.

The uncertainty has weighed on investor sentiment, with Nvidia shares declining for five consecutive trading sessions and facing the prospect of a seventh consecutive weekly loss. However, Wall Street analysts have pointed to the company's latest financial results as evidence that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong. Nvidia reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share, beating analyst expectations by 21 cents. Revenue reached $115.84 billion, up 103.2% from a year earlier and $7.13 billion above forecasts. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, compared with analyst estimates of $124.89 billion. The forecast assumes no data centre computing revenue from China. Analysts remain positive on Nvidia's outlook Several Wall Street firms have maintained positive views on Nvidia despite the leadership uncertainty. RBC reiterated its Outperform rating, citing demand that continues to exceed supply, a product roadmap extending over the next three years and limited near-term competitive risks due to industry supply constraints. The firm also highlighted rising supply purchase commitments as evidence of strong demand visibility. Morgan Stanley maintained its Overweight rating, pointing to strong demand for AI computing and Nvidia's competitive position. Its analysts also viewed the company's willingness to provide forward-looking commentary as a positive. Wedbush raised its price target to $293 from $275 while retaining an Outperform rating. The firm said Nvidia's near- and medium-term demand outlook remained unchanged despite Huang's departure. The company also has $227.3 billion remaining under its share buyback authorisation. Kress described returning capital to shareholders as a top priority during the earnings call and said Nvidia could fully utilise the remaining authorisation by fiscal 2028. Jefferies said the buyback programme offered another potential source of support for the stock, while noting that investors still need greater visibility into the company's strategic direction following the leadership transition. Meanwhile, Kress said Nvidia was raising its fiscal 2028 outlook and expected revenue growth of approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% previously and on a higher fiscal 2027 base. headline: SpaceX stock rises as Citi sees wireless network and AI growth potential
html_content:
SpaceX shares SPCX gained around 1.7% on Wednesday as investors assessed the company's expanding wireless ambitions, plans for artificial intelligence infrastructure in Texas and continued launch activity.

The stock also received support from positive analyst commentary.

Morgan Stanley reiterated its Overweight rating, suggesting investors consider buying shares during periods of weakness.

The brokerage said SpaceX had shown resilience despite volatility in AI-related stocks and could become a more durable holding as the market's AI investment theme evolves.

Meanwhile, Citi maintained its $280 price target on SpaceX, implying approximately 92% upside from current levels, as it examined the company's potential entry into the US mobile network market.

Citi sees SpaceX building its own mobile network

Citi believes SpaceX may need to develop a substantial ground-based network if it wants to compete with established US wireless operators, even as it plans to use Starlink satellites to reduce its reliance on traditional telecommunications infrastructure.

The brokerage highlighted comments from SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen at the TomorrowX Summit, where he outlined the company's plans for a wireless network that would rely less heavily on conventional cell towers.

SpaceX believes Starlink satellites could carry network traffic through space rather than depending as heavily on traditional fibre connections.

This could allow the company to operate a more efficient network using smaller cell sites.

However, Citi said a substantial number of macro cell sites would still be necessary, particularly in urban and suburban areas.

Ground infrastructure would help provide reliable indoor coverage and sufficient network capacity.

SpaceX could build its own network, acquire an existing telecommunications operator or operate as a mobile virtual network operator using another company's infrastructure.

Citi considers building its own network the most likely option.

Last month, SpaceX agreed to acquire Grain Management's nationwide portfolio of 800 MHz wireless spectrum licences, covering up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum.

The acquisition could strengthen Starlink Mobile's coverage, particularly indoors and in areas with weaker cellular signals.

JPMorgan had also highlighted the need for SpaceX to develop ground-based infrastructure to compete with established US telecom operators.

Texas approves SpaceX data centre and power project

SpaceX shares also gained after Texas resumed permitting for artificial intelligence facilities and approved the company's proposed data centre and natural-gas power plant, according to Politico.

The $24 billion project is located in the Rio Grande Valley, where SpaceX is headquartered.

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality issued a permit allowing the company to install 35 natural-gas-powered turbines.

The facility is expected to generate 750 megawatts of electricity.

It will not be connected to the state's electrical grid, and the permit allows it to emit up to 248 tons of nitrogen oxides annually.

The approval follows a September order by outgoing Texas Governor Greg Abbott to pause approvals for such projects.

Abbott lost his re-election bid earlier this month to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who won the election to become the state's next governor.

Upcoming Falcon 9 launch

SpaceX is also targeting Thursday, November 19, for a Falcon 9 launch of the USSF-317 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

The four-hour launch window is scheduled to open at 6:46 p.m. Pacific time, or 9:46 p.m. Eastern. A backup opportunity is available on Friday, November 20, at 8:26 p.m. Pacific time.

The first-stage booster is scheduled to make its 11th flight, following previous launches including NROL-105, USSF-385 and eight Starlink missions.

SpaceX plans to land the booster on its Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean.

headline: Evening digest: Anthropic IPO demand surges as gold and oil prices fall
html_content:
US markets faced mixed signals on Wednesday as Anthropic prepared to price its highly anticipated initial public offering amid exceptional investor demand.

Oil prices fell more than 2% after US crude and fuel inventories recorded larger-than-expected increases, while gold dropped to its lowest level in more than a year as hawkish Federal Reserve commentary strengthened the dollar and Treasury yields.

Nvidia shares also extended their losing streak as US lawmakers sought answers over alleged export control violations and reports involving former CEO Jensen Huang.

Anthropic IPO attracts nearly $500B in demand

Anthropic is considering increasing the size of its IPO and pricing shares above the initial range of $70 to $78, CNBC reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The company closed its order books on Tuesday, with institutional demand reaching approximately $400 billion and retail demand approaching $100 billion.

These indications of interest are non-binding, and the final offering terms remain subject to change.

Anthropic initially planned to offer 825 million shares, potentially raising up to $64.35 billion at the top of its proposed price range.

The company is expected to announce its final IPO price after Wednesday's market close.

The listing is a significant test of investor appetite for AI companies.

Anthropic's proposed offering has attracted more demand than SpaceX's IPO, which raised $85.7 billion in June.

The company's prospectus reported revenue of $33.24 billion for the nine months ended September 30, an increase of approximately 1,200% year over year.

However, it recorded a net loss of $104 billion during the period, largely reflecting changes in the fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities.

Its run-rate revenue reached approximately $81 billion at the end of October.

Oil prices fall as US inventories surge

Oil prices declined after the US Energy Information Administration reported larger-than-expected increases in crude and fuel inventories.

Brent crude futures fell 1.7% to $91.50 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate dropped 3.7% to $82.80.

Both benchmarks were on track to lose approximately 20% in November amid expectations of a global supply surplus.

US crude inventories increased by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13, significantly exceeding expectations for a 58,000-barrel rise.

Gasoline stocks climbed by 5.2 million barrels, compared with forecasts for a 1.6 million-barrel increase.

Distillate inventories also rose by 1.6 million barrels.

Rising Middle Eastern exports have added to expectations of greater supply, although the US-Iran conflict continues to threaten shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

Recent attacks on commercial vessels and infrastructure in the region have highlighted the risks to oil transportation.

Gold hits one-year low as rate hike expectations rise

Gold prices dropped 3% to $3,729.28 an ounce, reaching their lowest level since September 2025. US gold futures declined 3.4% to $3,732.10.

A stronger US dollar and rising Treasury yields weighed on the precious metal as investors increased expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank needed a more aggressive response to inflation, either through a 50-basis-point increase in December or a faster pace of rate hikes in 2027. Other officials have also indicated that additional increases may be necessary.

Markets priced in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point December rate hike and an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Silver fell 5.3%, platinum declined 4.6%, and palladium lost 2.6%.

Nvidia stock extends losing streak amid congressional probe

Nvidia shares fell 2.5%, extending their decline to a fifth consecutive session as the House Committee on Energy and Commerce demanded a formal briefing over alleged export control violations.

Committee chairman Brett Guthrie requested that interim CEO Colette Kress arrange for company officials to appear before lawmakers by December 2.

The inquiry involves Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed and allegations that it helped Chinese companies circumvent US export restrictions.

Lawmakers are also examining claims that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department officials seeking information about the investigation.

Despite the scrutiny, analysts remain positive about Nvidia's business outlook.

The company reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion, up 103.2% year over year, and forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion.

Wedbush raised its price target to $293 from $275, while RBC and Morgan Stanley maintained positive ratings.

Nvidia's remaining $227.3 billion share buyback authorisation could also provide support for the stock.

headline: Soybean price analysis: Brent oil price bounces off crucial support
html_content:
Soybean price is trading within a rather tight range as investors weigh the energy market and the overall supply/demand dynamics. The bulls attempts of a breakout late last week were unsuccessful as the differing factors failed to attract enough buyers. In the short term, sideways trading may continue, with a breakout being dependent on crucial resistance levels. 

Soybean price trades sideways amid a volatile energy market

CBOT soybean price has been trading sideways in recent sessions after easing from the bullish WASDE report. USDA’s forecast for the 2026/27 season included increased exports and lower ending stocks. This is despite the predicted surge in US production by 12 million bushels. US soybean exports are expected to increase by 25 million bushels while the global ending stocks have been lessened by 0.8 million tons. 

According to the latest NASS crop progress report, soybean harvesting is 96% complete across the United States. This is slightly higher than the average pace of 95%. 

At the same time, the Export Inspections data indicate that soybean shipments for the week that ended on 12th November were 1.708 million metric tonnes (MMT). This was a decline of 10.8% from the previous week, but an increase of 41.7% from a similar period in 2025. Notably, China was the leading destination with a shipment of 691,670 MT. Increased US exports and brisk Chinese demand continue to support soybean prices. 

However, a stronger US dollar and weaker Brazilian Real are curbing the asset’s price gains. Earlier on Tuesday, the  Brazilian Real extended its losses to a fresh 19-month low before easing slightly. Over the past three weeks, the South American currency has plunged by close to 15%, enticing local producers to increase export volumes for more US dollars. At the same time, a stronger greenback renders the dollar-priced asset more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies. 

In the ensuing sessions, investors within the soybean market will also be eyeing crude oil prices. The crude oil market has been rather volatile in recent sessions amid conflicting drivers. On the one hand, the persistent conflicts in the Middle East are offering steady support to energy prices. However, investors are increasingly betting on a global supply glut. Crude oil prices largely impact the demand for biofuel. In addition to corn and sugarcane, soybean is a major source of biofuel.  

Soybean price technical analysis

CBOT soybean futures made subtle movements on Tuessday as the agricultural commodity continues to trade sideways. Late last week, the bulls attempted a breakout, surging to a one-and-a-half week high at $12.41 a bushel before easing back to its tight trading range. At the time of writing, soybean price was at $12.29, up by 0.04%.  

A look at its daily chart points to continued sideways trading in the short term, as investors eye the driving fundamentals and technical indicators. To begin with, CBOT soybean price remains below the short-term 25-day EMA and the medium-term 50-day EMA. Indeed, in late October, the two technical indicators formed a bearish death-cross pattern that is still in place. The bearish formation occurs when short-term MA crosses the medium/long-term MA to the downside as an indication of further losses. Besides, its RSI of 46 supports the thesis on curbed gains and range-bound trading. 

Even with these bearish technical indicators, soybean price continues to trade above the long-term 200-day EMA. This is an indication that the long-term support is still intact.  

In line with these technical indicators, and the fundamentals, the range between the support level of $12.14 and the resistance along the 25-day EMA at $12.35 is worth watching. Further gains will likely be curbed at $12.41. On the flip side, additional losses will invalidate this cautious thesis as the sellers eye the lower support level at $12.09.
